title.$t: 札幌住宿 | 札幌大通公園皇家花園康瓦斯飯店 The Royal Park Canvas - Sapporo Odori Park | 房內直視札幌電視塔 | 地點超方便的文青飯店

content.$t:
在挑選札幌住宿的時候，由於都是利用大眾交通工具，所以希望盡量以交通方便為主，因此選了這家在大通公園站旁的 The Royal Park Canvas 大通公園。

飯店的位置相當便利，不只在大通公園站旁，房間窗外就能看到市中心的大通公園。只要從地鐵大通公園站 24 號出口走出來，直接就是飯店的大門口了，拖著行李也不會覺得麻煩(但這個出口只有樓梯)，無論要前往札幌車站、狸小路商店街或薄野都很方便。

📜  資訊

  • 入住價格：$10,986 (兩晚，週六&週日)
  • 地址：1 Chome-12 Odorinishi, Chuo Ward, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0042日本
  • 電話：+81112081555
  • 官方網站：https://www.royalparkhotels.co.jp/canvas/sapporoodoripark/
  • 訂房網站：

📍 地點位置

地鐵大通公園站 24 號出口出來即可看到飯店門口

如果是利用大眾運輸，從地鐵大通公園站 24 號出口出來，直接就是飯店的大門口了，但是如果是自行駕車，飯店沒有自己專屬停車場，就需要自行在附近找尋停車場了。

🏢 飯店環境與設施

飯店的一樓是餐廳，二樓才是主要的大廳。Lobby 使用大量木質與植物元素，整體明亮、乾淨，帶一點北歐風的文青感，大片落地窗能直接看到大通公園與札幌電視塔，白天光線灑進來時非常舒服，是個一進門就會放鬆的空間。


飯店一樓的餐廳，也是早餐用餐的場所

接待櫃檯在二樓，可以搭乘電梯或是樓梯直接前往

大片落地窗能直接看到大通公園與札幌電視塔

二樓大廳整體風格以大量暖木色系、柔和燈光、綠意植物為主，室內擺滿各式觀葉植物，與落地窗外的大通公園綠意相互呼應，這些植物不只是裝飾，更是設計的一部分，營造出療癒與自然感。且不只是木質家具與建材，整體建築本身就用了大量北海道木材，其中超過 80% 來自北海道。

暖木色系、柔和燈光、綠意植物的風格


大廳的一旁還有一個木質的 DJ 台，這裡是假日夜晚 DJ Live 表演的地點，而後面整面的黑膠牆上的黑膠都可以借來回到房間來播放。


DJ 台與後方的黑膠牆

大廳的每個角落都十分明亮舒適

兩台自助 Check-in 的機器

除了人工櫃檯外，大廳裡還有兩台自助 Check-in 的機器，掃描護照、刷卡等操作都可以在這裡一站完成，且都提供多國語言，使用起來很順暢，如不會使用一旁也會有飯店員工來協助。


📔 藝廊與閱讀區


🌃 Rooftop

飯店的屋頂還有一個舒適的空間，這裡使用木質甲板鋪成一大片露天平台，四周有著植物點綴，整個氛圍像城市裡的秘密花園，且可以直視完整的札幌電視塔。

白天來這裡，可以坐在戶外的沙發上吹風、曬太陽，慢慢看著電視塔與大通公園，夜晚裝飾的等也會亮起，這裏也會有 Rooftop 的季節限定專屬餐飲烤肉菜單。


🍸 Canvas Lounge - KOKAGA


飯店二樓除了 Lobby 之外，另一個很吸引人的空間就是 Canvas Lounge – KOKAGE。這裡從早上 10:00 一路營業到 23:00，晚上搖身一變成為帶點派對感的輕鬆酒吧空間。

整個 Lounge 在晚上電視塔點燈後，整個氛圍變得浪漫而帶點神秘，且假日夜晚會有 DJ Live，不少外面的人也會特地來喝一杯、聽音樂，整體氛圍蠻不錯的，不會像去一家酒吧般過於正式，可以十分輕鬆舒適在這裡喝一杯。

Apple x Japanese Black Tea（900 円）

青森蘋果汁＋紅茶，有微微氣泡，整體偏向水果茶風味，幾乎沒有酒感，但新鮮順口，很適合當第一杯。

Lavender Gin & Tonic（1400 円）

用的是我一直很想買的 ohoro GIN 限定版薰衣草（Limited Edition LAVENDER），其實是不在酒單上的，但因為這趟北海道行沒有買到這隻琴酒，因此就直接向吧台詢問看看能不能使用這隻做個簡單的 Gin & Tonic。味道果然如記憶中的很不錯，薰衣草香氣細緻、搭上通寧水很乾淨清爽好喝。

🛏️ 房間環境

這次入住的是有電視塔景觀的木質套房，房間的採光蠻好的，即使不需開燈也夠明亮。房間整體走木質調設計，從家具到插座、音響都以木頭色系統一。比較特別的是，房內沒有電視，而是提供了黑膠唱片機與雜誌，符合飯店「放鬆、沉澱心靈」的理念。

通常放置電視的位置，由一些雜誌取代

木質外觀的音響，是用來搭配黑膠唱片機撥放，質感十足

窗邊還設計了一個臥榻，從這裡往外看就是大通公園與札幌電視塔，視野完全不被遮擋。白天坐在這裡曬著光、看看行人與公園景色；而到了夜晚，電視塔點燈後，從房間裡就能直接欣賞夜景，不用特地出門，非常舒服，也讓房間更有度假的味道。

窗邊的臥榻

直視札幌電視塔

整體風格一致，延長線都是木質色系


牆角特別介紹踢腳版的顏色？

雙人床實際上是兩張單人床併在一起，有各自的棉被，床鋪睡起來軟硬度適中，房內的安靜度也還蠻不錯的。

🛁 衛浴

廁所與衛浴空間大小適中，一樣走木質調的設計，整體舒適有質感，除了基本該有的免治馬桶外，衛浴空間是足夠放下一個單人浴缸的。






整體來說，這次入住 The Royal Park Canvas – Sapporo Odori Park 的感受相當不錯，飯店位置便利，走出來就是大通公園，無論散步、用餐或移動都相當方便。整體空間帶有一致的木質調與植栽風格，氣氛舒適而不做作，其中大廳酒吧的環境是我特別喜歡的一點，不論白天或夜晚，都能找到放鬆的節奏。

房間的部分，床的軟硬度適中，隔音也良好，休息得相當安穩。雖然沒有電視，但實際入住後並不覺得是缺點；反而因為有黑膠播放，讓整體氛圍更沉靜、也更有質感。坐在窗邊的臥榻欣賞公園與電視塔的景色，是這趟住宿裡最放鬆的時刻之一。

如果你在札幌旅行時想找一間設計感好、地點優秀，同時兼具安靜與品味的飯店，這裡會是一個值得考慮的選擇。

title.$t: Sapporo Hotel Review | The Royal Park Canvas - Sapporo Odori Park | Best TV Tower View & Unbeatable Location

content.$t:
When choosing accommodation in Sapporo, my priority was convenience since I rely entirely on public transportation. That is why I selected The Royal Park Canvas - Sapporo Odori Park, located right next to the station.

The location is incredibly convenient. Not only is it situated right beside Odori Park Station, but the room also offers a direct view of the park in the city center. Stepping out of Exit 24 of the subway station, you arrive directly at the hotel entrance. Dragging luggage isn't a hassle here (though do note this exit only has stairs). It is also perfectly positioned for visiting Sapporo Station, Tanukikoji Shopping Arcade, or Susukino.

📜 Information

  • Price: $10,986 TWD (2 nights, Sat & Sun)
  • Address: 1 Chome-12 Odorinishi, Chuo Ward, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0042 Japan
  • Phone: +81112081555
  • Official Website: https://www.royalparkhotels.co.jp/canvas/sapporoodoripark/
  • Booking Site:

📍 Location

You can see the hotel entrance immediately upon exiting Exit 24 of Odori Park Station.

If you are using public transport, the hotel is right outside Exit 24 of Odori Park Station. However, if you are driving, please be aware that the hotel does not have its own parking lot, so you will need to find paid parking nearby.

🏢 Hotel Environment & Facilities

The first floor houses the restaurant, while the main lobby is on the second floor. The lobby features abundant use of wood and plant elements, creating a bright, clean, and slightly Nordic atmosphere. The large floor-to-ceiling windows offer a direct view of Odori Park and the Sapporo TV Tower. It is incredibly comfortable when the sunlight streams in during the day—a space that helps you relax the moment you walk in.


The restaurant on the 1st floor, which also serves as the breakfast venue.

The reception desk is on the 2nd floor; you can take the elevator or stairs directly up.

Large floor-to-ceiling windows offer a direct view of Odori Park and Sapporo TV Tower.

The second-floor lobby is characterized by warm wood tones, soft lighting, and lush greenery. The space is filled with various foliage plants that echo the greenery of Odori Park outside. These plants aren't just decorations but part of the design, creating a healing, natural vibe. Beyond the furniture, the building itself utilizes a significant amount of Hokkaido timber—over 80% is locally sourced.

A style featuring warm wood tones, soft lighting, and greenery.


To one side of the lobby is a wooden DJ booth, the stage for live DJ performances on holiday nights. Behind it lies a wall of vinyl records, which guests can borrow to play in their rooms.


The DJ booth and the vinyl record wall behind it.

Every corner of the lobby is bright and comfortable.

Two self-check-in kiosks.

In addition to the staffed counter, there are two self-check-in kiosks in the lobby. Passport scanning and payment can all be done here in one go. The system supports multiple languages and is very smooth to use, though staff are always nearby to assist if needed.


📔 Gallery & Reading Area


🌃 Rooftop

The hotel rooftop features another cozy space: a large open-air deck surrounded by plants. The atmosphere feels like a secret garden within the city, offering an unobstructed view of the Sapporo TV Tower.

During the day, you can sit on the outdoor sofas to enjoy the breeze and sun while watching the TV Tower and Odori Park. At night, decorative lights turn on, and the rooftop offers a seasonal exclusive BBQ menu.


🍸 Canvas Lounge - KOKAGE


Besides the lobby, another attractive space on the 2nd floor is the Canvas Lounge – KOKAGE. It is open from 10:00 AM all the way to 11:00 PM, transforming into a relaxed, party-like bar space at night.

When the TV Tower lights up at night, the lounge takes on a romantic, slightly mysterious atmosphere. With live DJ sets on holiday nights, many non-guests visit specifically for a drink and music. The vibe is excellent—relaxed and comfortable, not overly formal like a typical bar, making it a great place to unwind.

Apple x Japanese Black Tea (900 JPY)

Aomori apple juice mixed with black tea. It has a slight fizz and tastes mostly like a fruit tea with almost no alcohol sensation. Fresh and smooth—perfect for a first drink.

Lavender Gin & Tonic (1400 JPY)

This used the ohoro GIN Limited Edition LAVENDER I had been wanting to buy. It wasn't actually on the menu, but since I couldn't find this bottle during my trip, I asked the bartender if they could make a simple Gin & Tonic with it. It lived up to expectations: the lavender aroma was delicate, and paired with tonic water, it was clean, refreshing, and delicious.

🛏️ Room Environment

I stayed in a wood-toned suite with a view of the TV Tower. The room has great natural light, bright enough even without turning on the lamps. The design is consistently woody, from the furniture to the outlets and speakers. Uniquely, there is no TV in the room; instead, a vinyl record player and magazines are provided, aligning with the hotel’s concept of "relaxing and settling the mind."

The spot usually reserved for a TV is replaced by a selection of magazines.

A wooden speaker designed to pair with the record player, full of texture.

There is also a window seat designed by the window. Looking out, you have a completely unobstructed view of Odori Park and the Sapporo TV Tower. During the day, you can sit here basking in the sun, watching pedestrians and the park scenery; at night, when the TV Tower lights up, you can enjoy the night view right from your room. It is incredibly comfortable and gives the room a true vacation feel.

The window seat.

Direct view of Sapporo TV Tower.

Consistent style throughout, even the extension cords are wood-colored.


A corner detail highlighting the baseboard color?

The double bed is actually two single beds pushed together, each with its own duvet. The mattress firmness is moderate, and the room is quite quiet.

🛁 Bathroom

The toilet and bathroom space is moderately sized, continuing the wood-tone design. It feels comfortable and high-quality. Aside from the standard bidet toilet, the bathroom is spacious enough to fit a single bathtub.






Overall, my stay at The Royal Park Canvas – Sapporo Odori Park was a delightful experience. The location is convenient—step out, and you are in Odori Park—making walking, dining, and traveling easy. The consistent wood and plant-filled style creates an atmosphere that is comfortable without being pretentious. I particularly loved the lobby lounge environment; day or night, it’s easy to find a relaxing rhythm there.

As for the room, the bed was comfortable, soundproofing was good, and I rested well. Although there was no TV, I didn't find it to be a drawback; the vinyl music actually made the atmosphere calmer and more stylish. Sitting on the window seat admiring the park and TV Tower was one of the most relaxing moments of the trip.

If you are traveling to Sapporo and looking for a hotel with great design, an excellent location, and a blend of quiet and taste, this is a choice worth considering.

title.$t: 星宇航空 STARLUX Airlines | A330-900neo 商務艙 | 北海道札幌到台北 | 商務艙餐點與酒類 | 新千歲機場貴賓室

content.$t:
這次的北海道之旅是搭乘星宇航空，在規劃行程時，就打算讓這趟旅程更輕鬆一點，因此特地考慮升級商務艙。主要原因是航程約 4 小時，屬於中距離航班，若能在起飛後好好放鬆、吃頓好餐、甚至稍微躺平休息一下，整體體驗會舒適許多。另外的原因也是在票價部分，飛北海道航線比經濟艙貴大約一萬元，以旅程的品質來說算是可以接受的升級，最後就忍痛奢侈一下，選擇了商務艙。

A330-900neo 商務艙

其實原本的計劃是去回兩段都搭商務艙，不過後來發現我們是從函館進、札幌出，而「台北－函館」這一段使用的是較小型的 AIRBUS A321neo。查了一下座艙配置後發現，這台機型的商務艙座位採 2-2 排列，座位雖然寬敞，但無法完全平躺，也沒有大型的娛樂螢幕或隱私隔板，整體感覺比較像是加大版的經濟艙，所以考量 CP 值後，最後決定只在「札幌－台北」這一段升級商務艙。

💎 新千歲機場貴賓室

北海道的新千歲機場真的非常大，也非常值得多留一些時間好好逛逛。尤其是國內線航廈，裡面不僅有各式各樣的伴手禮店與美食餐廳，還曾有一個深受遊客喜愛的「多啦A夢空中樂園」（目前已結束營業）。

從國際線航廈步行過來大約需要 10 分鐘，建議預留一些時間，順道走到國內線這邊逛逛。這裡不僅好買好吃，也能感受到滿滿的北海道特色，是在返台前延續旅程餘韻的好地方。


這次回程搭乘的是商務艙，在辦理登機時就能直接走優先通道，不需要和長長的人龍一起排隊，非常方便。新千歲機場的貴賓室「Royal Lounge」是多家航空公司共用的，因此在辦理完登機手續後，地勤人員會提供一張「貴賓室使用券 Premium Access」。拿著這張券前往登機門上方的貴賓室入口，就能直接入內使用。


新千歲機場的貴賓室「Royal Lounge」在登機門樓上

Royal Lounge 入口

新千歲機場的貴賓室 「Royal Lounge」 環境非常舒適，整體空間寬敞明亮，設計上也相當用心，裡面分成好幾個不同的區域，有像吧台一樣的高桌區、可以欣賞停機坪景色的觀景座位區，以及帶有一定隱私感的沙發座位區，無論是想工作、放空還是用餐都能找到合適的角落。

這次到訪時，使用的人並不多，整體氛圍非常安靜，不會有擁擠或吵雜的情況。可以在這裡輕鬆地坐下來，吃點小食、喝杯飲料，為旅程畫下一個從容又愜意的句點。



餐點的部分，貴賓室提供了許多北海道在地特色料理，像是湯咖哩、拉麵等熱食，也有各式日式小點心，如炸雞塊、可樂餅等。此外，酒水的選擇也不少，從啤酒到各類烈酒都能無限暢飲，對喜歡小酌的人來說相當享受。

不過以口味來說，我個人覺得並沒有特別驚艷，大多數有點普通，若是回程還要享用商務艙的機上餐點，建議可以斟酌取用，留一點胃口在飛機上慢慢品嚐會更剛好。


北海道湯咖喱自助區

湯品區

自助啤酒機與飲料機

各式酒類，紅酒、梅酒、清酒，還有烈酒

叉燒豚骨拉麵

✈️ 星宇航空商務艙 

這次搭乘的 A330-900neo 雖然不是星宇最新的機型，不過整體體驗依然相當不錯。商務艙共有 28 個座位，採 1-2-1 的交錯配置，每個座位都能直通走道。雖然沒有隱私門設計，但座椅可以完全放平，空間感舒適，整個機艙的氛圍也很安靜，帶有星宇一貫的設計感與細節。


座位旁邊設有一個小邊桌，除了方便放置飲品或手機外，還內建無線充電板，讓你不需要再翻找充電線就能輕鬆補電，傳統的 USB 與多國插座也一應俱全，無論是手機、筆電或平板都能同時充電。

邊桌下方還藏著一個小置物櫃，裡面整齊放著一副降噪耳機與一瓶 Evian 礦泉水，降噪耳機的品質不錯，能有效隔絕引擎聲與環境噪音，搭配機上音樂或電影，讓整趟旅程更安靜舒適。



一到座位後，馬上空服員就會附上熱毛巾與迎賓的果汁，並且確認一下在網路上預先選好的餐點菜單。


這趟旅程的菜色

餐點菜單與酒單


與 Bar TCRC/ Bar Home 主理人阿翔合作的四款限定調酒

羅蘭香檳/兩款清酒

各式紅白酒

也有各種烈酒、啤酒、調酒，或是無酒精的飲品

開胃小點 with 羅蘭香檳

羅蘭香檳酒莊是法國五大香檳酒莊之一，品質自然不用多說。這支香檳酒體呈淡淡的金色，氣泡細緻又輕盈，香氣優雅而層次豐富，帶有柑橘和白色水果的清新香氣。入口清爽、果味飽滿，整體非常平衡，尾韻也相當悠長。搭配細緻的魚料理或清爽的海鮮都很合適，是一款非常適合當開胃酒的香檳。

羅蘭香檳


前菜 with 氣泡清酒

前菜的南瓜濃湯超濃郁，意外地好喝，附餐有兩種麵包，口感各不相同，但香氣都很棒，可以搭配奶油或橄欖油一起吃。

在前菜的酒我選了「白鶴淡雪」氣泡清酒，被稱作「像香檳一樣華麗」的日本氣泡清酒，喝起來有米的柔和甜味和清爽的酸度，酒精度不高，很順口也很適合搭餐。

全麥麵包與核桃小圓麵包

主餐 - 慢燉牛頰 with 還沒喝完的氣泡清酒


主餐我選了慢燉牛頰，肉質相當嫩，搭配的醬汁也很不錯，味道蠻平衡的。只是牛味對我來說稍微重了一點，不過整體來說還是挺可以的一道菜。


甜點、水果和起司盤的部分都表現得不錯，份量也相當充足。整盤上來有一種豐盛又精緻的感覺。尤其是北海道抹茶冰淇淋，抹茶香氣濃郁卻不苦澀，口感滑順，帶點奶香的餘韻，讓整個甜點收尾得很完美。搭配一旁新鮮的水果與起司，味覺層次豐富，也不會太甜膩。

銀河碧螺春 - 琴酒、碧螺春茶、蘇打水

這次機上提供了四款調酒，前兩款在經濟艙也能喝到，所以我特地挑了後面兩款來試試看。第一杯點的是「銀河碧螺春」，以琴酒、碧螺春茶和蘇打水調製，原本以為會是一杯帶有淡淡茶香、清爽風格的 Gin Fizz。

結果實際喝起來不太行，不確定是比例問題還是哪個環節出了狀況，整杯幾乎只有酒精味，完全喝不出茶香。加上用茶包冷泡茶的方式，根本泡不出茶味，整體來說這杯算是失敗的。

橙香迷霧 - 玄米龍眼酒、果汁

第二杯我點了「橙香迷霧」，材料看起來很簡單，用的是台灣製的玄米龍眼酒，搭配應該是橘子類的果汁。原本因為第一杯有點讓我失望，所以沒抱太大期待，結果這杯意外地蠻不錯的！有著淡淡的米香和一點煙燻味，配上果汁的酸甜，整體酒感不會太重，喝起來順口又有特色。


整體來說這次體驗真的蠻不錯的，商務艙的空間寬敞又舒適，服務也很細心。除了有一杯調酒比較不合口味外，餐點都很好吃，酒單的選擇也蠻用心。再加上商務艙可以無限使用、速度又穩的 Wi-Fi，整趟旅程下來非常舒服。

title.$t: STARLUX Airlines | A330-900neo Business Class | Sapporo, Hokkaido to Taipei | Business Class Meals & Drinks | New Chitose Airport Lounge

content.$t:
For this Hokkaido trip we flew with STARLUX Airlines. When planning the itinerary, I wanted to make the journey a little more relaxing, so I specifically considered upgrading to business class. The main reason was that the flight is about 4 hours—a medium-haul route—so being able to fully relax after takeoff, enjoy a nice meal, and even lie down for a rest would make the overall experience much more comfortable. Another reason was the fare: on the Hokkaido route, business class is only about NT$10,000 more than economy, which felt like an acceptable upgrade for the quality of the trip. In the end I gritted my teeth and treated myself to business class.

A330-900neo Business Class

Originally the plan was to fly business class on both the outbound and return legs, but we later realized our route was into Hakodate and out of Sapporo, and the "Taipei–Hakodate" leg used the smaller AIRBUS A321neo. After checking the cabin configuration, I found that this aircraft's business class uses a 2-2 layout. Although the seats are spacious, they can't fully recline flat and there are no large entertainment screens or privacy partitions—overall it feels more like an enlarged economy seat. So after weighing the value for money, I decided to upgrade to business class only on the "Sapporo–Taipei" leg.

💎 New Chitose Airport Lounge

New Chitose Airport in Hokkaido is truly enormous, and it's well worth setting aside extra time to explore. The domestic terminal in particular is packed with all kinds of souvenir shops and restaurants, and it even used to have a "Doraemon Waku Waku Sky Park" that was beloved by visitors (now closed).

It's about a 10-minute walk from the international terminal, so I'd recommend allowing some extra time to stroll over to the domestic side. Not only is there plenty of great shopping and food, but you can also soak up all the Hokkaido character—a great place to savor the last of your trip before heading back to Taiwan.


On this return trip we flew business class, so at check-in we could go straight through the priority lane without queuing in the long lines—very convenient. The lounge at New Chitose Airport, "Royal Lounge," is shared by several airlines, so after completing check-in the ground staff hand you a "Premium Access" lounge pass. With this pass, you head to the lounge entrance above the boarding gates and go straight in.


The "Royal Lounge" at New Chitose Airport is upstairs from the boarding gates

Royal Lounge entrance

The "Royal Lounge" at New Chitose Airport is a very comfortable space—bright, spacious, and thoughtfully designed. It's divided into several different areas: a bar-style high-table area, a viewing seating area where you can watch the tarmac, and a sofa seating area with a fair degree of privacy. Whether you want to work, unwind, or dine, you'll find a suitable spot.

During my visit there weren't many people, so the atmosphere was very quiet with no crowding or noise. You can easily settle in, enjoy some small bites and a drink, and bring your trip to a leisurely, relaxed close.



As for food, the lounge offers plenty of local Hokkaido specialties, such as hot dishes like soup curry and ramen, along with various Japanese-style small bites like fried chicken and croquettes. There's also a good selection of drinks—from beer to a range of spirits, all free-flowing—which is quite a treat for anyone who enjoys a tipple.

However, in terms of taste, I personally didn't find it particularly impressive—most of it was fairly ordinary. If you're going to enjoy the business class in-flight meal on the way back, I'd suggest taking it easy here and saving some appetite to savor the meal on the plane instead.


Hokkaido soup curry self-service station

Soup station

Self-service beer taps and drink machines

A variety of alcohol—red wine, plum wine, sake, and spirits

Chashu tonkotsu ramen

✈️ STARLUX Airlines Business Class 

The A330-900neo we flew this time isn't STARLUX's newest aircraft, but the overall experience was still excellent. Business class has 28 seats in a staggered 1-2-1 layout, with every seat having direct aisle access. Although there are no privacy doors, the seats recline fully flat, the sense of space is comfortable, and the cabin is very quiet—carrying STARLUX's signature design sensibility and attention to detail.


There's a small side table next to the seat, which is handy for placing drinks or your phone, and it has a built-in wireless charging pad, so you can top up your battery without digging out a charging cable. Traditional USB ports and universal power outlets are also all provided, so you can charge your phone, laptop, or tablet at the same time.

Beneath the side table there's a hidden small storage compartment that neatly holds a pair of noise-canceling headphones and a bottle of Evian mineral water. The noise-canceling headphones are of good quality, effectively blocking out the engine sound and ambient noise—paired with the in-flight music or a movie, they make the whole journey quieter and more comfortable.



As soon as you sit down, the flight attendant brings a hot towel and a welcome juice, and confirms the meal you pre-selected online.


The dishes on this trip

Food menu and drinks list


Four exclusive cocktails created in collaboration with A-Xiang, the mixologist behind Bar TCRC / Bar Home

Laurent-Perrier Champagne / two kinds of sake

Various red and white wines

There are also various spirits, beers, and cocktails, as well as non-alcoholic drinks

Appetizer bites with Laurent-Perrier Champagne

Laurent-Perrier is one of France's five great champagne houses, so its quality goes without saying. This champagne has a pale golden body with fine, delicate bubbles, an elegant and layered aroma, and fresh notes of citrus and white fruit. It's crisp on the palate with full fruit flavor, very well balanced overall, and has a nicely lingering finish. It pairs well with delicate fish dishes or light seafood—an ideal champagne to serve as an aperitif.

Laurent-Perrier Champagne


Appetizer with sparkling sake

The pumpkin soup for the appetizer was incredibly rich and surprisingly delicious. It came with two kinds of bread with different textures, both with wonderful aromas that you can enjoy with butter or olive oil.

For the appetizer I chose the "Hakutsuru Awayuki" sparkling sake—a Japanese sparkling sake said to be "as gorgeous as champagne." It has the gentle sweetness of rice with a refreshing acidity, a low alcohol content, and goes down smoothly, pairing very well with the meal.

Whole-wheat bread and walnut rolls

Main course - slow-braised beef cheek, with the still-unfinished sparkling sake


For the main course I chose the slow-braised beef cheek. The meat was very tender and the accompanying sauce was quite good, with a nicely balanced flavor. The beefiness was just a touch strong for my taste, but overall it was still a pretty good dish.


The dessert, fruit, and cheese plate all performed well, with generous portions. The whole plate had a sense of both abundance and refinement. The Hokkaido matcha ice cream in particular had a rich matcha aroma without being bitter, a smooth texture, and a lingering milky finish, bringing the dessert course to a perfect close. Paired with the fresh fruit and cheese on the side, the flavors were rich and layered, and not overly sweet.

Galaxy Biluochun - gin, Biluochun tea, soda water

This time four cocktails were offered in-flight. The first two are also available in economy class, so I specifically picked the latter two to try. The first one I ordered was the "Galaxy Biluochun," made with gin, Biluochun tea, and soda water. I'd expected a Gin Fizz–style drink with a light, refreshing tea aroma.

But it didn't really work out. I'm not sure whether it was a proportion issue or something else went wrong, but the whole glass tasted almost entirely of alcohol with no discernible tea aroma at all. On top of that, cold-brewing tea with a tea bag simply couldn't draw out the tea flavor, so overall this one was a bit of a failure.

Orange Mist - brown-rice longan liqueur, juice

For the second one I ordered the "Orange Mist." The ingredients looked simple—Taiwan-made brown-rice longan liqueur paired with what was probably an orange-type juice. Since the first drink had disappointed me a little, I didn't have high hopes, but this one turned out to be surprisingly good! It had a faint rice aroma with a hint of smokiness, combined with the sweet-and-sour juice, so the alcohol wasn't too strong—smooth to drink and full of character.


Overall, this was a really enjoyable experience. The business class cabin was spacious and comfortable, and the service was very attentive. Apart from one cocktail that wasn't to my taste, the food was all delicious and the drinks list was thoughtfully curated. Add to that the unlimited, fast, and stable Wi-Fi available in business class, and the whole journey was extremely comfortable.

title.$t: 北海道景點 | 小樽 Otaru | 北海道的小港灣情懷 | 小樽蒸汽鐘 | 大正硝子館 | 小樽運河

content.$t:
小樽（Otaru），一座離札幌不遠的小港町，卻有著完全不同的氣氛，這裡保留了許多明治與大正時期的老建築，玻璃工藝、音樂盒、甜點與港灣風光，是構成小樽的四大印象。到了明治時代，日本政府積極推動北海道的開拓與現代化，小樽因為地處札幌與日本海之間的要地，逐漸發展為物資輸入、漁獲輸出與煤炭運輸的重要港口。

在計劃北海道之旅的時候，小樽就是一個想要排進來的景點之一，從札幌出發只需半小時，一天就能來回，因此規劃了大約半天到一天的時間來到小樽。

🚄 交通

前往小樽最方便的方式是搭乘 JR ，從札幌站上車，搭「快速エアポート（Airport 號）」約 30～40 分鐘 就能抵達，票價約 750 日圓，可直接使用 Kitaca、Suica 等交通 IC 卡很方便。

由於小樽著名的小樽堺町通り商店街不算短，一直從小樽站延伸到南小樽站，在搜尋了一下網路上建議的走法是：

在「南小樽站」下車 → 沿著堺町通一路散步逛到「小樽站」回程

不但整段路線大多是緩下坡，不費力又能一路串起主要景點，非常順，回程的時候從小樽站上車也才比較會有座位可以坐。

⛩️ 住吉神社

  • 地址：2 Chome-5-1 Suminoe, Otaru, Hokkaido 047-0014日本
  • 開放時間：06:00 ~ 16:30
  • 官方網站：http://www.otarusumiyoshijinja.or.jp/

抵達南小樽站後，先往山坡方向走一小段，會抵達住吉神社。這裡相對來說觀光客不多且寧靜。長長的石階、綠樹夾道的參道、木質的鳥居與神社主殿，都透著一股淡淡的時間味。


從神社內還可以直接眺望海洋，景色蠻優美的

在住吉神社，最有趣的是「水籤」體驗，可以到社務所來購買水籤，門口就有可以用來浸泡的水，把籤紙放進清水裡，白色的紙上會慢慢浮出文字。



如果旅途需要一點儀式感，不妨在這裡抽一張籤，算是與小樽的第一次對話
直視海洋的住吉神社

⏰ 小樽蒸汽鐘與小樽音樂盒堂本館

小樽蒸氣鐘

順著路往堺町通走，會在小樽音樂盒堂本館前遇見那座著名的蒸汽鐘，遠遠就可以看到聚集著不少人，為了要拍照或是錄影，捕捉蒸汽鐘鳴響的那瞬間。

遠遠就會看到小樽音樂盒堂本館前，聚集了人潮等待蒸汽鐘鳴響的瞬間

它是由加拿大技師設計，與溫哥華 Gastown 的那座蒸汽鐘是「姊妹鐘」，每隔十五分鐘會鳴響一次，同時冒出蒸氣與音樂，讓整條街都瀰漫著懷舊的氣息。

小樽音樂盒堂本館裡面收藏著上千種音樂盒：玻璃的、木製的、旋轉木馬造型的，還有能隨音樂閃爍的小夜燈，每走一步，耳邊就有不同旋律響起。

這裡除了各種特殊新奇的音樂盒之外，也有傳統很日式風格的音樂盒，如果有興趣不妨在這裡挑個紀念品吧！

壽司音樂盒

🍰 LeTAO 總店


在小樽蒸汽鐘對面的廣場後方，有棟歐風建築，是北海道必買伴手禮之一的「小樽洋菓子舖 LeTAO」總店的位置。

LeTAO 的這棟樓，除了一樓是販賣部之外，還有著可以在這裡品嚐蛋糕與茶點的「LeTAO Cafe」，三樓更是一個免費的展望室，可以從上往下看看這個街區。


一樓販賣部

這裡有著所有的 LaTAO 商品，許多品相是到機場免稅也找不到的(不過熱門款機場都有)，其中很推紅茶巧克力夾心餅乾，茶香很濃又很好吃，也是 LeTAO 的伴手禮明星。



LeTAO Cafe

由於觀光人潮眾多，要到二樓享用甜點的話，記得直接到櫃檯的候位機器抽取號碼牌，再等待叫號後，就會有服務人員引導入座囉。


線上菜單：https://tabelog.com/tw/hokkaido/A0106/A010601/1000304/dtlmenu/

這次選擇了一個套餐的組合，可以任選三款蛋糕，搭配兩款茶飲。除了蛋糕十分好吃之外，這次兩杯茶飲就選擇了兩種不一樣的紅茶，表現也蠻出色的。


三樓展望室


由於三樓的高度並不是很高，因此展望室主要能看到的景色，就是前方的十字交叉路口，在這裡可以直接看到對面的蒸汽鐘。


🍭 北菓樓與六花亭

從 LeTAO 沿著堺町通商店街再往下走，會來到另一個北海道的甜點品牌，以米果、泡芙與年輪蛋糕為招牌的北菓樓，小樽總店是由舊倉庫改建，充滿歷史風味。




而知名的六花亭就在旁邊，創立於 1933 年的北海道代表洋菓子品牌，以「蘭姆葡萄奶油夾心餅乾」最為人熟知；它的分店多數只在北海道，保留在地限定風格，裡面有許多六花亭的伴手禮可以購買。

🛍️ 堺町通商店街

堺町通商店街是小樽最具代表性的老街之一，長約 1.3 公里，連接 JR 南小樽站與 JR 小樽站中段。 這條街上聚集了超過 120 間以上 各式老鋪與特色店家，包括玻璃工藝、音樂盒、甜點、海鮮與伴手禮店，是遊客在小樽最常走、最不想錯過的一段街道。

走在堺町通上，就像穿梭在明治、大正、昭和的交接時代：那邊一棟磚造或石造的舊倉庫被改成玻璃工藝店，那邊一間木造老屋變身甜點店，店鋪招牌、街燈、鋪面素材都保留不少古樸韻味。





🏞️ 小樽運河

說到對於小樽的印象，小樽運河絕對是最具代表性與象徵性的景點之一，它於 1923 年竣工，原本目的是為了提升貨物轉運與倉儲效率，使港口與填海地區之間有更順暢的水路連繫。

隨著時代演變，運河的實際物流功能逐漸式微，部分河道曾被填埋改為道路，不過因為當地保存意識高漲，最後僅保留了部分河段，並將沿岸石造倉庫改建為商店、餐廳、博物館等觀光用途。


最後走到小樽站，搭車回札幌

走完一整天的小樽，從住吉神社一路逛到運河邊，幾乎串起了這座城市最有代表性的樣貌。老街的節奏很慢，玻璃店、甜點店、音樂盒的聲音交錯著，有一種舊時代的安靜感。

如果安排來到北海道旅遊，可以留個半天到一天，來到小樽走一走，體驗與札幌一般的大城市完全不一樣的風情。

title.$t: Hokkaido Attractions | Otaru | The Charm of Hokkaido's Little Harbor | Otaru Steam Clock | Taisho Glass Hall | Otaru Canal

content.$t:
Otaru, a small harbor town not far from Sapporo, has a completely different atmosphere. It preserves many old buildings from the Meiji and Taisho eras, and glasswork, music boxes, sweets, and harbor scenery make up the four main impressions of Otaru. During the Meiji era, the Japanese government actively promoted the development and modernization of Hokkaido. Because of its strategic location between Sapporo and the Sea of Japan, Otaru gradually developed into an important port for importing goods, exporting seafood, and transporting coal.

When planning a trip to Hokkaido, Otaru was one of the spots I definitely wanted to fit in. It's only half an hour from Sapporo and can be done as a day trip, so I set aside about half a day to a full day for Otaru.

🚄 Getting There

The most convenient way to get to Otaru is by JR. Board at Sapporo Station and take the "Rapid Airport" train, which takes about 30–40 minutes to arrive. The fare is about 750 yen, and you can conveniently use IC cards like Kitaca or Suica directly.

Since Otaru's famous Sakaimachi shopping street is quite long, running all the way from Otaru Station to Minami-Otaru Station, after searching online, the recommended route is:

Get off at "Minami-Otaru Station" → Stroll along Sakaimachi Street all the way to "Otaru Station" for the return

Not only is most of the route a gentle downhill slope, effortless and neatly linking up the main sights, but on the way back, boarding at Otaru Station also makes it more likely to get a seat.

⛩️ Sumiyoshi Shrine

  • Address: 2 Chome-5-1 Suminoe, Otaru, Hokkaido 047-0014, Japan
  • Opening hours: 06:00 ~ 16:30
  • Official website: http://www.otarusumiyoshijinja.or.jp/

After arriving at Minami-Otaru Station, walk a short way uphill and you'll reach Sumiyoshi Shrine. It's relatively quiet with few tourists. The long stone steps, the tree-lined approach, the wooden torii gate, and the main shrine hall all carry a faint sense of the passage of time.


From within the shrine you can look out directly over the ocean—the scenery is quite beautiful

At Sumiyoshi Shrine, the most interesting thing is the "water fortune (mizu-mikuji)" experience. You can buy a water fortune slip at the shrine office; there's water at the entrance for soaking it. Place the fortune paper into the clear water, and characters will slowly appear on the white paper.



If your journey could use a little ritual, why not draw a fortune here—consider it your first conversation with Otaru
Sumiyoshi Shrine looking straight out to the sea

⏰ Otaru Steam Clock and Otaru Music Box Museum Main Hall

Otaru Steam Clock

Following the road along Sakaimachi Street, you'll come across the famous steam clock in front of the Otaru Music Box Museum Main Hall. From afar you can see quite a crowd gathered, trying to take photos or videos to capture the moment the steam clock chimes.

From a distance you'll see the crowd gathered in front of the Otaru Music Box Museum Main Hall, waiting for the moment the steam clock chimes

It was designed by a Canadian engineer and is a "sister clock" to the steam clock in Gastown, Vancouver. Every fifteen minutes it chimes, releasing steam and music at the same time, filling the whole street with a nostalgic atmosphere.

The Otaru Music Box Museum Main Hall houses thousands of kinds of music boxes: glass ones, wooden ones, carousel-shaped ones, and even little night lights that twinkle to the music. With every step, a different melody rings in your ears.

Besides all sorts of novel and unusual music boxes, there are also traditional, very Japanese-style ones. If you're interested, why not pick out a souvenir here!

Sushi music box

🍰 LeTAO Main Store


Behind the plaza across from the Otaru Steam Clock stands a European-style building—the main store of "Otaru Confectionery LeTAO," one of Hokkaido's must-buy souvenir brands.

Besides the ground-floor retail section, this LeTAO building also has "LeTAO Cafe," where you can enjoy cake and tea, and the third floor is a free observation room where you can look down over this district.


Ground-Floor Retail Section

Here you'll find all the LeTAO products, many of which can't even be found at airport duty-free shops (though the most popular items are available at the airport). I especially recommend the black tea chocolate sandwich cookies—very aromatic and delicious, and one of LeTAO's star souvenirs.



LeTAO Cafe

Because of the large tourist crowds, if you want to enjoy dessert on the second floor, remember to take a number from the queuing machine at the counter, and once your number is called, a staff member will guide you to your seat.


Online menu: https://tabelog.com/tw/hokkaido/A0106/A010601/1000304/dtlmenu/

This time I chose a set combination where you can pick any three cakes paired with two tea drinks. Besides the cakes being very tasty, this time I chose two different black teas for the drinks, and they were quite impressive too.


Third-Floor Observation Room


Since the third floor isn't very high, the main view from the observation room is the crossroads intersection in front, where you can look straight across at the steam clock opposite.


🍭 Kitakaro and Rokkatei

Continuing down Sakaimachi shopping street from LeTAO, you'll come to another Hokkaido sweets brand—Kitakaro, known for its rice crackers, cream puffs, and baumkuchen. The Otaru main store is converted from an old warehouse, full of historical flavor.




And the well-known Rokkatei is right next door. Founded in 1933, it's a representative Hokkaido Western-confectionery brand best known for its "rum raisin butter sandwich cookies." Most of its branches are only in Hokkaido, preserving a locally exclusive style, and inside there are many Rokkatei souvenirs to buy.

🛍️ Sakaimachi Shopping Street

Sakaimachi Shopping Street is one of Otaru's most iconic old streets. About 1.3 km long, it connects the middle section between JR Minami-Otaru Station and JR Otaru Station. This street is home to more than 120 various old shops and specialty stores, including glasswork, music boxes, sweets, seafood, and souvenir shops. It's the street tourists in Otaru walk most and least want to miss.

Walking along Sakaimachi Street feels like traveling through the transition between the Meiji, Taisho, and Showa eras: over there an old brick or stone warehouse has been turned into a glasswork shop, over there a wooden old house has become a dessert shop. The shop signs, street lamps, and paving materials all retain much of their quaint charm.





🏞️ Otaru Canal

When it comes to impressions of Otaru, the Otaru Canal is absolutely one of the most representative and symbolic sights. Completed in 1923, its original purpose was to improve cargo transshipment and warehousing efficiency, providing a smoother water route between the port and the reclaimed land.

As times changed, the canal's practical logistics function gradually declined, and parts of the waterway were once filled in and turned into roads. However, thanks to a strong local preservation movement, in the end only part of the canal was retained, and the stone warehouses along the banks were converted into shops, restaurants, museums, and other tourist uses.


Finally walking to Otaru Station to take the train back to Sapporo

After a full day in Otaru, walking all the way from Sumiyoshi Shrine to the canalside, I had strung together almost all of this city's most iconic sights. The old town's rhythm is very slow, with the sounds of glass shops, dessert shops, and music boxes intertwining—there's a kind of quiet from a bygone era.

If you're planning a trip to Hokkaido, you can set aside half a day to a full day to stroll around Otaru and experience a charm completely different from big cities like Sapporo.

title.$t: 北海道景點 | 洞爺湖 Lake Toya | 北海道三景之一 | 洞爺湖函館札幌交通 | 洞爺湖住宿 | 洞爺湖觀光船

content.$t:
洞爺湖，在北海道的無數美景之中，以「北海道三景」之一的地位聞名，一直是大家來到北海道，不會錯過的經典景點。

這座由火山爆發形成的圓形火山口湖，湖面如鏡般映照著四季變換的色彩，湖中心的中島群島就像漂浮在湖上的綠色小寶石，這裡是保護完好的自然生態區，棲息著野鹿與多樣植物，沒有過度開發，只有搭乘觀光船才能登島一探秘境。

其中，從洞爺湖可以遠眺被譽為「蝦夷富士」羊蹄山，即使在寒冬，湖水依舊不結冰，夏季還有長達數月的煙火秀點綴夜空，是一個四季都適合來的旅遊景點。

🚄 交通

這次北海道行程，我們是從函館進、札幌出，因此是從函館來到洞爺湖。不過，不論是從函館還是札幌，除了自駕之外，最方便的還是直接搭乘 JR 到洞爺站，再轉公車 or 飯店接駁。

JR 北斗號

從函館搭乘 JR 北斗號（特急北斗） 前往洞爺湖， 無需轉車，最快約僅需兩小時內即可從函館站抵達洞爺站。

  • 函館 -> 洞爺，單程價格：¥6,250
  • 洞爺 -> 札幌，單程價格：¥6,690

購票的方式也很簡單，直接去售票機 or 櫃檯說要購買到洞爺站的車票即可，現在售票機都有中文模式，也不會怕看不懂不知道怎麼操作。

JR 洞爺站


到了洞爺站後，出來右手邊遠遠的就可以看到公車站了。由於公車班次並沒有很多，但 JR 車次相對比較多，所以建議可以先看一下公車時刻表，再決定要搭哪一班 JR 來搭配，才不會在車站等太久喔。


一小時只有約兩班的公車

道南巴士就是一般的公車，並沒有任何放行李的空間，但因為要前往洞爺湖的旅客大部分都會攜帶大型行李，整個車內空間會非常擁擠... 所以能越早上車越好。


🏞️ 洞爺湖 Lake Toya


來到洞爺湖，通常都會選擇在洞爺湖温泉這裡選擇一間溫泉旅館，享受這裏的美景、住上一晚。除了遠眺羊蹄山美景，還可以搭船抵達湖中央的小島群「中島」，可以登上島嶼探訪原始森林，走在步道上，會覺得彷彿穿越時光，回到純粹的大自然懷抱。

沿著湖畔，「洞爺湖周遊雕刻公園」位於洞爺湖的湖畔步道旁，沿線設置了 58 件結合自然景觀與藝術的雕塑作品，散步其中能一邊欣賞湖光山色，一邊感受藝術氛圍，是洞爺湖相當經典的散策路線。



🏞️ 洞爺湖觀光船與中島

湖中央則有幾座因火山活動而誕生、被鬱鬱森林覆蓋的小島，合稱「中島」。這裡人煙稀少，保留著北海道少見的原始森林生態，夏季還能見到蝦夷鹿等野生動物在林間悠閒覓食。

想要前往中島必須搭乘洞爺湖觀光船，航程約 15 分鐘，船班約每 30 分鐘一班，但要特別注意最後一班船通常在下午四點左右，若錯過就只能等隔天了。



洞爺湖觀光船的船艙空間相當寬敞，共有三層樓。雖然內部裝潢略帶復古風格，但乾淨舒適，還設有小小販賣部，販售飲料與零食。遊客常會買一包類似「蝦味先」的餅乾到甲板上餵食成群跟隨船隻的海鷗，看著牠們在湖面上穿梭、搶食點心，也是搭船的一大樂趣。


聰明的海鷗都會跟著船一起航行


中島上的湖之森博物館

想在島上探索步道，需先至「湖之森博物館」櫃檯免費登記，領取號碼牌後便可進入步道健行，結束行程時再將號碼牌歸還即可。



穿過「湖之森博物館」後，首先映入眼簾的是一片筆直纖細的林木，整個空間靜謐得幾乎聽不見人聲，空氣中充滿清新的森林氣息。這裡很適合慢慢散步、放鬆心情。島上的步道相當平緩好走，不用擔心會迷路，分為多條不同長度的步道，可以根據自己體力與需求來選擇。

title.$t: Hokkaido Attractions | Lake Toya | One of the Three Great Views of Hokkaido | Transport from Hakodate & Sapporo | Lake Toya Accommodation | Lake Toya Sightseeing Cruise

content.$t:
Among the countless beautiful landscapes of Hokkaido, Lake Toya is famous for being one of the "Three Great Views of Hokkaido," and has long been a classic spot that no one wants to miss when visiting Hokkaido.

This circular caldera lake, formed by a volcanic eruption, mirrors the changing colors of the four seasons on its surface, while the Nakajima islands at its center look like little green gems floating on the water. It is a well-preserved natural ecological area, home to wild deer and diverse plant life. With no over-development, the only way to land on the islands and explore this hidden gem is by taking a sightseeing cruise.

From Lake Toya you can also gaze out at Mount Yotei, dubbed the "Ezo Fuji." Even in the depths of winter the lake never freezes, and in summer months-long firework shows light up the night sky, making it a destination worth visiting in any season.

🚄 Transportation

For this Hokkaido trip, we entered via Hakodate and departed from Sapporo, so we came to Lake Toya from Hakodate. However, whether coming from Hakodate or Sapporo, aside from driving, the most convenient option is to take the JR directly to Toya Station, then transfer to a bus or hotel shuttle.

JR Hokuto

Taking the JR Hokuto (Limited Express Hokuto) from Hakodate to Lake Toya requires no transfers, and at its fastest it takes just under two hours to reach Toya Station from Hakodate Station.

  • Hakodate -> Toya, one-way fare: ¥6,250
  • Toya -> Sapporo, one-way fare: ¥6,690

Buying tickets is also very simple—just go to the ticket machine or counter and say you want a ticket to Toya Station. Ticket machines now all have a Chinese-language mode, so there's no need to worry about not understanding how to operate them.

JR Toya Station


After arriving at Toya Station, once you exit, you can spot the bus stop in the distance on your right-hand side. Since there aren't many bus departures but JR trains are relatively more frequent, it's advisable to check the bus timetable first and then decide which JR train to pair it with, so you won't have to wait too long at the station.


Only about two buses per hour

The Donan Bus is just an ordinary bus with no space for luggage, but since most travelers heading to Lake Toya carry large suitcases, the entire cabin gets extremely crowded... so the earlier you board, the better.


🏞️ Lake Toya


When visiting Lake Toya, most people choose a hot spring inn in the Lake Toya Onsen area to enjoy the beautiful scenery and stay overnight. Besides gazing out at the beautiful view of Mount Yotei, you can also take a boat to the cluster of small islands in the middle of the lake, "Nakajima." You can land on the islands to explore the primeval forest, and walking along the trails feels like traveling back in time to the embrace of pure nature.

Along the lakeshore, the "Lake Toya Sculpture Park" is located beside the lakeside walking path, with 58 sculptures combining natural scenery and art set up along the route. Strolling through it, you can admire the lake and mountain views while soaking in the artistic atmosphere—a truly classic walking route around Lake Toya.



🏞️ Lake Toya Sightseeing Cruise and Nakajima

In the center of the lake are several small islands born from volcanic activity and covered in lush forest, collectively known as "Nakajima." Sparsely inhabited, they preserve a primeval forest ecosystem rarely seen in Hokkaido, and in summer you can even spot wild animals such as Ezo deer leisurely foraging among the trees.

To reach Nakajima you must take the Lake Toya sightseeing cruise. The voyage takes about 15 minutes, with boats departing roughly every 30 minutes, but note that the last boat usually leaves around 4 p.m.—miss it and you'll have to wait until the next day.



The cabin of the Lake Toya sightseeing cruise is quite spacious, spanning three floors. Although the interior décor has a slightly retro style, it is clean and comfortable, and there's even a small kiosk selling drinks and snacks. Tourists often buy a bag of crackers similar to "Shrimp Crackers" and head to the deck to feed the flocks of seagulls that follow the boat. Watching them dart across the lake surface and snatch up the snacks is one of the great joys of the cruise.


The clever seagulls all sail along with the boat


The Forest Museum of Lake on Nakajima

To explore the trails on the island, you first need to register for free at the "Forest Museum of Lake" counter. After receiving a numbered tag, you may enter and hike the trails, then simply return the tag when you finish.



After passing through the "Forest Museum of Lake," the first thing that comes into view is a stretch of straight, slender trees. The whole space is so quiet you can barely hear a human voice, and the air is filled with the fresh scent of the forest. It's a great place to stroll slowly and relax. The island's trails are quite gentle and easy to walk, so there's no need to worry about getting lost. They are divided into several routes of different lengths, so you can choose according to your stamina and needs.


The Lake Toya sightseeing cruise getting ready for the return trip

title.$t: 札幌咖啡 | Mermaid Coffee Roasters - Sapporo | 狸小路商店街內咖啡廳 | 自家烘焙精品咖啡

content.$t:
在日本，常常喝到的是傳統的日式咖啡，多半偏中焙甚至深焙，口感厚重、餘韻長，這次來到北海道，想找一家有著淺焙手沖的咖啡廳來體驗一下，也想順便買一些豆子回台灣，來到了朋友推薦的這家，位在貍小路商店街裡的 Mermaid Coffee Roasters。

📜  資訊

  • 地址：1 Chome-12-12 Minami 3 Jonishi, Chuo Ward, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0063
  • 營業時間：08:00 - 18:00
  • 電話：+81112072244
  • 官方網站：https://mermaid-coffee-roasters.com/

📍 地點與店內環境

位於狸小路商店街入口附近的 Mermaid Coffee Roasters，外觀低調得幾乎與街道融為一體，如果不是遠遠就看見門口排隊的人潮，很容易就錯過了這家店。這間店是2023年才在札幌狸小路一丁目開幕的新店，由東京池袋本店擴展而來，目前已成為札幌人氣手沖咖啡館之一。

這天我們抵達時還不到早上十點，店內早已座無虛席，外頭也聚集了不少等著入內的客人。這裡除了供應手沖與義式咖啡，還販售司康與厚片吐司，許多顧客也都會來這裡點享用一份司康或吐司，再搭配一杯現沖咖啡，作為今日的早餐組合。


店內共有兩層樓，一樓是開放式的座位區，點餐後可以自己找位子入座；二樓則是需要脫鞋的日式榻榻米空間，氣氛更加安靜，適合想久坐聊天或慢慢品味咖啡的客人。


整間店的裝潢以木質與暖色系為主，溫馨舒適的空間，配上許多的乾燥花束，讓人感覺非常放鬆，隨處可見的小巧美人魚圖案，或是可愛的小裝飾，也增添了一點趣味。


☕️ 咖啡

這裡最特別的是有一個 Tasting Area，提供多達 12 種手沖咖啡試飲，你可以先試喝不同豆子的風味，再決定喜歡的口感後到櫃台點餐，對於愛喝咖啡卻想嘗試不同風味的人來說，非常貼心。

除了咖啡，店內還販售司康、厚片吐司與手工餅乾

我們當天點了一杯手沖與一杯拿鐵，拿鐵也能選擇兩種不同的咖啡基底，並事先試飲，這樣點到的每一杯都能確保是自己喜歡的味道。




挑了兩款豆子帶回來喝


整體來說，Mermaid Coffee Roasters 不僅是一家提供優質咖啡的店，更是一個能讓人放慢腳步、感受札幌溫度的小角落。印象最深刻的是，每一組客人離店時，店員都會親自送到門口，以微笑和親切的語氣道別，體驗相當好。

如果你也計畫來到札幌，想找一間咖啡廳喝咖啡，很推薦到這裡坐坐，喝杯挑選過的好咖啡。不過建議可以早一點到，特別是週末早晨，才能享受最安靜舒適的空間。

title.$t: Sapporo Coffee | Mermaid Coffee Roasters - Sapporo | A Café Inside Tanukikoji Shopping Street | Self-Roasted Specialty Coffee

content.$t:
In Japan, what you most often drink is traditional Japanese-style coffee, usually medium or even dark roast, with a heavy body and a long finish. On this trip to Hokkaido, I wanted to find a café offering light-roast pour-over coffee to try out, and also to pick up some beans to bring back to Taiwan. So I came to this place a friend recommended, located in the Tanukikoji shopping street: Mermaid Coffee Roasters.

📜  Information

  • Address: 1 Chome-12-12 Minami 3 Jonishi, Chuo Ward, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0063
  • Opening Hours: 08:00 - 18:00
  • Phone: +81112072244
  • Official Website: https://mermaid-coffee-roasters.com/

📍 Location & Interior

Located near the entrance of the Tanukikoji shopping street, Mermaid Coffee Roasters has such an understated exterior that it almost blends into the street. If it weren't for the crowd lining up at the door visible from afar, it would be easy to walk right past. This shop is a new store that only opened in Sapporo's Tanukikoji 1-chome in 2023, an expansion from the main store in Ikebukuro, Tokyo, and it has already become one of Sapporo's most popular pour-over coffee shops.

When we arrived that day it wasn't even ten in the morning, yet the shop was already full, with quite a few customers gathered outside waiting to get in. Besides serving pour-over and espresso-based coffee, they also sell scones and thick-cut toast. Many customers come here to order a scone or toast paired with a freshly brewed cup of coffee as their breakfast set for the day.


The shop has two floors. The first floor is an open seating area where you can find your own seat after ordering; the second floor is a Japanese tatami space where you need to take off your shoes. The atmosphere there is quieter, ideal for customers who want to sit for a while chatting or slowly savoring their coffee.


The whole shop is decorated mainly in wood and warm tones, a cozy and comfortable space paired with plenty of dried flower bouquets that makes you feel very relaxed. The small mermaid motifs seen here and there, along with cute little decorations, add a bit of playful charm.


☕️ Coffee

The most special thing here is that there's a Tasting Area offering as many as 12 kinds of pour-over coffee to sample. You can first taste the flavors of the different beans, then decide on the taste you like before ordering at the counter. For those who love coffee but want to try different flavors, it's a very thoughtful touch.

Besides coffee, the shop also sells scones, thick-cut toast, and handmade cookies

That day we ordered a pour-over and a latte. The latte also lets you choose between two different coffee bases and sample them beforehand, so every cup you order is sure to be a taste you enjoy.




I picked two kinds of beans to take home and enjoy


Overall, Mermaid Coffee Roasters is not just a shop that serves quality coffee—it's also a little corner that lets you slow down and feel the warmth of Sapporo. What left the deepest impression on me was that whenever a group of customers left, the staff would personally see them to the door, bidding farewell with a smile and warm words. The experience was really wonderful.

If you're also planning a trip to Sapporo and looking for a café to enjoy some coffee, I highly recommend coming here to sit for a while and drink a well-chosen cup of good coffee. That said, I'd suggest arriving a bit early, especially on weekend mornings, so you can enjoy the quietest, most comfortable space.

content.$t:
提到日本自由行，北海道一直是一個特別的存在：它不像東京那樣熱鬧繁華，也不像關西那樣歷史悠久，卻有一種讓人放鬆的節奏，適合慢慢體會，但機票始終都很貴。

這次選擇在五月出發，一來是為了避開人潮，二來是因為這個時候的北海道還沒進入旅遊旺季，機票、住宿都相對便宜不少 (洞爺湖溫泉旅館還是不便宜...)，加上氣候舒適宜人，不冷也不熱，安排了一趟以函館、洞爺湖、小樽、札幌為主的自由行，希望用比較緩慢的步調，好好感受北海道初夏的風景與味道。

content.$t:
When it comes to independent travel in Japan, Hokkaido has always held a special place: it isn't as lively and bustling as Tokyo, nor as steeped in history as Kansai, yet it has a relaxing rhythm that's perfect for savoring slowly—though the flights are always expensive.

This time we chose to set off in May, partly to avoid the crowds, and partly because Hokkaido hasn't yet entered its peak tourist season at this time, so flights and accommodation are relatively much cheaper (though the Lake Toya hot spring inn still wasn't cheap...). With the comfortable, pleasant climate—neither cold nor hot—we arranged an independent trip centered on Hakodate, Lake Toya, Otaru, and Sapporo, hoping to take in the scenery and flavors of Hokkaido's early summer at a more leisurely pace.

🗾 Itinerary

This time we entered Hokkaido from Hakodate, traveled all the way to Lake Toya, then on to Sapporo, with a day trip to Otaru in between, and finally departed from Sapporo's New Chitose Airport to return to Taiwan. In total it was eight days and seven nights, without backtracking, to cut down on travel time.

title.$t: 洞爺湖住宿 | TOYA乃之風湖景度假村 The Lake view TOYA Nonokaze resort | 絕美湖景房型 | 房間內可以直接看洞爺湖煙火 | 湖景第一排

content.$t:
房內直接可以看到羊蹄山

這次的北海道行程，我們特別安排了一天入住洞爺湖。跟河口湖一樣，湖景第一排大多是價位不便宜的溫泉飯店，想要一邊泡湯、一邊欣賞湖景，通常都得多花點預算。剛好這次又遇上洞爺湖的花火大會，考量到如果能直接在房間看煙火，既方便又浪漫，我們也花了一些時間比較了幾間湖景第一排的飯店。

最後選擇了評價一直都很不錯的「TOYA乃之風湖景度假村」，不管是房型、餐點還是服務，幾乎是洞爺湖一帶最多人推薦、也是公認數一數二的選擇。想想下次再來洞爺湖，也不知道會是什麼時候，雖然房價真的不便宜，但最後還是決定給自己一次完整的湖景體驗。

📜  資訊

  • 入住價格：$10,942 (一泊二食 + 洞爺湖船票)
  • 地址：29-1 Toyakoonsen, Toyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido 049-5721日本
  • 電話：+81570026571
  • 官方網站：https://nonokaze-resort.com/

比較了一下訂房網站和官方網站的價格，發現直接在官方網站訂房通常會比較便宜，而且還能搭配像是洞爺湖遊船票或 SPA 票券的優惠組合，整體下來更划算。如果你也打算入住，推薦先從官方網站看看，有時候還會有一些限定優惠喔。

📍 地點位置

TOYA乃之風湖景度假村就坐落在洞爺湖溫泉街的中心，靠近櫻町和中央通公車站。飯店裡不管是大廳、餐廳還是溫泉，甚至每間房間，都能直接看到美麗的洞爺湖和羊蹄山，景色相當棒，地點也很方便。

交通

距 JR 洞爺車站約15分鐘車程，可以使用公車或是自行開車來抵達。

接駁車

飯店提供與札幌、新千歲機場的接駁車，必須要事先預約才能夠使用。

  • 札幌JR車站來回飯店：免費
  • 新千歲機場來回飯店：1500日圓/人，官網訂房的話可以再折500日圓
不過一天只有一班固定時間的接駁車，可以看看時間與自己行程有沒有搭上，我們由於是從函館過來，就沒有接駁車了。

  • 札幌JR車站出發：13:30
  • 新千歲機場出發：14:00

更多詳細資訊：https://en.nonokaze-resort.com/access

預定接駁車：https://www.noguchi-g.com/en/contact-bus/?bus_fac_id=17

🏢 飯店環境與設施

絕美的大廳

一走進 TOYA 乃之風湖景度假村，最吸引人的就是大廳那整面的落地窗，從這裡可以直接望向遠方的羊蹄山，美景一覽無遺。即使是沒有入住的遊客，很多人也會特地走進來拍照，這個角度幾乎是來到洞爺湖不可錯過的打卡景點。

大廳內也貼心擺放了許多面對湖景與羊蹄山的座位，住客可以隨時在這裡休息放空，邊欣賞美景，邊悠閒地享受渡假的氛圍。

一開門先經過長長的走廊

櫃檯的空間雖然不算大，但在入住的尖峰時段，現場有不少服務人員協助，不論是直接在櫃檯辦理，或是引導旅客使用自助 Check-in 機器，整體動線安排得還算順暢。值得一提的是，很多員工都會講英文、中文，溝通上相當方便。

我們大約下午三點抵達，雖然正值入住高峰，人潮不少，但整體 Check-in 速度還蠻快的，沒花太多時間就順利進房。


非常寬敞，座位很多的大廳休息區

這蠻特別的，有兩個座位可以讓你直接欣賞音樂

迎賓的蔓越莓果汁與餅乾

大廳旁的展示兼販賣區

飯店內的樓層圖，分為兩館


館內溫泉

乃之風湖景度假村內分為兩個主要館區，各自設有獨立的溫泉浴場：本館頂樓的「展望大浴場」以及俱樂部館的「昭和乃湯」。

展望大浴場

這次我只有體驗頂樓的展望大浴場，室內空間相當寬敞，裡面有大約 3～4 個不同的浴池，搭配整面的落地窗，泡湯的同時就能直接欣賞羊蹄山的壯麗景色。再往上一層樓，則是戶外的露天溫泉區，視野更開闊，零死角直接面對洞爺湖和遠方山景，天氣好的時候真的很美。

不過要提醒一下，露天溫泉的水溫相對室內池偏涼，尤其我們去的時候是五月，洞爺湖一帶天氣還是偏冷，泡在戶外多少會覺得風有點涼，怕冷的人可以自己斟酌要不要上去體驗。



浴場外的休息空間

昭和乃湯

更多照片可以直接觀看官方網站：https://en.nonokaze-resort.com/spa

宴會廳

本館二樓規劃為宴會場，這裡可以看到帶有濃濃和風氛圍的傳統日式宴會廳，主要用來舉辦團體聚會、活動或是私人包場，空間寬敞，整體氛圍也很有日本味。


SPA

同樣為在本館二樓，這裏也有付費的 SPA 區域，來到溫泉旅館渡假，也可以計劃來做個 SPA 放鬆一下。


Select 108

飯店內設有「Select 108」土產店，除了可從館內直接進入，另外也有對外的出入口，方便一般遊客進出。店內販售的商品相當多元，從各式北海道特色零食、飲料，到衣服、杯子、碗盤、生活小物都有。若是入住期間有空，不妨可以來店裡逛逛，無論是買伴手禮、紀念品，或只是隨意走走看看，都蠻適合。

🛏  房間環境

這次我們入住的是本館的房型，房間內有著大片落地窗，視野非常開闊，坐在房內就能直接欣賞洞爺湖與遠方的羊蹄山。不過比較可惜的是，我們這次被安排在五樓，剛好前方有一個小平台，稍微遮擋了部分視線，多少影響了一點湖景的完整度。


桌上有著迎賓的小點心

房間內配置兩張單人床，床墊屬於傳統偏軟的彈簧床，久違的彈簧床讓我稍微不太習慣。枕頭方面則是一顆偏硬、一顆較鬆軟，如果能有介於兩者之間的軟硬度會更理想。



有著一台偏舊且很吵的加濕器

備品陽春且偏舊一點

衛浴的部分是乾濕分離，空間算大的，有附許多不同的備品，且設計也是讓你可以在洗手台就可以直接看到外面的風景，不過設備感覺起來都是偏舊一些，像是有的年代感的高級旅館。





🍽️ 晚餐與早餐

早餐與晚餐我們都選在本館一樓的 Le Vent 餐廳用餐，餐廳擁有整片落地景觀窗，邊吃邊欣賞洞爺湖的美麗湖景，讓用餐氣氛更加愜意。餐點口味也相當不錯，是乃之風眾多好評中大家最推薦的亮點之一。

五月晚間七點入座可以看到的美景

晚餐採自助餐形式，料理種類相當多元，從日式、中式到西式通通都有，像是新鮮的生魚片、現煎牛排、各式熱食、沙拉、甜點與水果，選擇相當豐富，整體口味也都維持不錯水準。其中現場現煎的牛排、日式小菜，以及甜點區的蛋糕和霜淇淋，個人覺得都蠻有水準，適合慢慢享用。

不過比較可惜的是，海鮮的選擇相對少了一些，像是螃蟹、牡蠣這類北海道常見的特色食材，這次並沒有看到，整體偏向以熟食、牛排、甜點為主。如果是特別想大啖海鮮的人，可能會覺得稍微有點可惜。









其中我覺得現煎牛排最好吃，可以搭配蒜片或是馬鈴薯泥

早餐也是在同一個地點用餐，天氣好的時候搭配洞爺湖湖景，實在是非常享受的用餐環境！





會送到桌的奶油馬鈴薯

現榨蘋果汁超新鮮好喝

可以品嚐多種不同的北海道牛奶

🎇 洞爺湖 Long Run 花火大會

這次我們剛好遇上第44屆北海道「洞爺湖 Long Run 花火大會」，活動期間從2025年4月28日持續到10月31日，每晚8點45分準時在洞爺湖湖面施放煙火，煙火秀約持續20分鐘，夜空中絢麗的光影與湖面倒影交織，氣氛十分浪漫迷人。

入住「TOYA乃之風湖景度假村」的最大好處，就是用完晚餐後能直接回到房間，透過大片落地窗舒適地欣賞這場湖上煙火大會，讓整個觀賞體驗更加輕鬆愜意。





整體來說，這次入住「TOYA乃之風湖景度假村」，還是留下了不錯的回憶。無論是貼心的服務、豐富的自助餐、還是湖畔第一排的絕美景觀，都符合預期，特別是能直接在房間欣賞到洞爺湖的花火大會，這種體驗確實很加分。

不過，飯店的房間設備難免有點歲月痕跡，雖然整理得很乾淨，但家具、地毯與整體風格偏舊，床的舒適度也沒有想像中好，對睡眠品質比較要求的人可能會稍微有感。如果是單純追求住宿硬體條件，這部分可能不見得能滿足每個人。

另外，考量到一晚房價基本都落在一萬多台幣，以這個價位來說，景觀、服務確實不錯，但整體硬體若再更新些，會更值得推薦。

title.$t: Toyako Onsen Accommodation | The Lake View TOYA Nonokaze Resort | Stunning Lake View Rooms | Watch the Lake Toya Fireworks Right from Your Room | Front-Row Lake View

content.$t:
You can see Mount Yotei directly from the room

For this Hokkaido trip, we specially arranged a one-night stay at Lake Toya. Just like Lake Kawaguchi, the front-row lake-view spots are mostly pricey hot spring hotels — if you want to soak in the onsen while enjoying the lake view, you usually have to spend a bit more budget. We happened to coincide with Lake Toya's fireworks festival, and considering how convenient and romantic it would be to watch the fireworks right from the room, we spent some time comparing a few front-row lake-view hotels.

In the end we chose "The Lake View TOYA Nonokaze Resort," which has consistently received excellent reviews. Whether it's the room types, the food, or the service, it's one of the most recommended and widely acknowledged top choices in the Lake Toya area. Thinking about it, who knows when we'll come back to Lake Toya next time — although the room rate really isn't cheap, we ultimately decided to treat ourselves to a full lake-view experience.

📜  Information

  • Stay price: $10,942 (one night with two meals + Lake Toya cruise ticket)
  • Address: 29-1 Toyakoonsen, Toyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido 049-5721 Japan
  • Phone: +81570026571
  • Official website: https://nonokaze-resort.com/

Comparing prices between booking sites and the official website, I found that booking directly on the official website is usually cheaper, and you can also pair it with discount packages like a Lake Toya cruise ticket or SPA voucher, making it a better overall deal. If you're planning to stay, I recommend checking the official website first — sometimes there are limited-time offers.

📍 Location

The Lake View TOYA Nonokaze Resort is located right in the heart of the Lake Toya Onsen district, close to the Sakuramachi and Chuo-dori bus stops. Whether it's the lobby, the restaurant, the onsen, or even every guest room, you can see the beautiful Lake Toya and Mount Yotei directly. The scenery is fantastic and the location is very convenient.

Transportation

It's about a 15-minute drive from JR Toya Station. You can get there by bus or by driving yourself.

Shuttle Bus

The hotel offers shuttle buses to and from Sapporo and New Chitose Airport, but you must reserve in advance to use them.

  • Round trip between Sapporo JR Station and the hotel: free
  • Round trip between New Chitose Airport and the hotel: 1,500 yen/person, with an additional 500 yen discount if you book on the official website
However, there's only one shuttle at a fixed time each day, so check whether the timing fits your itinerary. Since we came from Hakodate, there was no shuttle for us.

  • Departs Sapporo JR Station: 13:30
  • Departs New Chitose Airport: 14:00

More details: https://en.nonokaze-resort.com/access

Reserve the shuttle bus: https://www.noguchi-g.com/en/contact-bus/?bus_fac_id=17

🏢 Hotel Environment & Facilities

The stunning lobby

As soon as you step into the TOYA Nonokaze Resort, the most eye-catching feature is the lobby's full wall of floor-to-ceiling windows, from which you can gaze directly at Mount Yotei in the distance — the view is completely unobstructed. Even visitors who aren't staying often come in specially to take photos; this angle is almost a must-visit photo spot when you come to Lake Toya.

The lobby also thoughtfully provides plenty of seating facing the lake and Mount Yotei, where guests can rest and unwind anytime, enjoying the beautiful view while leisurely soaking in the vacation atmosphere.

A long corridor greets you once the door opens

The reception area isn't very large, but during peak check-in hours there were quite a few staff members on hand to help, whether processing check-in directly at the desk or guiding guests to use the self check-in machines, so the overall flow was fairly smooth. Worth noting is that many staff speak English and Chinese, making communication very convenient.

We arrived around 3 p.m., and although it was peak check-in time with quite a crowd, the overall check-in speed was pretty fast, and we got into our room without much delay.


A very spacious lobby lounge with plenty of seating

This is quite special — two seats where you can directly enjoy the music

Welcome cranberry juice and cookies

The display and shopping area next to the lobby

The hotel's floor map, divided into two wings


On-site Onsen

The Nonokaze Resort is divided into two main wings, each with its own separate onsen bathhouse: the "Observation Grand Bath" on the top floor of the Main Building, and "Showa no Yu" in the Club Wing.

Observation Grand Bath

This time I only experienced the top-floor Observation Grand Bath. The indoor space is quite spacious, with about 3–4 different bathing pools, paired with a full wall of floor-to-ceiling windows so you can enjoy the magnificent view of Mount Yotei while soaking. One floor up is the outdoor open-air onsen area, with an even more open view directly facing Lake Toya and the distant mountains with no blind spots — truly gorgeous when the weather is good.

One thing to note, though: the water temperature of the open-air onsen is relatively cooler than the indoor pools. Especially when we went in May, the Lake Toya area was still quite cold, so soaking outdoors did feel a bit breezy. Those who get cold easily may want to consider whether to head up and try it.



The rest area outside the bathhouse

Showa no Yu

For more photos you can view the official website directly: https://en.nonokaze-resort.com/spa

Banquet Hall

The second floor of the Main Building is designed as a banquet venue. Here you can see a traditional Japanese-style banquet hall full of Japanese atmosphere, mainly used for group gatherings, events, or private functions. The space is spacious and the overall atmosphere is very Japanese.


SPA

Also on the second floor of the Main Building, there's a paid SPA area here. When staying at an onsen resort, you can plan to come and relax with a SPA treatment.


Select 108

The hotel has a souvenir shop called "Select 108." Besides being accessible directly from inside the hotel, it also has an outside entrance for the convenience of ordinary visitors. The shop sells a wide variety of goods, from all kinds of Hokkaido specialty snacks and drinks to clothing, cups, tableware, and lifestyle items. If you have some free time during your stay, it's worth dropping by — whether to buy souvenirs and gifts, or just to browse around, it's quite a nice spot.

🛏  Room Environment

This time we stayed in a room in the Main Building. The room has a large floor-to-ceiling window with a very open view, and you can enjoy Lake Toya and Mount Yotei in the distance right from your seat. What was a bit of a pity, though, was that we were assigned to the fifth floor, where there happened to be a small platform in front that slightly blocked part of the view, somewhat affecting the completeness of the lake view.


A welcome snack on the table

The room is furnished with two single beds. The mattresses are the traditional softer spring type, and after a long time it took me a while to get used to the spring bed again. As for the pillows, one was on the firmer side and one was softer — it would have been more ideal to have one with a firmness somewhere in between.



There was a rather old and quite noisy humidifier

The amenities are basic and a bit dated

The bathroom has separated wet and dry areas and is fairly large, with plenty of different amenities provided. The design also lets you look out at the scenery right from the sink. That said, the fixtures all feel a bit dated, like a high-end hotel with some years on it.





🍽️ Dinner & Breakfast

We had both breakfast and dinner at the Le Vent restaurant on the first floor of the Main Building. The restaurant has a full wall of scenic windows, so you can enjoy the beautiful view of Lake Toya while dining, making the atmosphere all the more pleasant. The food is also quite delicious — it's one of the most recommended highlights among Nonokaze's many rave reviews.

The beautiful view you can see when seated at 7 p.m. in May

Dinner is served buffet-style, with a very diverse range of dishes — Japanese, Chinese, and Western, all available — such as fresh sashimi, freshly grilled steak, various hot dishes, salads, desserts, and fruit. The selection is quite rich and the overall taste maintains a good standard. Personally, I thought the freshly grilled steak, the Japanese side dishes, and the cakes and soft-serve ice cream in the dessert area were all of good quality and well worth taking your time to enjoy.

One thing that was a bit of a pity, though, was that the seafood selection was relatively limited — Hokkaido specialty ingredients like crab and oysters weren't to be found this time, with the overall focus leaning toward cooked dishes, steak, and desserts. If you especially want to feast on seafood, you might find it a little disappointing.









Personally I thought the freshly grilled steak was the best — you can pair it with garlic chips or mashed potato

Breakfast is served in the same place, and on a good day, paired with the view of Lake Toya, it's truly a wonderful dining environment!





Buttered potato delivered right to your table

The freshly squeezed apple juice was super fresh and delicious

You can sample several different kinds of Hokkaido milk

🎇 Lake Toya Long Run Fireworks Festival

This time we happened to catch the 44th Hokkaido "Lake Toya Long Run Fireworks Festival." The event runs from April 28 to October 31, 2025, with fireworks launched over Lake Toya at exactly 8:45 p.m. every night. The fireworks show lasts about 20 minutes, and the dazzling lights in the night sky intertwined with the reflections on the lake create a wonderfully romantic and enchanting atmosphere.

The biggest advantage of staying at "The Lake View TOYA Nonokaze Resort" is that after dinner you can head straight back to your room and comfortably enjoy this lakeside fireworks festival through the large floor-to-ceiling windows, making the whole viewing experience all the more relaxing and pleasant.





Overall, this stay at "The Lake View TOYA Nonokaze Resort" left me with a good memory. Whether it was the thoughtful service, the abundant buffet, or the stunning front-row lakeside scenery, everything met expectations. In particular, being able to enjoy the Lake Toya fireworks festival right from the room was truly an experience that added a lot of value.

That said, the room's fixtures inevitably show some signs of age. Although kept very clean, the furniture, carpet, and overall style lean toward the dated side, and the beds weren't as comfortable as I'd imagined. Those with higher demands for sleep quality may notice this somewhat. If you're purely after top-tier hardware, this part might not necessarily satisfy everyone.

Also, considering that a night basically costs over ten thousand TWD, at this price point the views and service are indeed good, but the overall experience would be even more worth recommending if the hardware were a bit more up to date.

title.$t: 洞爺湖美食 | SoupCurry HLAHAL-ハラハル | 北海道美食 | 湯咖喱專門店 | 眺望湖光山色美景

content.$t:
眺望湖光山色

在洞爺湖周邊找餐廳，除了各家溫泉飯店內，在洞爺湖温泉區附近其實也都有蠻多不同的小店可以選擇。這次入住洞爺湖的飯店，在飯店附近找了一家看起來還蠻新穎，雖然網路上資訊不多，不過 Google map 評分也不錯的湯咖哩餐廳。

📜  資訊

  • 地址：27-34 Toyakoonsen, Toyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido 049-5721日本
  • 營業時間：11:00–15:00
  • 聯絡電話：+81142828003
  • 官方網站：https://hlahal.com/

📍 地點與店內環境

SoupCurry HLAHAL 位於洞爺湖兩家著名的溫泉酒店「萬世閣」與「乃之風」之間，從洞爺湖站或溫泉街步行數分鐘即可抵達，店旁設有停車場，也十分適合自駕遊客。

店內採光非常得好

HLAHAL 的意思是：Happy restaurant loved in the area with lake，店內走一個簡樸風格，以木質傢俱與白色色調為主，除了一般座位之外，還有吧台區，種共約有30個座位，空間寬敞不擁擠，採光非常得好。 


餐廳中最大的亮點為湖景景觀窗，雖然隔著停車場，但還是能將洞爺湖風光盡收眼底，遠眺羊駝山風景，讓人感受如同身處湖畔咖啡館的舒適。 


🍽️ 餐點與菜單

湯咖哩菜單

什麼是湯咖哩？

湯咖哩是起源於北海道札幌的「soupy curry」，不同於濃稠的日式咖哩，它湯汁清爽、偏湯盆型。底湯通常以雞骨湯或蔬菜湯為基礎，加入咖哩粉、香料、中式藥材、薑、蒜、番茄膏，再依店家風格添加椰奶或其他特色食材。

SoupCurry HLAHAL 的湯咖喱

SoupCurry HLAHAL 主要販售湯咖哩，蔬菜都使用北海道的在地蔬菜，搭配不同的主菜，例如海鮮、豬肉、牛肉，或是蔬菜等等，可以選擇咖喱的辣度與飯量，這裡附上的會是薑黃飯。

豬肉湯咖哩

牛肉湯咖哩

飲品、小點與冰淇淋




整體來說，SoupCurry HLAHAL 的用餐環境真的非常不錯，店內乾淨舒適，大片落地窗外就是洞爺湖的美景，邊吃邊欣賞湖光山色，格外享受。餐點部分，湯咖哩的湯頭濃郁香醇，香氣撲鼻卻不會讓人覺得油膩，搭配炸過的蔬菜，口感層次豐富，吃起來既清爽又有滿足感。至於肉類的表現，個人覺得就比較普通可惜了，肉質稍微偏硬一些，但整體來說還算不錯，沒有影響整體的用餐體驗。

如果你來到洞爺湖，想找個舒服的地方邊用餐邊欣賞湖景，這間店很值得安排進你的行程，尤其推薦給喜歡湯咖哩的人來試試看！

title.$t: Lake Toya Dining | SoupCurry HLAHAL | Hokkaido Food | Soup Curry Specialty Restaurant | Stunning Lake and Mountain Views

content.$t:
Gazing at the lake and mountain scenery

When looking for a restaurant around Lake Toya, aside from the various hot spring hotels, there are actually quite a few different small eateries to choose from near the Lake Toya hot spring district. For this stay at a Lake Toya hotel, I found a soup curry restaurant near the hotel that looked quite new and modern. Although there wasn't much information online, it had a pretty good rating on Google Maps.

📜  Information

  • Address: 27-34 Toyakoonsen, Toyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido 049-5721, Japan
  • Opening hours: 11:00–15:00
  • Phone: +81142828003
  • Official website: https://hlahal.com/

📍 Location and Interior

SoupCurry HLAHAL is located between two of Lake Toya's famous hot spring hotels, "Manseikaku" and "Nonokaze". It's just a few minutes' walk from Toya Station or the hot spring street, and there is a parking lot next to the restaurant, making it very convenient for those traveling by car as well.

The interior has excellent natural lighting

HLAHAL stands for "Happy restaurant loved in the area with lake." The interior has a simple, rustic style, featuring mainly wooden furniture and white tones. In addition to regular seating, there is also a bar area, with about 30 seats in total. The space is spacious and uncrowded, with excellent natural lighting. 


The biggest highlight of the restaurant is the lake-view window. Although the parking lot lies in between, you can still take in the full scenery of Lake Toya and gaze out at Mount Yotei (Ezo Fuji) in the distance, giving you the cozy feeling of being in a lakeside café. 


🍽️ Meals and Menu

Soup curry menu

What is soup curry?

Soup curry, or "soupy curry," originated in Sapporo, Hokkaido. Unlike thick, gooey Japanese curry, its broth is light and refreshing, served in a soup-bowl style. The base broth is usually made from chicken bone stock or vegetable stock, with curry powder, spices, Chinese medicinal herbs, ginger, garlic, and tomato paste added, and then depending on the restaurant's style, coconut milk or other signature ingredients are added.

SoupCurry HLAHAL's Soup Curry

SoupCurry HLAHAL mainly serves soup curry, using locally grown Hokkaido vegetables paired with different main ingredients, such as seafood, pork, beef, or vegetables. You can choose the spiciness level of the curry and the amount of rice, and it comes served with turmeric rice.

Pork soup curry

Beef soup curry

Drinks, snacks, and ice cream




Overall, the dining environment at SoupCurry HLAHAL is really excellent. The interior is clean and comfortable, and just outside the large floor-to-ceiling windows is the beautiful scenery of Lake Toya. Enjoying the lake and mountain views while dining is especially delightful. As for the food, the soup curry has a rich, fragrant broth that is aromatic yet not greasy, paired with deep-fried vegetables for a layered and varied texture that tastes both refreshing and satisfying. As for the meat, I personally found it a bit ordinary and a little disappointing, as it was slightly tough. But overall it was still quite good and didn't detract from the overall dining experience.

If you come to Lake Toya and want a comfortable place to dine while enjoying the lake view, this restaurant is well worth adding to your itinerary—especially recommended for those who love soup curry!

content.$t:
函館山百萬夜景

函館，位於北海道南端，是一座融合歷史、海港與夜景的迷人城市，這次我們的北海道之旅，第一站就到達函館。由於第一天抵達函館市區差不多都已經晚上了，只留下了隔天完整的一天可以在函館走走，因此只鎖定了最想看的幾個重要景點：函館山百萬夜景、八幡坂、金森紅磚倉庫與五稜郭，以及當地著名的「函館朝市」與「幸運小丑漢堡」。

必訪景點

  • 幸運小丑漢堡
  • 函館朝市
  • 五稜郭
  • 金森紅磚倉庫
  • 八幡坂
  • 函館山百萬夜景

行程參考

Day 1：幸運小丑漢堡晚餐
Day 2：
  • 函館朝市早餐
  • 五稜郭、五稜郭塔
  • 金森紅磚倉庫
    • Pastry Snaffle’s
    • Petite Merveille
  • 八幡坂
  • 函館山百萬夜景

  幸運小丑漢堡


幸運小丑漢堡：函館車站店

被當地人譽為靈魂美食、多次被日本美食家票選為全日本最好吃的漢堡的 -「幸運小丑漢堡」，是一家有 17 家分店，但全部分店都只在函館，也可以說是一家只在函館才吃得到的漢堡店，也是這次在查函館美食的時候，一定會出現推薦的必吃食物之一！

分店位置：https://luckypierrot.jp/ch/shop/

幸運小丑漢堡的分店都有著非常獨特(?)的風格，除了到處貼滿各種廣告介紹之外，店內還充滿各式各樣不同的周邊商品，非常的特別。

其中，大家都推薦要試試看的是：中華雞腿堡、荷包蛋漢堡，還有幸運薯條：

一開始預期是不是和台灣的拉亞漢堡、麥味登差不多的口味，但沒想到吃了覺得比預期要好吃不少，如果有到函館，可以選擇一餐來試試看。

  函館朝市


函館朝市官方網站：https://www.hakodate.travel/cht/sightseeing-spots/shopping-spot/hakodate-morning-market/

營業時間：5:00am - 2:00pm (主要根據各店鋪而定)

函館朝市始於二次大戰後，於1945年函館車站前的廣場角落開始流行早市，後來於1956年遷移至現時若松町的所在地，一路發展至今，已經有 250 間的店舖，以新鮮的海產為代表，蔬菜、水果、零食、乾貨等函館與北海道的美味食材都可以在這裡找到，是觀光客來到函館必訪的景點之一。

市場裡還有個很特別的釣烏賊體驗，可以使用釣竿釣活烏賊，店家會現場料理。而函館朝市的どんぶり横丁市場，還有提供許多平價又豐盛的海鮮料理，許多人會到這裡來享用早餐。

朝市內應有盡有，除了海鮮與土特產外，還有販售許多現切的水果，可以直接買來享用。另外，朝市外圍也有許多小店家，有著許多新鮮海鮮的料理，都可以在這裡吃到。



  五稜郭


五稜郭，是日本江戶時代末期由江戶幕府，在現北海道函館市郊外建造的一座星形要塞。五稜郭獲日本政府指定為特別史跡，在1914年改建為五稜郭公園，並且對外開放，自此成為函館市民的休憩地方和代表函館的旅遊景點之一。

五稜郭塔

五稜郭的位置距離函館車站附近較遠，需要搭乘公車、或是電車才能夠抵達。如果是從函館車站附近出發的話，推薦可以搭乘函館車站前的公車 (都可以使用西瓜卡)，會直接抵達五稜郭塔下，如果搭乘路面電車，電車站還需要步行 10~15 分鐘的路程。

如果想要拍照完整的五稜郭，一定要到五陵郭塔展望台，這裡可以看到整個五稜郭，也是最常出現在明信片中的必拍角度。

而五稜郭公園一圈大約 1.8 km，這裡很多人在跑步，或是遛狗，很適合在天氣好的時候，慢慢的散步走一圈，沿途也都有椅子隨時可以坐下來休息。


  金森紅磚倉庫


而另外一個最具代表性的景點，不能不提位在海灣邊的「金森紅磚倉庫（金森赤レンガ倉庫）」。這排紅磚建築不只是一座倉庫群，更是從19世紀至今，見證城市興衰與蛻變的重要舞台，如今改建成集合購物、美食與展演空間的文創聚落，和台北的松菸有點像，但多了一點異國港口的浪漫氛圍。

金森倉庫的歷史可以追溯到1859年函館開港，當時從長崎來的渡邊熊四郎在這裡設立第一家營業倉庫，見證了函館由貿易港口一路發展至現代城市的歷程。現在看到的建築，是1909年重建後保留下來的模樣。

整個倉庫群分成四個主要區域：

  • BAY函館：甜點店、雜貨選物。
  • 金森洋物館：有20多間小店，還有積木體驗室、聖誕老公公郵筒。
  • 函館歷史廣場：有啤酒館和在地料理，能喝到函館限定的自釀啤酒。
  • 金森廳：不定期舉辦音樂會或展演活動。

可參考官方網站：https://hakodate-kanemori.com/tw

這裡有兩家必吃的起司蛋糕，Pastry Snaffle’s 與 Petite Merveille，都是北海道著名的伴手禮，不妨在逛街之餘，坐下來休息一下，享受一下下午茶時光吧。

Pastry Snaffle’s

Petite Merveille


  八幡坂


八幡坂是電影、日劇、廣告常出現的經典場景，最知名的莫過於一整條筆直街道直通港口、盡頭還能看到船隻與海面的視角。八幡坂的名字，來自於過去坂上有一間「函館八幡宮」。雖然現在神社已不在，但這條斜坡卻成了函館元町地區的象徵。

在走上來八幡坂後，由於接著要直接去搭纜車上函館山，如果再走回港口，就要再走一次上坡，建議最好是直接從八幡坂上方筆直地走過去。

而我們隨意找了一家茶房 Sakura-Ya (tea house)，是一間改建自古民宅的咖啡店，外觀低調內斂，裡面是和式木造空間搭配昏黃燈光，有種難得的靜謐感。


鯨魚湯


  函館山百萬夜景


函館山夜景｜世界三大夜景之一

來到函館的重頭戲，絕對是被譽為世界三大夜景之一的函館山夜景。函館山標高334公尺，不算高，但因為城市剛好被海灣包夾，從山頂俯瞰整個市區，就像一顆閃閃發亮的寶石橫臥在夜色之中。這樣的景致，也讓函館夜景和香港、那不勒斯並列為「世界三大夜景」之一。

最建議就是下午到傍晚這段時間上山，因為可以先看一眼白天的港口全景，接著坐在觀景台慢慢等待夕陽、看整座城市從橘金轉為深藍，隨後街道一盞盞亮起，就像有人悄悄點亮星空下的地圖。

函館山最方便的上山方式是搭函館山纜車，大約3分鐘就能抵達山頂站。也可以選擇開車、搭巴士或健行，但冬季時部分道路會封閉，建議以纜車最好。

content.$t:
Mt. Hakodate Million-Dollar Night View

Hakodate, located at the southern tip of Hokkaido, is a charming city that blends history, a harbor and stunning night views. On this Hokkaido trip, Hakodate was our very first stop. Since we didn't arrive in the city until the evening of the first day, we only had one full day left to explore Hakodate, so we focused on just a few of the most important sights we most wanted to see: the Mt. Hakodate million-dollar night view, Hachiman-zaka Slope, the Kanemori Red Brick Warehouse and Goryokaku, along with the locally famous "Hakodate Morning Market" and "Lucky Pierrot Burger."

Must-Visit Attractions

  • Lucky Pierrot Burger
  • Hakodate Morning Market
  • Goryokaku
  • Kanemori Red Brick Warehouse
  • Hachiman-zaka Slope
  • Mt. Hakodate Million-Dollar Night View

Itinerary Reference

Day 1: Dinner at Lucky Pierrot Burger
Day 2:
  • Breakfast at Hakodate Morning Market
  • Goryokaku & Goryokaku Tower
  • Kanemori Red Brick Warehouse
    • Pastry Snaffle's
    • Petite Merveille
  • Hachiman-zaka Slope
  • Mt. Hakodate Million-Dollar Night View

  Lucky Pierrot Burger


Lucky Pierrot Burger: Hakodate Station Branch

Praised by locals as a soul food and repeatedly voted by Japanese gourmets as the best burger in all of Japan, "Lucky Pierrot Burger" has 17 branches—but all of them are located only in Hakodate. In other words, it's a burger shop you can only eat at in Hakodate, and it's definitely one of the must-try foods that always shows up when you search for Hakodate cuisine!

Branch locations: https://luckypierrot.jp/ch/shop/

Every Lucky Pierrot branch has a very distinctive (?) style—besides being plastered all over with all kinds of advertisements and introductions, the shops are also full of all sorts of different merchandise, which is quite special.

Among them, the items everyone recommends trying are: the Chinese Chicken Burger, the Fried Egg Burger, and the Lucky Fries:

At first I expected the flavors to be about the same as Taiwan's Laya Burger or MWEDaan, but to my surprise it turned out to be noticeably tastier than expected. If you visit Hakodate, it's worth trying for a meal.

  Hakodate Morning Market


Hakodate Morning Market official website: https://www.hakodate.travel/cht/sightseeing-spots/shopping-spot/hakodate-morning-market/

Opening hours: 5:00am - 2:00pm (mainly depending on each shop)

The Hakodate Morning Market began after World War II. In 1945 a morning market started to flourish at a corner of the plaza in front of Hakodate Station, and later in 1956 it moved to its present location in Wakamatsu-cho, developing steadily ever since. Today it has 250 shops. Best known for its fresh seafood, it's also where you can find delicious ingredients from Hakodate and Hokkaido such as vegetables, fruits, snacks and dried goods—making it one of the must-visit spots for tourists coming to Hakodate.

The market also has a very special squid-fishing experience, where you can use a fishing rod to catch a live squid, and the shop will cook it fresh on the spot. In addition, the Donburi Yokocho market within the Hakodate Morning Market offers many affordable and hearty seafood dishes, and many people come here to enjoy breakfast.

The morning market has everything you could want. Besides seafood and local specialties, there are also many freshly cut fruits you can buy and enjoy right away. In addition, there are many small shops around the market's outer edge serving all kinds of fresh seafood dishes that you can also enjoy here.



  Goryokaku


Goryokaku is a star-shaped fort built by the Edo shogunate at the end of Japan's Edo period, on the outskirts of what is now Hakodate City in Hokkaido. Goryokaku has been designated a Special Historic Site by the Japanese government, and in 1914 it was converted into Goryokaku Park and opened to the public, becoming a place of relaxation for Hakodate residents and one of the city's representative tourist attractions.

Goryokaku Tower

Goryokaku is located fairly far from the area around Hakodate Station, and you'll need to take a bus or a tram to get there. If you're setting out from near Hakodate Station, we recommend taking the bus in front of Hakodate Station (both can be used with a Suica card), which will take you directly to the base of Goryokaku Tower. If you take the tram, it's still a 10–15 minute walk from the tram stop.

If you want to photograph the full Goryokaku, you absolutely must go up to the Goryokaku Tower observation deck—from here you can see the entire star fort, which is also the most iconic must-shoot angle you often see on postcards.

A loop around Goryokaku Park is about 1.8 km. Many people jog or walk their dogs here, and it's a great place to take a slow stroll around on a nice day. There are also benches along the way where you can sit down and rest anytime.


  Kanemori Red Brick Warehouse


Another of the most iconic spots not to be missed is the "Kanemori Red Brick Warehouse (Kanemori Aka Renga Souko)" by the bay. This row of red brick buildings is not just a warehouse complex—it has been an important stage witnessing the city's rise, fall and transformation from the 19th century to today. Now it has been converted into a cultural and creative district combining shopping, dining and performance spaces. It's a bit like Taipei's Songshan Cultural Park, but with an added touch of the romance of an exotic port.

The history of Kanemori Warehouse can be traced back to the opening of Hakodate Port in 1859, when Kumashiro Watanabe, who came from Nagasaki, established the first commercial warehouse here, witnessing Hakodate's journey from a trading port to a modern city. The buildings you see today are what has been preserved after the 1909 reconstruction.

The entire warehouse complex is divided into four main areas:

  • BAY Hakodate: dessert shops and curated goods.
  • Kanemori Yobutsukan: over 20 small shops, plus a building-block experience room and a Santa Claus mailbox.
  • Hakodate History Plaza: has a beer hall and local cuisine, where you can drink craft beer exclusive to Hakodate.
  • Kanemori Hall: hosts occasional concerts and performances.

Refer to the official website: https://hakodate-kanemori.com/tw

There are two must-try cheesecakes here, Pastry Snaffle's and Petite Merveille, both famous Hokkaido souvenirs. While you're shopping, why not sit down and take a break to enjoy some afternoon tea time?

Pastry Snaffle's

Petite Merveille


  Hachiman-zaka Slope


Hachiman-zaka is a classic scene that frequently appears in films, Japanese dramas and commercials. Its most famous view is that of an entirely straight street running directly down to the harbor, with ships and the sea visible at the far end. The name Hachiman-zaka comes from a "Hakodate Hachiman-gu" shrine that once stood at the top of the slope. Although the shrine is no longer there, this slope has become a symbol of Hakodate's Motomachi district.

After walking up Hachiman-zaka, since we were heading straight to take the ropeway up Mt. Hakodate next, walking back down to the harbor would mean climbing back up the slope again. So it's best to head straight across from the top of Hachiman-zaka.

We randomly found a place called Sakura-Ya (tea house), a café converted from an old traditional house. Its exterior is understated and restrained, and inside is a Japanese-style wooden space paired with dim, warm lighting—giving it a rare sense of tranquility.


Whale Soup


  Mt. Hakodate Million-Dollar Night View


Mt. Hakodate Night View | One of the World's Three Great Night Views

The highlight of a visit to Hakodate is undoubtedly the Mt. Hakodate night view, hailed as one of the world's three great night views. Mt. Hakodate stands 334 meters tall—not very high—but because the city happens to be flanked on both sides by bays, looking down over the whole city from the summit is like seeing a glittering jewel lying amid the night. This scenery has earned Hakodate's night view a place alongside Hong Kong and Naples as one of the "world's three great night views."

The best time to go up is from afternoon to dusk, because you can first catch a glimpse of the full harbor panorama in daylight, then sit at the observation deck and slowly wait for the sunset, watching the entire city shift from orange-gold to deep blue. Afterward the streets light up one lamp at a time, as if someone were quietly lighting up a map beneath the starry sky.

The most convenient way up Mt. Hakodate is to take the Mt. Hakodate Ropeway, which reaches the summit station in about 3 minutes. You can also choose to drive, take a bus or hike, but some roads are closed in winter, so the ropeway is recommended as the best option.

content.$t:
入住 The Royal Park Canvas 的時候，我們並沒有預定飯店的早餐，而是選擇來到了旁邊這家在在札幌平價連鎖日式麵包店，Donguri Odori 大通公園店，來享用早餐。

📜  資訊

  • 地址：札幌市中央区大通西1丁目13 ル・トロワ1F
  • 營業時間：10:00–21:00
  • 官方網站：https://www.donguri-bake.co.jp/shop/odori/

📍 地點與店內環境

Donguri Odori 是在札幌連鎖的日式麵包店，這間大通公園的分店，地點位於大通公園站地鐵出口24的位置，一上來就可以看到 le trois 這間百貨，Donguri Odori 就位於一樓的位置。

🍽️ 餐點

一進來 le trois 這間百貨，可以很明顯的看到 Donguri Odori 的位置，以及陳列出來各式各樣的不同麵包。





品相與種類都很多，有鹹的麵包、也有甜的麵包，還有些炸物類，非常豐富，選擇很多。

麵包的價位大概都 100 多日圓～200、300 日元不等，自行夾好麵包後去櫃台結帳，在櫃檯也可以一起點飲料，如咖啡、熱巧克力或是奶茶等等，來搭配麵包。





旁邊有著一曲的內用做為區，內用座位雖然不多，但大部分人吃完就會離開，所以位置也不會等待太久。


後方的廚房持續在做麵包

用餐完後自行回收即可

這趟北海道行程幾乎都沒有預定早餐，光是 Donguri Odori 就吃了兩次當早餐，實在是很方便且又不會很貴，唯一缺點可能是早上 10 點才開始營業，如果一早要吃早餐就要稍微等待一下囉。

title.$t: Sapporo Food | Donguri Odori | Affordable Japanese Bakery Chain in Sapporo | Hokkaido Food | Next to Odori Park and Sapporo TV Tower

content.$t:
When we stayed at The Royal Park Canvas, we didn't book the hotel breakfast. Instead, we chose to come to this affordable Japanese bakery chain right next door, Donguri Odori Odori Park branch, to enjoy breakfast.

📜  Information

  • Address: Le Trois 1F, 1-13 Odori Nishi, Chuo-ku, Sapporo
  • Opening hours: 10:00–21:00
  • Official website: https://www.donguri-bake.co.jp/shop/odori/

📍 Location & Interior

Donguri Odori is a Japanese bakery chain in Sapporo. This Odori Park branch is located right at Exit 24 of Odori Park Station. As soon as you come up, you'll see the Le Trois department store, and Donguri Odori is located on the first floor.

🍽️ The Food

As soon as you step into the Le Trois department store, you can clearly spot Donguri Odori, along with all kinds of different breads on display.





There is a great variety in both appearance and type — savory breads, sweet breads, and even some deep-fried items — very abundant with plenty of choices.

The bread prices range roughly from just over 100 yen to 200 or 300 yen. After picking your own bread with tongs, you head to the counter to pay, where you can also order drinks such as coffee, hot chocolate, or milk tea to go with your bread.





Next to the counter there is a small dine-in area. Although there aren't many seats, most people leave once they finish eating, so you won't have to wait long for a spot.


The kitchen in the back keeps baking bread

Just clear your own table when you're done

On this Hokkaido trip we hardly booked any breakfasts, and we ended up eating at Donguri Odori twice for breakfast alone — it's really convenient and not expensive at all. The only downside is that it doesn't open until 10 a.m., so if you want to eat breakfast early in the morning, you'll have to wait a little while.
