title.$t: Taipei Attractions | Beitou Hot Spring Museum | A Public Bathhouse from the Japanese Colonial Era | Free Admission

content.$t:
Did you know that the building in Beitou Park that blends Japanese and Western architectural styles is actually the Beitou Hot Spring Museum?

The Beitou Hot Spring Museum was formerly the "Beitou Public Bathhouse." Its signature feature is a two-story building in a Japanese-Western eclectic style, and at the time it was the largest public hot spring bathhouse in East Asia. In 1997 the Ministry of the Interior designated the Beitou Public Bathhouse as a Grade 3 historic site, and the following year, in 1998, it officially reopened under the name "Beitou Hot Spring Museum."

Admission is free, and guided tours are offered on weekdays as well. It's a spot right in the city that's well worth a visit.

  • Address: No. 2, Zhongshan Rd., Beitou District, Taipei 112
  • Opening hours: Tuesday to Sunday 10:00–18:00 (last admission 17:45)
  • Admission: Free
  • Official website: https://hotspringmuseum.taipei/

🚃 Transport / Parking Info

Xinbeitou MRT Station

The Beitou Hot Spring Museum is near Xinbeitou MRT Station, so getting there by MRT is very convenient!

MRT

Take the MRT Tamsui Line to "Xinbeitou Station," then walk about 5–10 minutes.

Bus

Take bus 216, 216 (Shuttle), 218, 218 (Shuttle) or 266 and get off at "Beitou Park," or take Xiao 22 and get off at "Beitou Park Station," then walk about 5 minutes toward Zhongshan Road.

Driving

If you drive, you'll need to park near Xinbeitou MRT Station and walk from there.


🏞 Entrance Info

Entrance to the Beitou Hot Spring Museum

If you walk in through Beitou Park, after passing the Beitou Library you'll see the side of the Beitou Hot Spring Museum — the actual main entrance requires going up the stairs to Zhongshan Road!


Since the Beitou Hot Spring Museum is a Grade 3 historic site, its maximum capacity is 200 people, so staff at the entrance control the number of visitors. You also need to take off your shoes and change into the slippers provided, to keep shoes from scratching or damaging the wooden building.

🏞 Inside the Museum

Tatami Activity Hall

As soon as you enter the museum, the first space you reach is the Tatami Activity Hall. Here you can imagine how people once cooled off on the tatami after bathing; this was also where they dined and rested, and you can take in views of the whole Beitou valley and the park.


The "Observation Deck," next to the tatami hall, where bathers could rest and admire Beitou's mountain and water scenery

The Beitou Hot Spring Museum has two floors, each with a number of different exhibition areas focusing on Beitou's history, the hot spring culture of the era, and the development of hot spring inns. Exhibits may change over time, so check the Beitou Hot Spring Museum's official website for the latest exhibition information.

During this visit, the special exhibition "Beitou Impressions: Bathing Again" was on display, presenting the hot spring culture of the time. On the second floor there's the "Hot Spring DOZO" exhibition area, which mainly introduces the development history of Beitou's hot spring inns, with plenty of cultural and historical stories, alongside lots of photo-friendly setups. There isn't a huge amount of content, but overall it's quite interesting.

The "Hot Spring DOZO" exhibition area

Beitou Hot Spring Waters


Symbiotic Industries – Beitou Banquet Cuisine

The staircase also retains its original wooden style

The "Beitou Bathhouse SENTO" exhibition area

The first floor mainly preserves the original bathing pools. The adjacent "Beitou Bathhouse SENTO" exhibition area recreates Taiwan's bathing culture of the time, with two small pools and a VIP bath room. This space mainly served female guests, since few women bathed in hot springs back then — those who came usually did so as family members accompanying others.

The small pools and VIP bath room, which mainly served female guests

Some artifacts and photos from the era

The Great Bath

Another section is the Great Bath. During the Japanese colonial period this was the men's bath, where you had to stand while soaking. Surrounded by large arched columns, it was the largest bathing pool in East Asia at the time.

I chose to visit on a weekday, but there were still quite a lot of visitors. The building is very well maintained, and there are many more exhibits inside — well worth visiting in person and savoring at your own pace.

title.$t: 台北住宿 | 台北晶華酒店 Regent Taipei | 中山北路上的老字號五星級飯店 | 19坪精緻套房

content.$t:
1990 年開始營運的台北晶華酒店，是位於中山北路上的老字號五星級飯店，也是晶華國際酒店集團的旗艦飯店，所在的地點非常的方便，離捷運中山站與中山商圈都非常近，相信住在台北的人都不陌生。

除了飯店之外，比較特別的是它的地下層設有精品商場「麗晶精品」，館內也有許多有名的餐廳與商店，自己也是從小時候就有來過這裡吃飯。但通常不會特別居住在台北的住宿，今年剛好有機會，入住了同一個房型兩次，就來分享一下內部究竟是如何。

📜  資訊

  • 入住日期：2022-05-25 & 2022-12-03
  • 入住房型：精緻套房
  • 付款方式：可刷卡，可打統編
  • 飯店地址：台北市中山區中山北路二段39巷3號
  • 聯絡電話：0225238000
  • 訂房網站：https://www.booking.com/hotel/tw/the-regent-taipei.en.html?aid=8003516

📍 地點位置

台北晶華酒店的地點就在捷運中山站附近的中山北路上，附近除了有非常熱鬧的中山商圈之外，餐廳也是非常非常的多，地段十分的好。

捷運

淡水信義線中山站3號出口，步行約6分鐘

公車

218、220、221、227、247、260、261、287、310 於國賓飯店站下車，步行約3分鐘

自行開車

停車場的入口在林森北路與中山北路二段45巷的交叉處，車位並不是很多，不過附近也還有蠻多停車場的。另外，台北晶華酒店的停車場有兩層，但是電梯只有一台可以到大廳，電梯也沒有到很大，並不是很好等，尖峰的時刻往往都要等非常久。

photo from 台北晶華酒店


🏢 飯店環境

寬敞明亮的大廳

大廳的櫃檯

飯店的接待櫃檯位於 2 樓，大廳明亮寬敞，就算是超過30年的飯店，但內部維持的都還蠻不錯的，接待櫃檯後方會有一區沙發區域，提供訪客可以在這裡稍作休息，或是當作等待 checkin 的地點。 

台北晶華酒店一直都是很熱門的住宿地點，導致每次來到這個大廳幾乎都是人滿為患，吵雜程度也是蠻高的，快要跟菜市場一樣？雖然飯店員工服務都蠻不錯，但這次兩次入住都沒辦法在 3~4 點抵達的時候準時入住，都必須要在這沙發區多等待將近 30 分鐘房間才準備好，而且通常這裡都會坐滿沒有位置，這點倒是對於體驗有一些小扣分。

再往裡面走一點，有一個大中庭也是台北晶華酒店讓人印象深刻的地方，每到聖誕節前後，就會有一顆三層樓高的聖誕樹，也會有燈光秀搭配音樂，讓在這裡用餐的旅客有著很不錯的體驗。

來到台北晶華酒店入住，不妨可以考慮一樓餐廳 azie 的著名牛肉麵，曾獲美國有線電視網CNN評選為”台北最讚牛肉麵”，並多次受邀前往紐約、東京、以及香港客座。口味自己覺得是真的還蠻好吃的，不管是牛肉份量、嫩度都很不錯，不過一碗牛肉麵要超過 $500 元，口袋不深的可以嚐一次體驗看看就好 😅

晶華紅燒牛肉麵

🛏  房間環境

精緻套房全景

這次入住的房型是位於15樓的精緻套房，位於電梯旁的第一間，室內有著19坪的一房一廳，空間十分的寬敞，一進門還有個一個玄關來與客廳內部做區隔，雖然內部裝潢感覺得出年代感，不能與近幾年的新興飯店相比，但是整潔度與整體維持的程度都還是非常好。

一進門的玄關

一進門看到的景色

五星旅館必備的膠囊咖啡與基本的茶包

冰箱內有很充足的飲料和啤酒

桌上的迎賓水果

客廳與臥室各有一台電視，也各有一個大片的窗戶，剛好我們這面可以看到林森公園，不過台北市中心的景色不怎麼樣就是了。

臥室的床 size 非常的大，是由兩個床併起來的，軟硬度也很適中，兩次入住睡起來都還蠻舒適的。隔音方面也不錯，兩次入住都是假日(一次週日晚、一次週六晚)，夜晚都沒有聽到其他房間或是任何走廊上的聲音。


床頭兩邊都有 USB 充電孔

另一個角度的房間

浴室的部分也是非常的大，有著淋浴、也有浴缸，也還有一個更衣空間，這裡有著衣櫃與保險箱，但與浴室沒有任何的們區隔，是屬於同一個空間。

佔地也很廣的浴室

提供浴袍、拖鞋與保險箱

如同其他晶英體系的酒店一樣，都是使用沐蘭的備品

很大的洗手台檯面

一人 size 的浴缸 & 免治馬桶

🏢 飯店設施

台北晶華酒店一般房客可以使用的設施大概就只有健身房、頂樓溫水游泳池與5F的兒童遊戲室了，其他如沐蘭 SPA、Sky Studio 都是需要額外付費的。

健身房，照片取自官方網站: https://www.regenttaiwan.com/wellness

健身俱樂部
營業時間： 早上 6:30 – 晚上 10:30
三溫暖營業時間: 早上 7:00 – 晚上 10:30(最後入場：晚上10:00)


往頂樓的溫水游泳池



頂樓的溫水游泳池，晚上的時候會有露天電影院，天氣好可以來這裡

露天溫水游泳池

開放時間：早上 6:30 – 晚上 10:00


🍽 早餐


早上的早餐是在 brasserie 栢麗廳用餐，現在還算是疫情期間，所以有作分流，7:00/8:00/9:00 各三個時段。栢麗廳也是台北著名的自助餐之一，還曾經被 CNN 評為唯一推薦台北必吃自助式早餐，早餐很豐盛、菜色很多，食物口味也都很不錯，以飯店早餐來說沒什麼特別可挑惕的。


高挑的用餐空間

 聖誕節入住的房卡

台北晶華酒店一直以為不太會有機會入住(畢竟就住在附近...)，這次實際入住之後，體驗還是真的蠻不錯，不愧是一直存活到現在的老字號飯店之一。加上處於中山商圈，附近逛街、觀光，或是美食都很多，地點也是優勢之一。至今住過幾間晶華集團旗下的飯店，體驗都蠻一致蠻不錯的，是值得推薦可以回訪的住宿地點。

其他晶英系列飯店：

  • 台南晶英酒店 Silks Place Tainan
  • 太魯閣晶英酒店 Silks Place Taroko

title.$t: Taipei Accommodation | Regent Taipei | Spacious Junior Suite | A Classic Five-Star Hotel in Zhongshan District

content.$t:
Regent Taipei, which began operations in 1990, is a well-established five-star hotel located on Zhongshan North Road. It is also the flagship hotel of the Silks Hotel Group. The location is incredibly convenient, being very close to Zhongshan MRT Station and the Zhongshan shopping district. I believe anyone living in Taipei is no stranger to it.

Besides the hotel itself, what makes it special is the "Regent Galleria," a luxury shopping mall located on its basement levels. There are also many famous restaurants and shops within the building. I have been coming here to eat since I was a child. However, I usually don't stay in hotels in Taipei. This year, I happened to have the opportunity to stay in the same room type twice, so I'm here to share what it's like inside.

📜 Information

  • Stay Dates: 2022-05-25 & 2022-12-03
  • Room Type: Junior Suite
  • Payment: Credit cards accepted, Tax ID number available
  • Address: No. 3, Ln. 39, Sec. 2, Zhongshan N. Rd., Zhongshan Dist., Taipei City 104, Taiwan
  • Phone: +886-2-2523-8000
  • Booking Website: https://www.booking.com/hotel/tw/the-regent-taipei.en.html?aid=8003516

📍 Location

Regent Taipei is located on Zhongshan North Road, near Zhongshan MRT Station. In addition to the bustling Zhongshan shopping district nearby, there are also countless restaurants in the area. The location is excellent.

MRT

Tamsui-Xinyi Line (Red Line), Zhongshan Station, Exit 3. About a 6-minute walk.

Bus

Bus 218, 220, 221, 227, 247, 260, 261, 287, 310. Get off at the Ambassador Hotel stop and walk for about 3 minutes.

Driving

The entrance to the parking lot is at the intersection of Linsen North Road and Lane 45, Section 2, Zhongshan North Road. Parking spaces aren't plentiful, but there are quite a few other parking lots nearby. Additionally, Regent Taipei has two levels of parking, but only one elevator goes up to the lobby. The elevator isn't very large and is not easy to wait for; waiting times can be quite long during peak hours.

Photo from Regent Taipei


🏢 Hotel Environment

Spacious and bright lobby

Lobby reception counter

The hotel's reception counter is located on the 2nd floor. The lobby is bright and spacious. Even though the hotel is over 30 years old, the interior is well-maintained. Behind the reception counter is a sofa area where visitors can rest or wait for check-in.

Regent Taipei has always been a popular accommodation choice, which means the lobby is almost always crowded. The noise level is quite high—almost like a market? Although the staff service is good, during both my stays, I couldn't check in on time when arriving between 3-4 PM. I had to wait in the sofa area for nearly 30 minutes for the room to be ready. Moreover, this area is usually full with no seats available, which slightly deducted points from the experience.

Walking further inside, the grand atrium is another impressive feature of Regent Taipei. Around Christmas, there's a three-story tall Christmas tree, accompanied by light shows and music, providing a great experience for dining guests.

When staying at Regent Taipei, you might want to consider trying the famous beef noodle soup at the **azie** restaurant on the first floor. It was once voted "Taipei's Best Beef Noodles" by CNN and has been invited for guest appearances in New York, Tokyo, and Hong Kong. Personally, I think it tastes really good; both the portion and tenderness of the beef are excellent. However, a bowl of beef noodles costs over $500 TWD, so if you're on a budget, trying it once for the experience is probably enough 😅

Regent Braised Beef Noodles

🛏 Room Environment

Panoramic view of the Junior Suite

The room type for this stay was the **Junior Suite** on the 15th floor, located right next to the elevator. The room is a spacious 19-ping (approx. 63 sq. meters) one-bedroom suite with a living room. Upon entering, there's a foyer separating the entrance from the living area. Although the interior decoration feels a bit dated and can't compare with newer hotels from recent years, the cleanliness and overall maintenance are excellent.

The foyer upon entering

View from the entrance

Capsule coffee and basic tea bags, essentials for a 5-star hotel

The fridge is well-stocked with drinks and beer

Welcome fruit on the table

There is a TV in both the living room and the bedroom, as well as large windows. Our side faced Linsen Park, though the view of downtown Taipei isn't particularly spectacular.

The bed in the bedroom is very large (likely two beds joined together) with moderate firmness. It was quite comfortable to sleep in during both stays. Soundproofing is also good; both stays were on weekends (one Saturday night, one Sunday night), and we didn't hear any noise from other rooms or the corridor at night.


USB charging ports on both sides of the bed

Another angle of the room

The bathroom area is also very large, featuring a shower, a bathtub, and a dressing area. The dressing area has a wardrobe and a safe, but it's not separated from the bathroom by any door; it's all one open space.

Spacious bathroom area

Bathrobes, slippers, and safe provided

Like other hotels in the Silks group, Wellspring amenities are used

Huge vanity counter

Single-person bathtub & bidet toilet

🏢 Hotel Facilities

The facilities available to general guests at Regent Taipei are mainly the gym, the heated rooftop pool, and the kids' playroom on the 5th floor. Other facilities like the Wellspring SPA and Sky Studio require additional fees.

Gym, photo from official website: https://www.regenttaiwan.com/wellness

Health Club
Opening Hours: 6:30 AM – 10:30 PM
Sauna Opening Hours: 7:00 AM – 10:30 PM (Last entry: 10:00 PM)


Heading to the rooftop heated pool



The rooftop heated pool hosts open-air movie screenings at night. It's great to come here when the weather is nice.

Rooftop Heated Swimming Pool

Opening Hours: 6:30 AM – 10:00 PM


🍽 Breakfast


Breakfast is served at **Brasserie**, a buffet restaurant. Due to the pandemic, seating was split into three time slots: 7:00, 8:00, and 9:00. Brasserie is a famous buffet in Taipei and was once the only buffet breakfast in Taipei recommended by CNN. The breakfast is lavish with a wide variety of dishes, and the taste is excellent. For a hotel breakfast, there's really nothing to complain about.


High-ceilinged dining space

Room card from our Christmas stay

I always thought I wouldn't have many chances to stay at Regent Taipei (since I live nearby...), but after actually staying here, the experience was genuinely good. It lives up to its reputation as a classic hotel that has stood the test of time. Plus, being located in the Zhongshan shopping district means plenty of shopping, sightseeing, and food options nearby—location is definitely one of its advantages. Having stayed at several hotels under the Silks Hotel Group so far, the experiences have been consistently good. It's an accommodation worth recommending and revisiting.

  • Silks Place Tainan
  • Silks Place Taroko

View from the window at 6 AM

title.$t: 花蓮景點 | 太魯閣國家公園景點 Taroko | 清水斷崖 | 太魯閣牌樓 | 長春祠 | 山月吊橋 | 九曲洞 | 天祥遊憩區

content.$t:
東西橫貫公路起點(太魯閣牌樓)

擁有壯麗自然景色的太魯閣，一直都是來花蓮遊玩代表性的景點，也絕對是必訪景點之一。這次由於已經計畫要入住太魯閣晶英酒店，且要從台北開車下來，那當然要趁這機會走一下太魯閣國家公園的景點囉！

太魯閣國家公園是台灣成立的第四座國家公園，它的範圍其實蠻廣的，並不是只包含從中部橫貫公路進去這段而已，東到東部海岸的清水斷崖，其實也在太魯閣國家公園的範圍之內喔。

P.S. 有興趣的話實際範圍可以看官方的地圖：太魯閣國家公園遊憩簡圖


太魯閣沿線景點

🏞  清水斷崖


清水斷崖是位於秀林鄉清水山東側的海岸斷崖，綿延21公里，其陡峭幾乎垂直的海岸自然景觀，是因為板塊作用與強烈的海蝕作用而形成的，也是目前台灣八景之一。

🚘  交通/停車資訊

在進入東部橫貫公路之前，如果是南下下來，在蘇花公路上會經過可以看到清水斷崖的兩個休息站 - 「匯德休憩區」與「崇德休憩區」，看到的景色不會相差太多，可以考慮一下優缺點決定要停哪個點。

匯德休憩區
優點：停車位置較多，比較好停車
缺點：可以停遊覽車，因此團客可能會比較多，到海岸的路比較長

崇德休憩區
優點：遊客人數會少一點，停好車就到觀景台
缺點：停車位置少，南下方向無法跨越雙黃線到停車空間

🏞  太魯閣牌樓

東西橫貫公路起點(太魯閣牌樓)
太魯閣牌樓是台灣中橫公路的入口牌樓，由於牌樓位於路中間，如果假日期間這裡的車流量也不小，拍照還是停在旁邊從旁邊拍就好，不然跨越馬路到中間應該是蠻危險的。

🚘  交通/停車資訊



🏞  長春祠

矗立在立霧溪谷峭崖邊階的長春祠

到了長春祠停車空間的時候，遠遠就可以看到與瀑布一起在山壁上的長春祠，矗立在立霧溪谷峭崖邊階的長春祠，是為了紀念開闢中橫公路殉職人員所建立的祠堂，祠內供奉著中橫公路興建工程殉職的225位築路人靈位。

🚘  交通/停車資訊


往長春祠的路要在出中橫公路長春隧道口時就要左轉，這裡如果一不注意就會直接過頭，而且是在隧道內，開車往天祥方向要到長春祠這段要小心一點。

導航定位地址：長春祠停車場

轉進來沒多就，就可以看到一塊空地，這裡就是長春祠停車場，位置還算蠻多的，旁邊也有廁所可以使用。

停車場旁的廁所，往下走一層樓


從停車場往長春祠還要走一小段路，這段路地層不穩定，好像常常會容易發生坍方，建議避免在雨天或是大雨過後前往。

穿過這顯眼的紅色長春橋，可以看到有一個往下的階梯，這裡下去才會是往長春祠的入口。而這入口處之外，有一個舊的長春橋，因為洪水沖斷後，原址留在這裡變成一個平台，也是變成一個旅遊秘境(?)，蠻多人會特別來拍這個斷橋的景。



長春橋舊橋


要往長春祠方向，從這個長春祠步道進去步行5~10分鐘就可以抵達長春祠了，一路上就是這種高度不高的平緩道路。



🏞  山月吊橋


山月吊橋是位於布洛灣遊憩區內的一座景觀人行吊橋，它是太魯閣國家公園跨距最長、距離溪谷落差最大的吊橋，橫跨立霧溪太魯閣峽谷，在這裡可以從高點看太魯閣壯麗的峽谷景色。

不過由於有人數限制，這個吊橋每天有固定開放時段，且每個時段有固定可以上橋的人數，想要來山月吊橋，一定要事先預約。(14天前開放預約)

預約山月吊橋：https://www.taroko.gov.tw/ShanyueApplication.aspx?n=13934&sms=12352

🚘  交通/停車資訊

導航定位地址：布洛灣遊憩區

布洛灣遊憩區有很大的停車空間，所以不太需要擔心停車的問題，到了布洛灣遊憩區走到最裡面，就是山月吊橋的入口囉！




過橋後可以到景觀平台上看吊橋的全貌

🏞  九曲洞


九曲洞步道原是中橫公路舊道，民國85年九曲洞隧道通車後，公路舊道改為步道。九曲洞也被稱作是太魯閣峽谷最精華的路段之一，步道全長700公尺，需原路折返，可以在這段路上看到太魯閣峽谷鬼斧神工與險峻的地勢。

🚘  交通/停車資訊

九曲洞完全不能停車，必須靠公車接駁。

由於我們住在天祥的大魯閣晶英酒店，所以還可以把車停回飯店，在直接搭公車往返前往(單趟 $25)，不過當天我們是假日，抵達天祥的時候看到天祥停車場已經全滿，所以假日開車來要前往九曲洞，可能要規劃一下停車位置與公車接駁，這段大概是整段最麻煩的地方 😅。

離九曲洞最近的停車空間是合流，但中間也是有兩公里的距離，基本上如果要用走的，在蘇花公路上應該是蠻危險...


九曲洞隧道口(車子只能暫停下客)

入口處有廁所

九曲洞步道

終點的一個石碑

一路上可以欣賞太魯閣峽谷的壯麗景色

🏞  天祥遊憩區


天祥遊憩區這裡除了有停車場外，有一些餐廳、飲食還有 7-11，如果有要繼續往太魯閣深處遊玩的話，這裡可以是一個中間休息點。

這裡還有太魯閣晶英酒店，如果想體驗在峽谷中住上一晚，可以考慮來入住：

花蓮住宿 | 太魯閣晶英酒店 Silks Place Taroko | 峽谷客房 | 在房內欣賞壯麗峽谷景觀

往上走一點點會到文天祥公園




太魯閣沿線其實有蠻多步道的，像是砂卡礑步道、小錐麓步道等等，這次只有利用入住的前後兩天遊玩，其實時間蠻不夠的，也因為連假遊客比較多，放棄了不好停車的燕子口步道，且遇到連日豪雨結束，本來想去的水簾洞與綠水步道也因此封閉，比較可惜一點。不過太魯閣的景色真的很美，常值得一訪。

title.$t: Hualien Attractions | Taroko National Park | Qingshui Cliff | Taroko Archway | Eternal Spring Shrine | Shakadang... Shanyue Suspension Bridge | Tunnel of Nine Turns | Tianxiang Recreation Area

content.$t:
Starting point of the Central Cross-Island Highway (Taroko Archway)

With its magnificent natural scenery, Taroko has always been the signature destination for a trip to Hualien, and it is absolutely one of the must-visit spots. Since we had already planned to stay at Silks Place Taroko and were driving down from Taipei, of course we had to take the chance to tour the attractions of Taroko National Park!

Taroko National Park was the fourth national park established in Taiwan. Its boundaries are actually quite extensive — it doesn't only cover the section you enter from the Central Cross-Island Highway. To the east, Qingshui Cliff on the east coast also lies within the range of Taroko National Park.

P.S. If you're interested, you can check the official map for the actual boundaries: Taroko National Park Recreation Map


Attractions along the Taroko route

🏞  Qingshui Cliff


Qingshui Cliff is a coastal cliff on the eastern side of Mount Qingshui in Xiulin Township, stretching for 21 kilometers. Its steep, almost vertical coastal landscape was formed by tectonic activity and intense marine erosion, and it is one of Taiwan's Eight Scenic Wonders.

🚘  Transport / Parking Info

Before entering the Cross-Island Highway, if you're heading south you'll pass two rest areas on the Suhua Highway where you can view Qingshui Cliff - "Huide Rest Area" and "Chongde Rest Area." The views from the two aren't very different, so you can weigh the pros and cons to decide which one to stop at.

Huide Rest Area
Pros: More parking spaces, easier to park
Cons: Tour buses can park here, so there may be more tour groups; the walk down to the coast is longer

Chongde Rest Area
Pros: Fewer visitors; the viewing platform is right by the parking spot
Cons: Few parking spaces, and heading southbound you can't cross the double yellow lines to reach the parking area

🏞  Taroko Archway

Starting point of the Central Cross-Island Highway (Taroko Archway)
The Taroko Archway is the entrance gate to Taiwan's Central Cross-Island Highway. Since the archway sits in the middle of the road and traffic here can be heavy on weekends, it's best to park at the side and take photos from there — crossing the road to the middle would be quite dangerous.

🚘  Transport / Parking Info



🏞  Eternal Spring Shrine

The Eternal Spring Shrine standing on a cliff ledge above the Liwu River valley

As soon as you reach the Eternal Spring Shrine parking area, you can see the shrine in the distance set on the cliff face alongside a waterfall. Standing on a cliff ledge above the Liwu River valley, the shrine was built to commemorate the workers who died building the Central Cross-Island Highway, and it enshrines the spirit tablets of the 225 road builders who lost their lives during construction.

🚘  Transport / Parking Info


The road to the Eternal Spring Shrine requires a left turn right as you exit the Changchun Tunnel on the Central Cross-Island Highway. If you're not paying attention you'll drive straight past it, and since it's inside a tunnel, you need to be extra careful on this stretch when driving toward Tianxiang.

Navigation address: Eternal Spring Shrine Parking Lot

Shortly after turning in, you'll see an open area — this is the Eternal Spring Shrine parking lot. There are quite a few spaces, and there are restrooms available nearby.

The restrooms next to the parking lot, one level down


From the parking lot you still have a short walk to the shrine. The ground along this stretch is unstable and landslides seem to occur fairly often, so it's best to avoid going on rainy days or right after heavy rain.

After crossing the eye-catching red Changchun Bridge, you'll see a staircase leading down — going down here is the entrance to the Eternal Spring Shrine. Just outside this entrance there's the old Changchun Bridge; after it was washed away by a flood, the original site was left as a platform and has become something of a hidden gem (?), with quite a few people coming specially to photograph the broken bridge.



The old Changchun Bridge


To head toward the Eternal Spring Shrine, enter via the Eternal Spring Shrine Trail; it's about a 5–10 minute walk to reach the shrine, and the whole way is this kind of gentle, fairly level path.



🏞  Shanyue Suspension Bridge


The Shanyue Suspension Bridge is a scenic pedestrian suspension bridge within the Buluowan Recreation Area. It has the longest span and the greatest height above the valley floor of any bridge in Taroko National Park, crossing Taroko Gorge over the Liwu River. From here you can take in the magnificent gorge scenery from above.

However, because visitor numbers are limited, the bridge only opens during fixed time slots each day, with a set number of people allowed on the bridge per slot. If you want to visit the Shanyue Suspension Bridge, you must book in advance. (Reservations open 14 days ahead.)

Book the Shanyue Suspension Bridge: https://www.taroko.gov.tw/ShanyueApplication.aspx?n=13934&sms=12352

🚘  Transport / Parking Info

Navigation address: Buluowan Recreation Area

The Buluowan Recreation Area has a large parking area, so you don't need to worry much about parking. Once at Buluowan, walk all the way to the far end and you'll find the entrance to the Shanyue Suspension Bridge!




After crossing the bridge you can reach a viewing platform to see the bridge in full

🏞  Tunnel of Nine Turns


The Tunnel of Nine Turns Trail was originally part of the old Central Cross-Island Highway; after the Jiuqudong Tunnel opened to traffic in 1996, the old road was converted into a trail. The Tunnel of Nine Turns is regarded as one of the most spectacular sections of Taroko Gorge. The trail is 700 meters long and you have to return the same way, and along it you can see the marvelously sculpted, precipitous terrain of Taroko Gorge.

🚘  Transport / Parking Info

There is absolutely no parking at the Tunnel of Nine Turns; you must take the shuttle bus.

Since we were staying at Silks Place Taroko in Tianxiang, we could park the car back at the hotel and take the bus there and back (NT$25 one way). However, we visited on a weekend, and when we arrived at Tianxiang the parking lot was already completely full. So if you drive here on a weekend and want to visit the Tunnel of Nine Turns, you may need to plan out your parking and bus connections — this is probably the most troublesome part of the whole route 😅.

The nearest parking area to the Tunnel of Nine Turns is Heliu, but that's still two kilometers away. Basically, walking along the Suhua Highway would be quite dangerous...


The Jiuqudong tunnel entrance (cars may only stop briefly to drop off passengers)

There are restrooms at the entrance

The Tunnel of Nine Turns Trail

A stone monument at the end of the trail

You can enjoy the magnificent scenery of Taroko Gorge all along the way

🏞  Tianxiang Recreation Area


Besides a parking lot, the Tianxiang Recreation Area has several restaurants, food stalls and a 7-11. If you plan to continue deeper into Taroko, this makes a good midway rest stop.

Silks Place Taroko is also here, so if you'd like to experience a night in the gorge, consider staying:

Hualien Accommodation | Silks Place Taroko | Gorge Room | Enjoy Magnificent Gorge Views from Your Room

Walk up a little further and you'll reach Wen Tianxiang Park




There are actually quite a few trails along the Taroko route, such as the Shakadang Trail and the Xiaozhuilu Trail. This time we only had the days before and after our stay to explore, which really wasn't enough time. Because there were more tourists over the long weekend, we gave up on the Swallow Grotto Trail where parking is difficult, and after days of torrential rain the Water Curtain Cave and Lushui Trail that we had wanted to visit were closed — a bit of a shame. Still, the scenery in Taroko is truly beautiful and well worth a visit.

title.$t: 花蓮住宿 | 福康大飯店 Full Kind Hotel | 近東大門夜市 | 花蓮平價住宿

content.$t:
福康大飯店是在 2018 年開幕的飯店，地理位置離市區的一些景點都蠻近的，算是很不錯的地理位置，步行約七分鐘到東大門夜市、步行三分鐘到公正包子，到文化創意產業園區也只要10分鐘的步行路程，可以不需要交通工具就可以抵達幾個有名的點。

一開始在查的時候，其實有發現網路上沒幾篇介紹福康大飯店的文章，不過看了一下網路上的負評沒有什麼太嚴重的問題，以連假時段的價格與地點來說算是蠻划算，再加上也有自己的室內停車場，最後就選擇入住這間飯店。

📜  資訊

  • 入住日期：2022-02-27
  • 入住房型：標準雙床房
  • 入住價格：$3,630 (含早餐)
  • 付款方式：可刷卡，可使用國旅卷
  • 飯店地址：970花蓮縣花蓮市公園路5號
  • 聯絡電話：038337988
  • 訂房網站：https://www.booking.com/hotel/tw/hua-lian-fu-kang-fan-dian-hua-lian-xian1.xt.html?aid=8003516

📍 地點位置

福康大飯店位於花蓮市的公園路上，飯店大門旁邊就是地下停車場的出入口，地下兩層的停車位並不是太多，而且空間蠻小的，會車要很小心。

如果車位滿了，櫃檯會引導到對面的特約停車場，單次的費用也是由飯店這裡會支付，所以車位不會是太大的問題。

🏢  飯店環境

挑高明亮的大廳

福康大飯店比較偏向簡單的商務旅館的感覺，沒有太多的設施與華麗的裝潢，一進門會有一大片的書架與挑高的大廳，整體門面的感覺給人第一印象還不錯。

櫃檯人員的處理入住速度也蠻快速的，沒遇到什麼特殊情況，相對的可能接待服務也沒有特好與特壞，所以也沒特別留下什麼很深的印象 😂

大廳的沙發休息區

迎賓飲品

接待櫃檯區

不過我自己覺得比較有亮點的，反而是房間樓層電梯一打開的時候，整個走廊的空間感很夠，加上還算蠻新的，整體明亮又寬敞，不會像一般商務飯店的走廊那麼擁擠，但反而導致有很多小孩在這走廊奔跑玩耍....


🛏  房間環境


這次入住的是標準的雙床間，床的軟硬適中，是蠻好睡的床，而房內基本的備品與設備都有，像是書桌、電視等等，沒有太多華麗的設施，屬於簡樸乾淨的風格。

靠窗的書桌辦公區

基本的備品

浴室區

浴室的部分是乾濕分離，直接洗手台是在外面的那種乾濕分離，這設計就有點微妙了，如果水開太大或是在洗手台這裡洗臉，有很高機率水會噴到你的床上...  好不好用就見仁見智了。



🍽  早餐


早餐的部分就真的普通，有部分中式與部分西式，種類不多，口味也真的是普通，就是吃飽讓接下來行程不會挨餓的程度這樣。

早餐部分 (罐裝飲料的果汁與真心不好吃的滷肉飯)


吃早餐的環境



沒照太多照片，用花蓮米老鼠來結尾

整體住起來舒適度還可以，如果晚上要去夜市逛逛的話，這地點是真的蠻理想的，可以車停好就走路去附近逛逛。

不過房間與走房隔音蠻差的，入住隔天早上有小孩在外面走廊奔跑玩耍，且外面的人經過講話聲都一清二楚，如果對於聲音敏感的，可能要考慮一下。

title.$t: Hualien Accommodation | Full Kind Hotel | Near Dongdamen Night Market | Affordable Hualien Stay

content.$t:
Full Kind Hotel opened in 2018, and its location is quite close to several attractions in the city center — a really convenient spot. It's about a seven-minute walk to Dongdamen Night Market, three minutes to Gongzheng Baozi, and only a 10-minute walk to the Hualien Cultural and Creative Industries Park, so you can reach several famous spots without needing any transportation.

When I first started researching, I found that there were hardly any articles online introducing Full Kind Hotel. However, after looking through the negative reviews online, there didn't seem to be any serious issues. Considering the price and location during a long holiday period, it was quite good value, and it also has its own indoor parking lot, so in the end I chose to stay here.

📜  Information

  • Stay date: 2022-02-27
  • Room type: Standard Twin Room
  • Price: $3,630 (breakfast included)
  • Payment: Credit cards accepted, Domestic Travel Vouchers accepted
  • Address: No. 5, Gongyuan Rd., Hualien City, Hualien County 970
  • Phone: 038337988
  • Booking site: https://www.booking.com/hotel/tw/hua-lian-fu-kang-fan-dian-hua-lian-xian1.xt.html?aid=8003516

📍 Location

Full Kind Hotel is located on Gongyuan Road in Hualien City. Right next to the hotel entrance is the entrance to the underground parking garage. There aren't many parking spaces across the two basement levels, and the space is quite tight, so you need to be careful when passing other cars.

If the parking is full, the front desk will direct you to a partner parking lot across the street, and the one-time fee is covered by the hotel, so parking isn't much of a problem.

🏢  Hotel Environment

The bright, high-ceilinged lobby

Full Kind Hotel feels more like a simple business hotel, without many facilities or fancy decor. As you walk in there's a large bookshelf and a high-ceilinged lobby, and the overall entrance makes a pretty good first impression.

The front desk staff handled check-in quite quickly, and nothing unusual happened. On the flip side, the service wasn't especially good or especially bad either, so it didn't leave a particularly deep impression 😂

The lobby sofa lounge area

Welcome drinks

The reception desk area

What I personally found more of a highlight, though, was the moment the elevator doors opened on the guest room floors — the corridor felt really spacious, and being fairly new, it was bright and roomy overall, not cramped like the hallways of typical business hotels. The downside is that it also led to lots of kids running around and playing in the corridor....


🛏  The Room


This time we stayed in a standard twin room. The beds were just the right firmness and quite comfortable to sleep on, and the room had all the basic amenities and equipment, such as a desk and a TV. There were no fancy extras — it's a simple, clean style.

The desk and work area by the window

Basic toiletries and amenities

The bathroom area

The bathroom has a wet/dry separation design, but the type where the sink is placed outside the bathroom. This design is a bit odd — if you turn the water on too strongly or wash your face at the sink, there's a high chance water will splash onto your bed...  Whether it's practical is a matter of personal opinion.



🍽  Breakfast


The breakfast was honestly just average, with some Chinese and some Western options. There wasn't much variety and the taste was truly ordinary — just enough to fill you up so you won't go hungry during the day's itinerary.

Part of the breakfast (canned juice and some genuinely not-tasty braised pork rice)


The breakfast dining area



I didn't take many photos, so let's end with the Hualien Mickey Mouse

Overall the stay was reasonably comfortable, and if you plan to wander around the night market in the evening, the location is really ideal — you can park the car and just walk to the nearby spots.

However, the soundproofing between the rooms and the corridor is quite poor. The next morning there were kids running and playing in the hallway outside, and you could clearly hear people talking as they walked past. If you're sensitive to noise, you may want to think twice.

title.$t: 花蓮住宿 | 太魯閣晶英酒店 Silks Place Taroko | 峽谷客房 | 在房內欣賞壯麗峽谷景觀

content.$t:
位於花蓮太魯閣國家公園境內的「太魯閣晶英酒店」，是全台唯一座落在山嶽型國家公園內的五星級酒店，其位於天祥地區緊鄰峽谷、被群山圍繞，不但可以在客房內就可以欣賞壯麗峽谷美景，也有許多設施與活動，是來到花蓮相當有名的高級酒店之一。

太魯閣晶英酒店最早前身為天祥招待所，1991年改建為天祥晶華度假酒店，2009年又再從天祥晶華度假酒店改裝，並且改名為太魯閣晶英酒店。

這次是第二次入住晶英系列的酒店，上一次入住台南晶英的體驗也不錯，趁著這次來花蓮，選擇入住太魯閣晶英酒店並選擇了一泊二食方案，想要享受一下在峽谷中度假的體驗。

📜  資訊

  • 入住日期：2022-02-28
  • 入住房型：休閒客房 - 峽谷河景房(2F)
  • 專案價格：$11,800 (一泊二食)
  • 付款方式：可刷卡，可打統編
  • 飯店地址：97253花蓮縣秀林鄉天 祥 路18號
  • 聯絡電話：038691155
  • 訂房網站：https://www.booking.com/hotel/tw/tai-lu-ge-jing-ying-jiu-dian.xt.html?aid=8003516

📍 地點位置

花蓮太魯閣晶英酒店，地點位於太魯閣國家公園內的天祥地區，從花蓮市區開車過來，如果不塞車順著中橫公路，大約不到一小時就可以抵達天祥地區。

太魯閣晶英酒店正門口

自行開車：

沿著中橫公路抵達天祥地區，太魯閣晶英酒店就位於天祥停車場旁。

飯店地下有停車場，不過停車空間並不是太多，且車道很小，車位的大小也不大，停車的時候要小心停放。飯店外圍也有一些停車區域，如果再沒有位置的話，天祥停車場的停車空間也非常多。

飯店外圍的一些停車空間

大眾運輸：

可以搭乘花蓮客運或是台灣好行抵達天祥站。

時刻表

  • 花蓮客運
  • 台灣好行太魯閣線

飯店接駁：

還有一種選擇是可以使用飯店接駁，太魯閣晶英酒店提供花蓮火車站／機場定時定點接駁服務，每人單趟 $250 元 (12歲以下佔位孩童每人單趟NT$150)，但注意需要入住前三天預約。

可以參考：接駁車時刻表

🏢 飯店環境

寬敞有質感的大廳

太魯閣晶英酒店大約只有四層樓，其實跟我一開始想像的不太一樣(一直以為現在飯店都應該很高😅)。

由於地形的關係，從正門走進來的大廳其實是位於二樓樓層，一進門和台南晶英或是台北晶華的感覺類似，是個寬敞有質感的大廳，且有著淡淡的花香氣味。

電梯間與櫃檯後方的休息區

大廳整體燈光偏暗，但很有氣氛，走廊上也有裝飾不少藝術品或是畫作，整體可以算是一個低調奢華的風格。而飯店的建築是一個環形，圍繞著一樓中庭廣場，總共有 160 間客房，低樓層是休閒客房，高樓層為行館套房，而館內設施分別在不同樓層。


🛏  房間環境

加大的雙人床，軟硬適中且舒適

這次入住的是二樓的峽谷河景一大床房，主打的就是在房間可以直接看到峽谷的壯麗景觀！房間內的大小算寬敞適中，雖然沒有像入住台南晶英時候那麼大的嚇人，但這樣的房間大小其實很舒適了。

進房的時候，電視上一樣有著入住房客姓名的歡迎字樣，自己覺得蠻喜歡的是房間內的蘭花香氣，這在一進房的時候整體體驗蠻舒適驚豔的。

有著入住房客姓名的歡迎字樣

這裡電視也是內建 apple tv 與 chromecast，只要用手機掃描 QRcode 就可以在房間內不論是播放  Spotify 的音樂，還是晚上用 Netflix 追劇都沒有問題喔！

房內可以欣賞峽谷景觀

房內 minibar 隱藏在這個櫃子中

房內設施如同每家高級酒店一樣，有著必備的咖啡機，也和台南晶英一樣附贈了面膜，沙發區的桌子上也有準備迎賓的小點心。

浴室的部分是乾濕分離，空間大小一般，有著單人大小的浴缸與免治馬桶，備品一樣是使用沐蘭系列的備品。


浴缸旁附了一碗浴鹽可以使用


🏢 飯店設施

沐蘭SPA、小澡堂、洗衣室

可能因為太魯閣晶英酒店位於峽谷中，附近休閒娛樂較少，館內提供的服務設施與體驗活動其實算蠻多的。

  • 服務設施：https://taroko.silksplace.com/tw/amenities
  • 館內活動：https://taroko.silksplace.com/tw/activities

娛樂館

位於 B1 休閒樓層的娛樂館，大概可以說是小朋友的天堂了(?) 這裡有很多可以讓小孩或是小小孩玩很久的設施，像是樂高、汽車，甚至還有一整排的迷你商店。當然這裡也還有撞球、桌球台，或是手作教室也在娛樂館這裡。


室內游泳池

一樣位於B1 休閒樓層的還有室內游泳池，空間寬敞的室內泳池，這裡還有石板床可以使用，兒童池中現在還有數量驚人的黃色小鴨在池子裡面 🐤

山水澗/戶外泳池

頂樓戶外泳池

位於 RF 頂樓的戶外泳池，這也是太魯閣晶英的一大賣點，之前在查別人住宿心得的時候，也看到很多網美會來拍這個戶外泳池，面向整片峽谷美景的戶外泳池，天氣好的時候怎麼拍應該都是蠻美的。

夜晚搭配燈光，更加有氣氛

在泳池的另一端，是一區中間有著火爐的露天座位區，這裡也是每晚原住民歌唱表演活動的地點，每晚 20:30 開始會有一小時的原住民歌唱表演活動，吃完晚餐後蠻推薦可以來這裡坐坐，在這大自然的環境中，享受原住民歌唱表演。(假日晚上會變成原住民舞蹈表演)


大家圍著火爐，聆聽歌唱表演

晚上 20:00 ~ 22:00 這段時間，頂樓的池畔酒吧小攤位也會開始營業，可以到這裡與三五好友，點杯調酒或是無酒精飲料，在星空下聊聊天，讓身心靈都放鬆。



酒類與飲料 Menu

說到酒的部分呢，身為常常會到酒吧走跳的人，一般來說都不會特別對飯店附設的酒吧有什麼期待，除了像是台南晶英那種噱頭的36計或是伏魔塔。這次因為飯店之外晚上什麼東西都沒有，大家就約來這裡喝個一杯聊聊天，在星空下小酌一杯還蠻不錯蠻舒適的。

在沒有點經典調酒之下，選了幾杯看起來有趣的特調，意外的都不會太差，甚至到蠻有趣，但口味喜好主觀的體驗就留給大家自己來嘗試看看了。不過由於小攤位只有一個員工在處理調酒，所以當大家同時點的時候，出酒的速度就蠻久的，且材料可能也沒有準備足夠，很多特別想試試看的特調都沒辦法點，這點就蠻可惜的。

太魯閣 Taroko $400

🍽 晚餐 / 早餐

這次我們的方案是包含晚餐的一泊二食，用餐地點都是在衛斯理自助餐廳，晚餐的部分會分流，有著 17:20/19:30 兩梯次可以選擇。

晚餐與早餐的食物口味都不錯，但種類比較少一點，吃完一輪就會不知道要吃什麼了。餐廳的座位數量也比較少，晚餐分流後大概差不多坐滿，但早餐由於沒分流，如果在尖峰時刻，就會區要在門口等一陣子，等到有人吃完才能入坐。




一早起床從房間看出去的景色

太魯閣晶英酒店一直是花蓮蠻熱門搶手，且不太好訂到的飯店之一，我們入住這天感覺應該也是都客滿，而且如果想要在太魯閣國家公園內舒適的住一晚，大概也只有太魯閣晶英這個唯一選擇了。

整體入住的體驗也沒什麼太多可以挑惕的地方，畢竟一個晚上也要破萬元的五星級住宿，不管是服務或是舒適度都算蠻不錯的。如果想要太魯閣國家公園有著蠻舒適的渡假體驗，是還蠻推薦可以來住一次試試看。

title.$t: Hualien Hotel | Silks Place Taroko | Gorge View Room | Enjoy Magnificent Canyon Views from Your Room

content.$t:
Located within Taroko National Park in Hualien, Silks Place Taroko is the only five-star hotel in Taiwan set inside a mountain-type national park. Situated in the Tianxiang area right beside the gorge and surrounded by mountains, it not only lets you take in magnificent canyon scenery from your room, but also offers plenty of facilities and activities — making it one of the most famous luxury hotels to visit in Hualien.

Silks Place Taroko began life as the Tianxiang Guest House. In 1991 it was rebuilt as the Tianxiang Grand Formosa Resort, and in 2009 it was renovated once again and renamed Silks Place Taroko.

This was my second stay at a Silks Place hotel. My previous stay at Silks Place Tainan was also a good experience, so while visiting Hualien this time I chose Silks Place Taroko with a one-night, two-meal package, hoping to enjoy a resort getaway in the gorge.

📜  Information

  • Stay date: 2022-02-28
  • Room type: Leisure Room - Gorge & River View Room (2F)
  • Package price: $11,800 (one night, two meals)
  • Payment: Credit cards accepted, business tax ID invoices available
  • Address: No. 18, Tianxiang Rd., Xiulin Township, Hualien County 97253
  • Phone: 038691155
  • Booking site: https://www.booking.com/hotel/tw/tai-lu-ge-jing-ying-jiu-dian.xt.html?aid=8003516

📍 Location

Silks Place Taroko is located in the Tianxiang area of Taroko National Park. Driving from downtown Hualien along the Central Cross-Island Highway, you can reach Tianxiang in a little under an hour if there's no traffic.

The main entrance of Silks Place Taroko

Driving:

Follow the Central Cross-Island Highway to the Tianxiang area; Silks Place Taroko sits right next to the Tianxiang parking lot.

There is a parking garage beneath the hotel, but there aren't many spaces, the ramp is narrow and the spots are small, so park carefully. There are also some parking areas around the hotel, and if those are full, the Tianxiang parking lot has plenty of space.

Some parking spaces around the hotel

Public transport:

You can take the Hualien Bus or the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle to Tianxiang Station.

Timetables

  • Hualien Bus
  • Taiwan Tourist Shuttle Taroko Route

Hotel shuttle:

Another option is the hotel shuttle. Silks Place Taroko offers a scheduled shuttle service to and from Hualien Train Station / Airport at NT$250 per person each way (NT$150 per way for children under 12 occupying a seat). Note that reservations must be made three days before check-in.

See: shuttle bus timetable

🏢 Hotel Environment

A spacious, tasteful lobby

Silks Place Taroko is only about four storeys tall, which was actually different from what I'd imagined (I always assumed hotels these days were all high-rises 😅).

Because of the terrain, the lobby you walk into from the main entrance is actually on the second floor. Stepping inside feels similar to Silks Place Tainan or Regent Taipei — a spacious, tasteful lobby with a faint floral fragrance in the air.

The elevator lobby and the lounge area behind the front desk

The lobby lighting is on the dim side, but very atmospheric, and the corridors are decorated with plenty of artwork and paintings — overall a understated, luxurious style. The hotel building is ring-shaped, wrapping around the first-floor courtyard, with 160 guest rooms in total: leisure rooms on the lower floors and club suites on the upper floors, with the various facilities spread across different levels.


🛏  The Room

The oversized double bed — comfortable, neither too firm nor too soft

This time we stayed in a Gorge & River View King Room on the second floor. The main selling point is being able to see the magnificent canyon scenery straight from the room! The room size is comfortably moderate — not shockingly large like the one at Silks Place Tainan, but plenty comfortable.

On entering the room, the TV displayed a welcome message with the guest's name, and something I really liked was the orchid fragrance in the room — it made stepping in a comfortable and pleasantly surprising experience.

A welcome message with the guest's name

The TV also has built-in Apple TV and Chromecast — just scan the QR code with your phone and you can stream Spotify music in the room or binge Netflix at night, no problem!

Canyon views right from the room

The in-room minibar is hidden inside this cabinet

In-room amenities are what you'd expect from any luxury hotel: the essential coffee machine, plus complimentary facial masks just like at Silks Place Tainan, and welcome snacks laid out on the table in the sofa area.

The bathroom has separate wet and dry areas and is average in size, with a single-person bathtub and a washlet toilet. The toiletries are from the Wellspring (Mu Lan) series.


A bowl of bath salts is provided beside the tub


🏢 Hotel Facilities

Wellspring Spa, the small bathhouse, and the laundry room

Perhaps because Silks Place Taroko sits deep in the gorge with few entertainment options nearby, the hotel offers quite a lot of in-house facilities and activities.

  • Facilities: https://taroko.silksplace.com/tw/amenities
  • In-house activities: https://taroko.silksplace.com/tw/activities

Entertainment Hall

The Entertainment Hall on the B1 leisure floor could pretty much be called a kids' paradise (?). There are lots of things that can keep children — even toddlers — busy for ages, such as LEGO, toy cars, and even a whole row of mini shops. Of course, there are also pool and ping-pong tables, and the craft classroom is here too.


Indoor Swimming Pool

Also on the B1 leisure floor is the indoor swimming pool — a spacious indoor pool with heated stone loungers available, and right now there's an astonishing number of rubber ducks floating in the children's pool 🐤

Mountain Brook / Outdoor Pool

The rooftop outdoor pool

The outdoor pool on the rooftop (RF) is one of Silks Place Taroko's biggest draws. When I was reading other people's stay reviews beforehand, I saw plenty of influencers coming here to shoot photos at this outdoor pool. Facing an entire sweep of canyon scenery, it must look beautiful from any angle on a clear day.

At night, the lighting makes it even more atmospheric

At the other end of the pool is an open-air seating area with a fire pit in the middle. This is also the venue for the nightly Indigenous singing performance — every evening at 20:30 there's an hour-long Indigenous vocal performance. After dinner I'd definitely recommend coming to sit here and enjoy the singing surrounded by nature. (On weekend evenings it becomes an Indigenous dance performance instead.)


Everyone gathers around the fire pit to listen to the performance

Between 20:00 and 22:00, the little poolside bar stand on the rooftop opens for business. You can come here with a few friends, order a cocktail or a non-alcoholic drink, and chat under the stars — completely relaxing for body and mind.



The drinks and cocktails menu

As for the drinks — as someone who frequents bars, I generally don't have high expectations for hotel bars, apart from gimmicky ones like Silks Place Tainan's "36 Stratagems" or "Demon-Subduing Tower". This time, since there's nothing else to do outside the hotel at night, everyone agreed to come here for a drink and a chat. Sipping a drink under the stars was actually rather nice and relaxing.

Without ordering any classic cocktails, I picked a few interesting-looking signature creations, and surprisingly none of them were bad — some were even quite fun. But taste is subjective, so I'll leave that for you to try yourself. That said, since the little stand only had one staff member making drinks, whenever everyone ordered at once the wait was quite long, and they may not have prepared enough ingredients either — many of the signature drinks I especially wanted to try weren't available, which was a shame.

Taroko $400

🍽 Dinner / Breakfast

Our package included dinner as a one-night, two-meal plan, with both meals served at the Wellesley Buffet Restaurant. Dinner is split into two seatings, 17:20 and 19:30, and you can choose which one.

Both dinner and breakfast tasted good, but the variety was a little limited — after one round you're not sure what else to eat. The restaurant also has relatively few seats; with the split dinner seatings it was roughly full, but since breakfast isn't split, at peak times you have to wait at the door for a while until someone finishes before you can be seated.




The view from the room first thing in the morning

Silks Place Taroko has always been one of Hualien's most popular and hard-to-book hotels. The day we stayed it felt fully booked, and if you want a comfortable night inside Taroko National Park, Silks Place Taroko is pretty much the only choice.

Overall there wasn't much to fault about the stay — after all, it's a five-star hotel costing over NT$10,000 a night, and both the service and the comfort were quite good. If you're after a comfortable resort experience in Taroko National Park, I'd definitely recommend giving it a try.

title.$t: 宜蘭景點 | 東澳粉鳥林秘境 fenniaolin | 愛情鎖海灘 | 台版下龍灣

content.$t:
位在宜蘭東澳的粉鳥林秘境，實際位於「愛情鎖海灘」，一個必須穿越防波堤與消波塊，才能抵達的一個礫石海灘，因爲海灣中有著奇岩怪石，搭配清澈藍海，成為了爆紅的美麗秘境景點。

但因為遊客欠缺公德心，讓海灘充滿了垃圾，在2017年的時候曾經封閉一陣子。不過現在已經是開放的狀態囉！這次從花蓮回程順道經過，來看看一直在網路上有名的粉鳥林秘境。

  • 地址：270宜蘭縣蘇澳鎮漁港右側
  • 營業時間：24hr
  • 停車塲：蘇澳鎮漁港(50元/次)

🚘 交通/停車資訊

大眾運輸

搭乘火車至蘇澳轉運站或東澳火車站，再轉乘國光客運122路公車，即可抵達粉鳥林漁港。

發車時間

  • 08:00 (週一~週日)
  • 09:40 (週一~週日)
  • 11:20 (週一~週日)
  • 13:00 (週一~週日)
  • 14:40 (週一~週日)
  • 16:20 (週一~週日)

國光客運122路公車：http://www.kingbus.com.tw/ticketPriceResult.php?sid=28


自行開車

基本上還是自行開車會比較方便，粉鳥林秘境位於粉鳥林漁港右側，所以只要導航到「粉鳥林漁港」就可以囉！

粉鳥林漁港地址：宜蘭縣蘇澳鎮蘇花路三段東澳灣

在東奧的時候，從萊爾富前面這條路轉進去

沒過多久就會到沿著海邊的路，一路上可以欣賞風景

粉鳥林漁港

粉鳥林漁港停車場已經開始收費囉！到了粉鳥林漁港，會先抵達漁港的停車場，只要直接開進來即可，會有人再去找你收費，以次計費，一次50元。

繳費過後就會在車窗上夾一張繳費證明

🐟 粉鳥林漁港

為什麼叫粉鳥林呢？粉鳥其實是鴿子的意思，以前在這裡是鴿子群聚的天堂，且當地漁民說現在清晨，偶爾也可見上千隻的野鴿成群下來喝溪水與覓食，所以這裡才被稱為粉鳥林。

粉鳥林漁港小小的，很多人在這裡釣魚，這次剛好也遇到漁船回港，直接就現場賣起最新鮮的魚貨，許多當地居民或是遊客就會直接在這裡跟漁民們購買魚貨。

粉鳥林漁港
最新鮮的魚貨

⛰ 粉鳥林秘境

要到粉鳥林秘境(愛情鎖海灘)，只要從粉鳥林漁港前的小路直直走，跨過防波堤與消波塊就可以抵達囉！

直走穿過正前方的防波堤

跨過消波塊後就可以看到這個美景了，但要注意跨過消波塊這段並不是很好走，行動不便或是年長者、小孩可能不是很適合。


補一張天氣好的照片

粉鳥林秘境的礫石海灘其實很小一塊，可想而知假日遊客爆滿在這裡的話應該會很可怕，而且這個秘境的景色很吃天氣的狀況，我們從花蓮一路上來的時候都還晴空萬里，結果到了粉鳥林竟然雲層變很厚，很可惜就沒有看到藍天搭配海水的美景了 🥲。

更新：後來二訪粉鳥林，天氣非常好，拍出來的照片就很美！

title.$t: Yilan Attractions | Fenniaolin Secret Beach, Dong'ao | Love Lock Beach | Taiwan's Ha Long Bay

content.$t:
The Fenniaolin Secret Spot in Dong'ao, Yilan is actually located at "Love Lock Beach" — a pebble beach you can only reach by crossing a breakwater and a pile of wave-dissipating blocks. With its strangely shaped rocks set against a crystal-clear blue sea, it has become a wildly popular hidden gem.

However, because some visitors lacked civic-mindedness and left the beach covered in trash, it was closed for a while back in 2017. Now, though, it's open again! On the way back from Hualien we swung by to see this Fenniaolin secret spot that's been all over the internet.

  • Address: Right side of the fishing harbor, Su'ao Township, Yilan County 270
  • Opening hours: 24hr
  • Parking: Su'ao Township fishing harbor (NT$50 per entry)

🚘 Transport / Parking Info

Public Transport

Take the train to Su'ao Transfer Station or Dong'ao Railway Station, then transfer to Kuo-Kuang Bus route 122 to reach Fenniaolin Fishing Harbor.

Departure times

  • 08:00 (Mon–Sun)
  • 09:40 (Mon–Sun)
  • 11:20 (Mon–Sun)
  • 13:00 (Mon–Sun)
  • 14:40 (Mon–Sun)
  • 16:20 (Mon–Sun)

Kuo-Kuang Bus route 122: http://www.kingbus.com.tw/ticketPriceResult.php?sid=28


Driving Yourself

Driving is basically the more convenient option. The Fenniaolin secret spot sits on the right side of Fenniaolin Fishing Harbor, so just navigate to "Fenniaolin Fishing Harbor" and you're set!

Fenniaolin Fishing Harbor address: Dong'ao Bay, Section 3, Suhua Road, Su'ao Township, Yilan County

In Dong'ao, turn onto the road in front of the Hi-Life convenience store

Before long you'll reach the coastal road, with scenery to enjoy the whole way

Fenniaolin Fishing Harbor

Parking at Fenniaolin Fishing Harbor now charges a fee! When you arrive you'll first come to the harbor parking lot — just drive straight in and someone will come around to collect the fee. It's charged per entry, NT$50 each time.

After paying, a payment slip is clipped onto your car window

🐟 Fenniaolin Fishing Harbor

Why is it called Fenniaolin? "Fenniao" actually means pigeon in Taiwanese. This place used to be a paradise where flocks of pigeons gathered, and local fishermen say that even now, at dawn you can occasionally see thousands of wild pigeons swooping down to drink from the stream and forage — hence the name Fenniaolin ("Pigeon Grove").

Fenniaolin Fishing Harbor is tiny, and lots of people come here to fish. This time we happened to catch fishing boats returning to port and selling their freshest catch right on the spot — plenty of locals and tourists were buying seafood directly from the fishermen.

Fenniaolin Fishing Harbor
The freshest catch

⛰ Fenniaolin Secret Spot

To reach the Fenniaolin secret spot (Love Lock Beach), just walk straight along the small path in front of Fenniaolin Fishing Harbor and climb over the breakwater and the wave-dissipating blocks!

Walk straight through the breakwater right ahead

Once you cross the wave-dissipating blocks you'll see this gorgeous view, but note that this stretch isn't easy going — it may not be suitable for those with limited mobility, the elderly, or small children.


Adding a shot from a day with good weather

The pebble beach at the Fenniaolin secret spot is actually very small, so you can imagine how overwhelming it must be when it's packed with visitors on weekends. The scenery here also depends heavily on the weather — the sky was completely clear all the way up from Hualien, but by the time we got to Fenniaolin the clouds had thickened, so sadly we missed out on that blue-sky-and-blue-sea view 🥲.

Update: We later visited Fenniaolin a second time in beautiful weather, and the photos turned out stunning!

title.$t: 台北酒吧 | Lab | 分子調酒 | 極簡風格與澄清調酒

content.$t:
位於大安區仁愛路上的「Lab」酒吧，各種澄清系列調酒與追求風味的變化，一直都是想去的名單之一，只是都沒有找機會去光臨，這次剛好認識老闆的友人提議，在第一站先來這裡喝一杯，順道來與老闆打個招呼。

  • 酒吧地址：106台北市大安區仁愛路四段409號
  • 營業時間：18:00 - 01:00
  • 消費金額：$350/杯 (無服務費)
  • 官方粉絲頁：https://www.instagram.com/lab_tw/

🏢  店內環境

P.S. 到酒吧拍攝前記得禮貌性問一下能否拍攝喔 (已得到許可)

走進 Lab 的店內，完全可以體驗到什麼是極簡風格，室內的走偏暗的灰色調，除了純白色吧台與後面的一組白色桌椅外，就沒有其他空間了，店內也沒有其他過多的裝飾，讓你專注於體驗調酒的風味上。

入座時的水


🍸 調酒

老闆 Taka 是待過 Washu 與  Room by le kief 的日本人，有去過這兩間店的人就知道，不同於提供大眾般口感，致力在追求調酒的風味，Lab 所想要帶給顧客的也是這種的體驗，至少實際光臨後真正的有感受到。

📃 酒單

酒單的部分是直接掃 QR code 到官方 IG 去看酒單，主要分為三種：

  • Home Cocktail: 可以從字面上看出風味的各種調酒
  • Bar Counter Only: 只有坐在吧台的客人才能選擇
  • Flavor Pairing: 讓顧客自己選擇風味的搭配

詳細更多介紹可以直接看酒單：(如連結失效請直接到 lab 粉絲頁)

https://www.instagram.com/stories/highlights/18003135397372917/

🍸 Beer

以威士忌為底的調酒，不是啤酒卻有著類似啤酒的風味，清爽帶點苦味

🍸 Tapioca Milk Tea


顧名思義，風味就是珍奶，透明的酒體帶有威士忌味道與奶香，搭配很好吃的珍珠。平衡抓得很好，讓不喜歡威士忌的我都覺得十分好喝，可惜的是這杯有一點小杯 🙈

🍸 Yakult Green Tea


這杯是多多綠，喝下去第一口覺得蠻驚艷，充滿養樂多香氣，尾韻也有茶香，蠻有層次也清爽好喝，會不小心一次喝太大口。

🍸 Spice

主題是 Spice，充滿香料卻又不會太突出到不好入口的一杯

🍸 Flower

以花香為主題的一杯，有著明顯的玫瑰風味，對我稍微有一點點偏甜，不過是蠻順口的

🍸 Vegetable

這杯就是重頭戲了，主題是蔬菜類，由於風味特殊，是香菜+香菇，所以在點之前老闆再三確認我們能不能接受這個風味，最後還好有點，實在是太特別XD

聞的時候滿滿香菜味，入口是平衡的酒體，最後喝下去後嘴巴內會留著香菇的風味，這實在是太特別，而且可能不是大眾都可以輕易接受的風味。但如果平常不是只喝酸甜調酒，且不排斥香菜與香菇，蠻推薦試試看這杯，來場味蕾的饗宴。



單杯價格都是 $350 且沒有服務費


這次我們一吃完晚餐就直接過來，整間店也只有我們這組客人，第一次來到 Lab，體驗蠻好的，價格在台北也算蠻合理，如果喜歡追求風味與特色調酒，推薦可以來 Lab 試試看！

title.$t: Taipei Bars | Lab | Molecular Mixology | Minimalist Style and Clarified Cocktails

content.$t:
Located on Ren'ai Road in Taipei's Da'an District, the bar "Lab" — with its range of clarified cocktails and its pursuit of flavor variation — has long been on my must-visit list, though I never quite found the chance to drop by. This time a friend of the owner suggested we start the night here for a drink, and say hello to the owner while we were at it.

  • Address: No. 409, Sec. 4, Ren'ai Rd., Da'an District, Taipei 106
  • Opening hours: 18:00 - 01:00
  • Price: NT$350 per drink (no service charge)
  • Official page: https://www.instagram.com/lab_tw/

🏢  The Space

P.S. Remember to politely ask whether photography is allowed before shooting in a bar (permission granted here)

Step inside Lab and you'll immediately understand what minimalism means. The interior leans toward a dark gray tone, and apart from the pure white bar counter and a set of white table and chairs behind it, there's nothing else — no excessive decoration, so you can focus entirely on experiencing the flavors of the cocktails.

Water served when you sit down


🍸 The Cocktails

Owner Taka is a Japanese bartender who previously worked at Washu and Room by le kief. Anyone who has been to those two bars knows they don't aim for crowd-pleasing flavors but instead pursue flavor in its own right. That's exactly the experience Lab wants to offer its guests — and after actually visiting, I really did feel it.

📃 The Menu

For the menu, you scan a QR code that takes you to their official Instagram. It's divided into three main categories:

  • Home Cocktail: cocktails whose flavors you can tell right from the name
  • Bar Counter Only: only available to guests seated at the bar
  • Flavor Pairing: guests choose their own flavor combinations

For more details you can view the menu directly: (if the link is dead, head straight to Lab's Instagram page)

https://www.instagram.com/stories/highlights/18003135397372917/

🍸 Beer

A whisky-based cocktail — not beer, yet with a beer-like flavor: refreshing with a touch of bitterness.

🍸 Tapioca Milk Tea


As the name suggests, it tastes just like bubble milk tea — a clear liquid carrying whisky notes and a creamy aroma, paired with really tasty tapioca pearls. The balance is spot on; even though I'm not a whisky fan, I found it delicious. The only shame is that the glass was a little small 🙈

🍸 Yakult Green Tea


This one is Yakult green tea. The first sip was quite a surprise — full of Yakult aroma with a tea note on the finish. Layered, refreshing and easy to drink; you might accidentally take too big a gulp.

🍸 Spice

The theme here is spice — full of spice notes, yet never so dominant that it becomes hard to drink.

🍸 Flower

A drink built around floral notes, with a distinct rose flavor. Slightly on the sweet side for me, but very smooth.

🍸 Vegetable

This was the highlight of the night. The theme is vegetables, and because the flavor is so unusual — cilantro plus shiitake mushroom — the owner double- and triple-checked whether we could handle it before taking the order. In the end I'm glad we ordered it; it was just too unique, haha.

On the nose it's packed with cilantro; on the palate the body is balanced; and after you swallow, the shiitake flavor lingers in your mouth. Truly distinctive, and probably not something everyone can easily accept. But if you don't only drink sweet-and-sour cocktails and you don't mind cilantro and mushrooms, I'd definitely recommend giving this one a try — a real feast for the palate.



Every drink is NT$350 with no service charge


This time we came straight over right after dinner, and we were the only group in the whole bar. It was my first visit to Lab and the experience was great — the prices are quite reasonable by Taipei standards. If you enjoy chasing flavor and distinctive cocktails, I recommend giving Lab a try!

title.$t: 台北景點 | 青出於藍染工坊 | 三峽藍染遊客服務中心 | 手做 DIY 藍染體驗

content.$t:
到了三峽，除了逛三峽老街與祖師廟之外，你知道在三峽老街這裡，還有一間可以手作藍染 DIY 的藍染工坊嗎？來到藍染遊客服務中心，這裡不但可以購買許多由手工製作的藍染商品，還可以讓遊客自己 DIY，做出屬於自己獨一無二的藍染物品喔！

  • 地址：新北市三峽區仁愛街47號
  • 營業時間：10:00 - 18:00
  • DIY費用：視商品而定
  • 停車塲：無，可停在附近三峽國小地下停車場
  • 官方粉絲頁：https://www.facebook.com/YangChun.2015/

🚃 交通/停車資訊

三峽老街的藍染公園

藍染遊客服務中心與青出於藍染工坊，位於三峽老街後半段的另一條仁愛街上，旁邊是很小的一個藍染公園，有不少大眾運輸的交通工具都可以抵達三峽老街。

大眾運輸

  • 板橋站搭臺北客運702、705至三峽老街站
  • 新埔站搭首都客運802至三峽老街站
  • 永寧站搭臺北客運706、812至三峽老街站

自行開車

由於附近沒有停車的位置，可以考慮停到距離不遠的三峽國小地下停車場，步行距離約5分鐘。

👕 什麼是藍染

藍染是天然染的一種，起源於三千多年前於先秦時期已有記載，是用植物或礦物天然染料把織物染成藍色的一種印染工藝。在三峽這裡，日治時期有超過21間的藍染坊，後來因為化學染及工業化染整廠的大量生產，才開始讓傳統染布業没落。

藍染的原料是藍草(幾種可以作為藍染原料植物的統稱)，透過氧化的原理，讓本來是深綠色的染液，接觸空氣之後，變化成藍靛色的顏色。

馬蘭(大菁)

🔧 DIY 體驗活動


青出於藍染工坊的 DIY 活動價目表如上，依你製作的物品而不同，如果是一般散客過來是不用預約的喔，直接在營業時間(10:00 - 18:00)入內說你想要做 DIY 就可以了，不過手作以及晾乾都需要時間，建議不要太晚抵達。

手工書製作

這次我們選擇了製作幾本手工書與門簾，選擇完付完款之後，會有工作人員帶你到座位區做簡單的解說，並且讓你挑選你想要做的藍染樣式。

天花板會掛著各種不同圖案可以選擇

接著就是先來做染色前的前置作業了！在做藍染之前，沒想到原來這些圖案都是用綁的綁出來的，對於布料不同的綑綁方式，可以製作出各式各樣不同美麗的圖案，對於這種傳統工藝真心佩服。

不同的花樣，需要不同的綑綁方式

接著就是要實際進入染缸來染布料了，要將我們手上的布染上藍色，需要反覆浸泡染液且不斷地揉捏，這樣才能讓染液有進入布料的深層，並且還要時時翻動布料，讓染料與空氣結合後產生氧化作用，才會從深綠色變成最後的藍靛色。

青出於藍染工坊有兩個染缸可以使用


現場會有手套與工作圍裙

黃綠色才是染液本來的顏色

不同品項所需要的浸泡時間與次數也都不太相同，基本上都需要最少三次，每次3分鐘的浸泡揉捏時間，最後擰乾之後需要風乾一陣子，才方便讓遊客帶回家。


掛在現場風乾

在現場風乾其實也需要一段時間，而且也會視天氣而定。當天因為下雨，我們做完之後，跑去三峽老街逛逛，還吃了午餐回來其實也還沒乾 😅，不過就裝袋帶回家，回家繼續晾乾囉！



你以為，回家晾乾就結束了嗎？



沒有，還有一些後續的步驟要做喔！

回去放三天後，還要浸泡白醋，如果是做手工書，還需要把你的書皮自己組裝起來。

🏞 最終成品

門簾

漸層手工書

以前到三峽老街，由於藍染工坊的位置實在太不起眼，他也不是位於三峽老街主要的街道上，要不是網路上有查到別人分享，很少人會注意到竟然還有個可以手工做 DIY 的地方。

雖然自己覺得價格好像稍微偏高了一點，不過體驗過程是還蠻有趣的，有興趣之後到了三峽老街，除了逛逛老街之外，想體驗點不一樣旅程且沒做過手工藍染的話，可以來三峽藍染遊客服務中心逛逛考慮看看。

  • DIY fee: depends on the item
  • Parking: none on site; you can park at the nearby Sanxia Elementary School underground parking lot
  • Official fan page: https://www.facebook.com/YangChun.2015/

🚃 Transport / Parking Info

The Indigo Dye Park on Sanxia Old Street

The Indigo Dye Visitor Center and the Qing Chu Yu Lan (Blue Dye) Workshop are located on Ren'ai Street, another street running behind the latter half of Sanxia Old Street, right next to a tiny indigo-themed park. Plenty of public transport options can get you to Sanxia Old Street.

Public Transport

  • From Banqiao Station, take Taipei Bus 702 or 705 to Sanxia Old Street stop
  • From Xinpu Station, take Capital Bus 802 to Sanxia Old Street stop
  • From Yongning Station, take Taipei Bus 706 or 812 to Sanxia Old Street stop

Driving

Since there's no parking nearby, consider parking at the Sanxia Elementary School underground parking lot not far away — about a 5-minute walk.

👕 What Is Indigo Dyeing?

Indigo dyeing is a form of natural dyeing, with records dating back over 3,000 years to the pre-Qin period. It's a printing and dyeing craft that uses natural plant or mineral dyes to color fabric blue. Here in Sanxia, there were more than 21 indigo dye houses during the Japanese colonial era; the traditional dyeing industry only began to decline later, with the mass production of chemical dyes and industrial dyeing and finishing plants.

The raw material for indigo dyeing is the indigo plant (a general term for several plants used as indigo dye sources). Through oxidation, the dye liquid — originally dark green — turns an indigo blue once it comes into contact with air.

Assam indigo (strobilanthes)

🔧 The DIY Experience


Above is the price list for DIY activities at the Qing Chu Yu Lan workshop — prices vary by the item you make. Individual walk-in visitors don't need a reservation; just come in during business hours (10:00 - 18:00) and say you'd like to do a DIY session. That said, both the making and the drying take time, so it's best not to arrive too late.

Making a handmade book

This time we chose to make a few handmade books and a door curtain. After choosing and paying, a staff member takes you to the seating area for a brief explanation and lets you pick the indigo pattern you'd like to make.

All kinds of patterns hang from the ceiling for you to choose from

Next comes the prep work before dyeing! Before trying indigo dyeing, I had no idea that all these patterns are created by tying. Different ways of binding the fabric produce all sorts of beautiful patterns — I have genuine admiration for this traditional craft.

Different patterns require different binding techniques

Then it's time to actually get into the dye vat. To dye our fabric blue, you have to dip it in the dye repeatedly and knead it constantly so the dye penetrates deep into the cloth, while also turning the fabric over frequently so the dye reacts with the air and oxidizes — that's how it goes from dark green to the final indigo blue.

The workshop has two dye vats available


Gloves and work aprons are provided on site

Yellow-green is the dye liquid's original color

Different items require different soaking times and numbers of dips. Generally you need at least three rounds of about 3 minutes of soaking and kneading each. After wringing it out, the piece needs to air-dry for a while before visitors can take it home.


Hung up to air-dry on site

Air-drying on site actually takes quite a while, and it depends on the weather too. It was raining that day, so after we finished we went off to wander around Sanxia Old Street and even had lunch — and it still wasn't dry when we came back 😅. But they bagged it up for us to take home and keep drying there!



Think you're done once it dries at home?



Nope — there are still a few follow-up steps!

After leaving it for three days at home, you also need to soak it in white vinegar, and if you made a handmade book, you'll need to assemble the cover yourself.

🏞 The Finished Products

Door curtain

Gradient handmade book

On previous visits to Sanxia Old Street, the indigo workshop was just too inconspicuous — it isn't on the main street of the old town either. If I hadn't found someone's post about it online, hardly anyone would notice there's a place here where you can do hands-on DIY.

Although I personally felt the prices were a touch on the high side, the experience was really fun. If you're interested, next time you're at Sanxia Old Street, besides strolling the old street itself, and if you want something a little different and have never tried handmade indigo dyeing, consider dropping by the Sanxia Indigo Dye Visitor Center.

title.$t: 台北住宿 | 大板根森林溫泉酒店 | 大板根森林遊樂區 | 國寶級低海拔原生亞熱帶雨林

content.$t:
位於新北市三峽區大豹溪流域附近，有一個台灣僅存極其珍貴的國寶級低海拔原生亞熱帶雨林，這裡有許多百年大型國寶級板根植物，豐富的生態也有許多昆蟲與鳥類，位在這個大板根森林遊樂區內。

而在大板根森林遊樂區這裡，有一間可以讓遊客同時體驗溫泉與大自然芬多精的度假村「大板根森林溫泉渡假村」，除了大板根森林遊樂區步道之外，園區內也有一些設施，如烤肉、遊樂場、戶外溫泉與溫泉湯屋，也有咖啡廳，蠻適合旅客來兩天一夜的放鬆小旅行。

📜  資訊

  • 入住日期：2022-01-29
  • 入住房型：秋收冬藏一泊二食住房專案 - 板根套房
  • 專案價格：$9,240
  • 付款方式：可刷卡，可打統編
  • 飯店地址：237新北市三峽區79號
  • 聯絡電話：+886266212000
  • 訂房網站：https://www.booking.com/hotel/tw/greatrootsresort.xt.html?aid=8003516


📍 地點位置

大板根森林溫泉酒店位於離三峽老街，開車大約20分鐘的地方，一路上的山路不會太難開，有幾個地方稍微路小一點，因為還有公車會走這條路，所以會車時要小心一點。

看到這個招牌就到囉！

自行開車：

  • 國道3號三鶯交流道下，沿著臺3線，轉北114，約30分鐘車程

大眾運輸：

  • 捷運府中站搭臺北客運910至三峽老街，轉搭臺北客運807至插角（大板根）站
  • 捷運永寧站搭首都客運916至三峽老街站，轉搭臺北客運807至插角（大板根）站

停車場：

大板根森林溫泉酒店有許多停車場，大部分都是戶外露天的，有好幾個大型停車場
  • 住在度假村區：可以停地下室內停車場
  • 住在太子會館：直接開入園區，停會館附近的戶外停車場
左方車道下去是室內停車場，右方是到大廳入口


住在園區內的太子會館，可以直接開車進入園區


🏢 園區設施


渡假酒店

渡假酒店位於整個園區的入口處，是行人主要的出入口，也是辦理入住與退房的櫃檯所在。如果是開車前來，可以先把車暫停在門口這裡，先去辦理入住，如果是住在園區內的太子會館，再直接開車進去園區內。



大廳的接待櫃檯

森林園區入口

園區範圍不算小，除了大廳所在的渡假酒店之外，入住的區域還有園區後半段的太子會館、板根會館，以及獨棟小木屋式的芬多精客房與景觀客房等等，後半段的客房都必須要從園區內的椰林大道，通過森林區入口才會到。


園區內的椰林大道


園區地圖 (from 官方網站)

森林園區入口處


入口處餵養的貓 (管理員說有15隻)


薰風會館

薰風會館是由日治時代建築改建而成，這裡有著禮品館、茶葉歷史文物館、露天溫泉區，以及部分的客房喔！

茶葉歷史文物館

這裡可以了解以前茶產業在這裡的歷史



禮品館有著各種伴手禮，也可以在這裡買到零食，且這次入住的專案一房有送一個馬克杯+一片面膜，也是要來禮品管兌換。

另外，大板根森林步道有六個可以蓋章的點，如果都蓋完章，也可以到禮品管來免費兌換一張大板根限定的明信片唷！

來森林步道搜集六個章吧！


從薰風會館進入的露天溫泉區


板根便利店

由於大板根園區附近比較沒有什麼東西，園區內的板根便利店，就成為最重要的補給站囉！這裡有賣許多飲料零食或是泡麵，也有賣一些許的酒類，提供住宿旅客如果晚上想吃吃宵夜，可以到這裡來購買。(營業時間到晚上 10 點)



板根巨獸遠古生物展

剛好入住的這段期間，在整個園區內正在展出「板根巨獸遠古生物展」，除了有展出恐龍骨頭之外，在各個角落都會有恐龍之類的模型，而且還會聲控來發聲或是做一些動作。如果有帶小朋友來玩的可能會覺得很有趣，可以跟他們拍拍照，但我覺得在園區內跟自然景觀好像有點違和...? 😅



🏓 遊戲區

在太子會館 B1 還有一區遊戲區，這裡有各種電動電玩、桌球撞球、投籃機，或是兒童遊戲區，部分需要付費，部分入住房客只需登記即可。

https://www.thegreatroots.com/leisure-facility/game/


🛏  房間環境


這次入住的是位於太子會館的兩間房，他的配置都是一張雙人床與一張單人床，如果是三人入住，會加收 $1,800 包含早晚參與森林園區門票的費用。

房內空間大小適中，床的軟硬度舒適，不過設施與備品就普普通通，像電視就看起來比較就而且又小，大概就是個商務旅館的等級，比想像中的還要差一點(好像渡假飯店那棟比較好)，但至少就是乾乾淨淨，沒什麼太大缺點。





🍽 晚餐 / 早餐

早餐統一都會在太子會館餐廳用餐，而這次晚餐選擇了太子會館的西餐廳用餐，假日晚餐是採用 buffet 的型式。由於疫情的關係，入口有一個全身的消毒噴霧，取餐的時候也必須要全程戴口罩與雙手戴手套，服務人員會在一旁巡視提醒沒有戴手套的客人。


早餐就不提了，我覺得很普通沒有什麼驚豔的點，反而是晚餐的菜色還不錯，而且有些平常自助餐少見的菜色，像是自助麻辣燙就蠻有趣的，可以自己選喜歡的料，自己燙熟，有點像是外面店家在煮滷味一樣。

甜點種類也蠻多，而且口味也不錯，另外還有一個可以做花生捲冰淇淋捲餅的也很有趣。比起早餐，反而覺得晚餐蠻有記憶點的，如果有來入住可以考慮在這裡吃他的晚餐。

自助麻辣燙


🌲 森林遊樂區


大板根原始森林區分為三條步道，一環、二環與三環，一環的步道是最好走也距離最短的，如果正常速度行走，一環走一圈只需要半個小時就可以走完了。二環與三環是稍微比較不好走的路，這次來剛好遇到下雨，櫃檯人員也有建議說如果下雨天就不建議行走二環與三環了。

一環大多是平坦的石板路

每天的 09:30 與 14:30 都會有一場一個小時到一個半小時的導覽，導覽員會介紹園區的一些歷史、設施還有植物，然後帶大家走一環繞一圈。這次我們趕在入住前就參加下午場的導覽，如果時間有對上，還蠻推薦可以跟著導覽來走一走，聽一聽介紹。

國寶級大板根

大板根彩虹橋

大板根早期為泰雅族人的居住地，在古老的傳說中，泰雅族人從小就必須與族人互信合作，努力學習各種生活紀律與技能，維護山林尊重祖靈，爭取自生榮譽直到生命盡頭，才能通過彩虹橋，到達祖靈所在之處。

彩虹橋 (神靈橋)



用一張像是拍恐怖片的鯉魚池做結尾

這次剛好有機會來入住，整個園區還算蠻舒適的，但入住太子會館的客房沒有想像中的好，可能也有點年份有點久了，就只能算是中規中矩可接受，只是對上這價格是稍微有點太貴了，整體來說 CP 值有點低。

不過大板根森林遊樂區是不需要入住，可以單買門票進入的，如果想吸收一點森林的芬多精，不妨直接買門票來森林遊樂區吧！

title.$t: Taipei Accommodation | Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort | Great Roots Forest Park | Taiwan's National Treasure Low-Altitude Primeval Subtropical Rainforest

content.$t:
Near the Dabao River basin in Sanxia District, New Taipei City lies one of Taiwan's last remaining and extremely precious national-treasure-class low-altitude primeval subtropical rainforests. Here you'll find many century-old, national-treasure-class buttress-root trees, along with rich ecology including plenty of insects and birds — all located within the Great Roots Forest Park.

Within the Great Roots Forest Park there is a resort where visitors can enjoy both hot springs and the phytoncides of nature — the "Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort." Besides the forest park trails, the grounds also offer facilities such as barbecue areas, a playground, outdoor hot springs and private spa rooms, plus a café — making it a great spot for a relaxing two-day, one-night getaway.

📜  Information

  • Stay date: 2022-01-29
  • Room type: Autumn Harvest & Winter Storage One-Night Two-Meal Package - Great Roots Suite
  • Package price: $9,240
  • Payment: Credit cards accepted; company tax ID invoice available
  • Address: No. 79, Sanxia District, New Taipei City 237
  • Phone: +886266212000
  • Booking site: https://www.booking.com/hotel/tw/greatrootsresort.xt.html?aid=8003516


📍 Location

The Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort is about a 20-minute drive from Sanxia Old Street. The mountain road isn't too difficult to drive, though a few sections are a bit narrow — and since buses also use this road, take extra care when passing oncoming vehicles.

When you see this sign, you've arrived!

By car:

  • Exit National Highway 3 at the Sanying Interchange, follow Provincial Highway 3, then turn onto County Road North 114 — about a 30-minute drive

By public transport:

  • From MRT Fuzhong Station take Taipei Bus 910 to Sanxia Old Street, then transfer to Taipei Bus 807 and get off at Chajiao (Great Roots) stop
  • From MRT Yongning Station take Capital Bus 916 to Sanxia Old Street, then transfer to Taipei Bus 807 and get off at Chajiao (Great Roots) stop

Parking:

The Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort has plenty of parking, mostly open-air, including several large lots
  • Staying in the resort hotel area: you can park in the underground indoor car park
  • Staying at the Prince Hall: drive straight into the grounds and park in the outdoor lot near the hall
The ramp on the left leads down to the indoor car park; the right leads to the lobby entrance


If you're staying at the Prince Hall inside the grounds, you can drive straight in


🏢 Resort Facilities


Resort Hotel

The resort hotel sits at the entrance to the whole complex and serves as the main pedestrian entrance as well as the check-in/check-out counter. If you're driving, you can park briefly out front to check in first, and if you're staying at the Prince Hall inside the grounds, then drive on in.



The lobby reception desk

Forest Park Entrance

The grounds are fairly large. Besides the resort hotel where the lobby is, accommodation also includes the Prince Hall and Great Roots Hall in the rear half of the grounds, as well as standalone cabin-style Phytoncide Rooms and Scenic Rooms. To reach the rooms in the back section, you have to walk down the palm-lined avenue inside the grounds and pass through the forest area entrance.


The palm-lined avenue inside the grounds


Map of the grounds (from the official website)

The forest park entrance


Cats fed at the entrance (the caretaker said there are 15 of them)


Xunfeng Hall

Xunfeng Hall was converted from a Japanese colonial-era building. Here you'll find a gift shop, a tea history museum, an open-air hot spring area, and some guest rooms too!

Tea History Museum

Here you can learn about the history of the tea industry in this area



The gift shop stocks all kinds of souvenirs and snacks. Our package this time included one mug and one face mask per room, which also had to be redeemed at the gift shop.

Also, the Great Roots forest trails have six stamp stations — collect all the stamps and you can redeem a Great Roots exclusive postcard for free at the gift shop!

Head out on the forest trails and collect all six stamps!


The open-air hot spring area accessed from Xunfeng Hall


Great Roots Convenience Store

Since there isn't much around the Great Roots area, the on-site convenience store becomes the most important supply stop! It sells plenty of drinks, snacks and instant noodles, plus a small selection of alcohol — perfect for guests who fancy a late-night snack. (Open until 10 pm)



Great Roots Prehistoric Giant Beasts Exhibition

As it happened, during our stay the whole complex was hosting the "Great Roots Prehistoric Giant Beasts Exhibition." Besides displays of dinosaur bones, there were dinosaur models tucked into every corner, some of which were sound-activated to roar or move. Kids would probably find it great fun and love taking photos with them, but I felt it clashed a bit with the natural scenery of the grounds...? 😅



🏓 Games Area

On B1 of the Prince Hall there's a games area with all sorts of arcade machines and video games, table tennis, billiards, basketball shooting machines and a children's play area. Some cost extra, while some are free for hotel guests upon registration.

https://www.thegreatroots.com/leisure-facility/game/


🛏  The Room


This time we stayed in two rooms at the Prince Hall, each configured with one double bed and one single bed. For three guests there's an extra charge of $1,800, which includes forest park admission for both morning and evening.

The room size was just right and the bed was comfortably firm, but the facilities and amenities were only so-so — the TV, for instance, looked rather old and was small. It felt roughly business-hotel grade, a bit worse than I'd expected (the resort hotel building seems to be better), but at least it was clean with no major drawbacks.





🍽 Dinner / Breakfast

Breakfast is served for everyone at the Prince Hall restaurant, while for dinner this time we chose the Western restaurant at the Prince Hall, which serves a buffet on weekends. Because of the pandemic, there was a full-body disinfectant spray at the entrance, and masks and gloves had to be worn at all times when serving yourself; staff patrolled nearby to remind guests who weren't wearing gloves.


I won't say much about breakfast — I thought it was pretty ordinary with nothing outstanding. Dinner, on the other hand, had a decent spread, including some dishes rarely seen at buffets, like the DIY spicy mala soup station, which was quite fun: you pick your own ingredients and cook them yourself, a bit like braised snacks shops outside.

There was also a good variety of desserts and they tasted good; another fun option was making your own peanut brittle ice cream rolls. Compared to breakfast, dinner was the memorable one — if you stay here, consider having dinner on site.

DIY spicy mala soup station


🌲 Forest Park


The Great Roots primeval forest area is divided into three trails: Loop 1, Loop 2 and Loop 3. Loop 1 is the easiest and shortest — at a normal pace you can complete the whole circuit in just half an hour. Loops 2 and 3 are somewhat tougher going; it happened to rain during our visit, and the front desk staff advised against walking Loops 2 and 3 on rainy days.

Loop 1 is mostly flat stone-paved path

Every day at 09:30 and 14:30 there's a guided tour lasting one to one and a half hours. The guide introduces the history of the grounds, the facilities and the plants, then leads everyone around Loop 1. This time we joined the afternoon tour just before check-in — if the timing works out, I'd recommend following the tour and listening to the commentary.

The national-treasure giant buttress-root tree

The Great Roots Rainbow Bridge

The Great Roots area was once home to the Atayal people. According to ancient legend, from a young age the Atayal had to build mutual trust and cooperation with their kin, diligently learn the disciplines and skills of life, protect the mountains and forests, respect the ancestral spirits, and strive for personal honor until the end of life — only then could they cross the Rainbow Bridge and reach the realm of the ancestral spirits.

Rainbow Bridge (Spirit Bridge)



Ending with a shot of the carp pond that looks straight out of a horror film

It was great to have the chance to stay here — the grounds as a whole are quite pleasant, but the Prince Hall rooms weren't as nice as I'd imagined, likely because they're getting on in years. They're acceptable and by-the-book, but for the price it feels a bit expensive; overall the value for money is a little low.

That said, you don't have to stay overnight to visit the Great Roots Forest Park — you can simply buy an admission ticket. If you want to soak up some forest phytoncides, why not just buy a ticket and visit the forest park!

title.$t: 宜蘭住宿 | 慢學院  Andante School | 南澳包棟民宿 | 體驗寧靜的慢活生活

content.$t:
每次來到宜蘭遊玩，大家都是入住羅東、宜蘭在田野間的民宿嗎？還是習慣入住大型的溫泉飯店呢？這次由於在跨年時段訂房不好訂，且人數比較多的關係，從來沒想過會入住到南端南澳的民宿，本來沒有特別期待，但入住之後的體驗意外的相當不錯。

位於武塔車站附近的慢學院，是由台鐵老宿舍改建而成，主打給旅客一個慢下來的生活體驗。除了正對武塔國小有著大片綠地與操場之外，慢學院也還有許多另外付費的慢活體驗課程，讓入住旅客參加喔！

📜  資訊 

  • 入住日期：2021-12-31 ~ 2022-01-02
  • 入住房型：包棟
  • 入住價格：$1,000/人，入住兩晚
  • 民宿地址：272宜蘭縣南澳鄉新溪路23號
  • 聯絡電話：+88639981858
  • 聯絡方式：https://www.facebook.com/andanteschool99

📍 地點位置

慢學院位於南澳，距離武塔車站約500公尺，如果不是開車前來的住客，也是可以透過搭乘火車的方式到達慢學院。若是開車前來，需要從蘇澳往花蓮方向，走一段不近的路程才會到。

小小的新溪路旁的這棟建築就是「慢學院」

這次我們雖然兩天晚上都住在慢學院，可是行程都在宜蘭、羅東，所以開車來回折返跑了好久次... 而且晚上的蘇花公路，沒有蘇花改的這段實在是很恐怖，完全沒有路燈的一大段山路，能不要晚上開車開這段就盡量避開😅。

🏢 戶外空間

由舊台鐵宿舍改建的慢學院，一共有三棟連在一起的獨立空間，每棟的房型都一模一樣，是兩間雙床房與一間單人房，每間最多都可以入住五人。這次我們一共有15人一起來跨年，剛好就把三棟全部包起來，整個都是我們的空間。

三棟的外面有個小小的走道空間，還有一個類似小院子，這裡有些桌椅可以讓三五好友在這裡聊天喝喝小酒，一起看看夜晚滿天的星星。這次我們來晚上很幸運天氣都不錯，也因為沒有什麼光害，可以看到滿天的星星！

戶外的一個很舒適的空間

🏢 廚房

在房間旁邊停車場的位置，這裡還有一間住客可以使用的廚房，廚房內的器具與餐具、碗盤、杯子都很齊全，也有瓦斯爐與烤箱，比較多人一起來住宿的話，很適合買一點食物在這裡一起煮晚餐。


天冷的時候適合大家一起煮火鍋

🏢 室內空間

溫馨的閱讀區

每一間裡面有兩間雙床房與一間單人房，一進門會有一個小客廳，有個舒服的沙發與一些書籍，還有一個五人座的餐桌，隔天早上民宿老闆會在約定好的時間把早餐放在每一間的餐桌上。另外這裡是沒有電視的喔，不妨拿本書度過個寧靜的夜晚吧！

五人座的餐桌

夜晚時的舒適閱讀空間

衛浴的部分有兩間，一間比較小間的在室內，一間大間的算是在半室外，室內的馬桶還有免治馬桶，並且是使用茶籽堂的備品。

室內的浴室

茶籽堂的備品

衛浴空間超級大的浴室

每一間都還有一個茶水間，這裡有飲水機、快煮壺、冰箱，還有一台脫水機

臥室的部分每一間都長得一樣XD 都是這樣的單人床，只是分雙床或是單床的房間而已。床還滿好睡，軟硬適中，且房間與客廳都有冷暖氣機，我們入住這兩天其實晚上算蠻冷的，房間有暖氣的話，入睡整個就會很舒服。

武塔國小操場一景

武塔國小綠色隧道

由於附近其實沒什麼東西，步行到達的距離基本上沒什麼景點，早上起床不妨到對面的武塔國小散散步吧，運氣好的話可以遇到武塔國小裡面一隻親人的虎斑貓喔！


由於慢學院後方山上緊鄰鐵軌，所以火車經過的時候會有不小的聲音與震動，我們入住兩天的時間，大約12點之後就不會再有火車經過了，早上大約也是 7~8點才有火車經過的聲響，自己在睡眠的時候對聲音比較敏感，不過兩天入住下來並沒有什麼在半夜被吵醒的情況，整體住起來還蠻舒適的。

除了地點真的是遠了點之外，整體入住體驗其實還蠻不錯，是還蠻推薦的，假日時段一間是 $5,000，五個人入住等於一人一千元，這個價位 CP 值其實還蠻不錯，蠻適合找一群朋友一起來入住。不過如果要來入住，行程可以稍微安排一下，不要像我們一樣不斷地折返跑才不會太累。

title.$t: Yilan Accommodation | Andante School | Whole-House B&B in Nan'ao | Experience the Quiet, Slow Life

content.$t:
Whenever you visit Yilan, do you usually stay at a B&B out in the fields around Luodong or Yilan City? Or do you prefer a big hot spring hotel? This time, because rooms were hard to book over the New Year period and we had a fairly large group, we ended up staying at a B&B down south in Nan'ao — something we'd never considered before. We didn't have any particular expectations, but the stay turned out to be surprisingly good.

Located near Wuta Station, Andante School was converted from old Taiwan Railways staff dormitories, and its whole concept is to give travelers a chance to slow down. Besides facing Wuta Elementary School with its large green field and playground, Andante School also offers a variety of paid "slow living" experience classes that guests can join!

📜  Information 

  • Dates of stay: 2021-12-31 ~ 2022-01-02
  • Room type: Whole house
  • Price: $1,000/person for two nights
  • Address: No. 23, Xinxi Rd., Nan'ao Township, Yilan County 272
  • Phone: +88639981858
  • Contact: https://www.facebook.com/andanteschool99

📍 Location

Andante School is in Nan'ao, about 500 meters from Wuta Station, so guests who aren't driving can easily get here by train. If you do drive, you'll need to head from Su'ao toward Hualien, and it's a fairly long stretch of road.

This building along the small Xinxi Road is "Andante School"

Although we stayed at Andante School both nights, our itinerary was all around Yilan and Luodong, so we drove back and forth countless times... And the Suhua Highway at night — the stretch without the Suhua Improvement Project — is genuinely scary: a long section of mountain road with no street lights at all. Avoid driving that stretch at night if you can 😅.

🏢 Outdoor Space

Converted from the old Taiwan Railways dormitories, Andante School consists of three connected but independent units. Each unit has exactly the same layout — two twin rooms and one single room — and can accommodate up to five people. This time there were 15 of us celebrating New Year together, so we booked all three units and had the entire place to ourselves.

Outside the three units there's a small walkway and something like a little courtyard, with tables and chairs where you and your friends can chat over a few drinks and gaze at the star-filled night sky. We were lucky with the weather both nights, and with almost no light pollution here, the sky was full of stars!

A very comfortable outdoor space

🏢 Kitchen

Next to the rooms, by the parking area, there's a kitchen guests can use. It's fully equipped with cookware, utensils, plates, bowls and cups, plus a gas stove and an oven. If you're traveling with a bigger group, it's perfect for picking up some ingredients and cooking dinner together.


Cold weather is perfect for a group hot pot

🏢 Indoor Space

A cozy reading corner

Each unit has two twin rooms and one single room. As you walk in there's a small living room with a comfortable sofa and some books, plus a five-seater dining table. The next morning, the owner sets breakfast out on each unit's dining table at the agreed time. Note that there's no TV here — so why not pick up a book and enjoy a quiet evening?

The five-seater dining table

The cozy reading space at night

There are two bathrooms: a smaller one indoors and a larger, semi-outdoor one. The indoor toilet even has a bidet seat, and the toiletries are from Chatzutang (Tsaotun).

The indoor bathroom

Chatzutang toiletries

The super spacious bathroom

Each unit also has a pantry with a water dispenser, electric kettle, fridge, and even a spin dryer

As for the bedrooms, they all look exactly the same lol — all with single beds like this; the only difference is whether a room has two beds or one. The beds are pretty comfortable, just the right firmness, and both the bedrooms and living room have air conditioning with heating. It was quite cold at night during our two-day stay, so having heat in the room made sleeping really comfortable.

A view of the Wuta Elementary School playground

The green tunnel at Wuta Elementary School

Since there really isn't much around — basically no attractions within walking distance — why not take a morning stroll over to Wuta Elementary School across the street? If you're lucky, you might run into the friendly tabby cat that lives there!


Since the hillside behind Andante School runs right alongside the railway tracks, passing trains do make a fair amount of noise and vibration. During our two-night stay, trains stopped running after around midnight, and in the morning you'd only hear them from about 7–8 a.m. I'm fairly sensitive to noise when I sleep, but over the two nights I was never woken up in the middle of the night — overall it was a pretty comfortable stay.

Apart from being a bit far out, the overall stay was really quite good and I'd recommend it. On weekends a unit costs $5,000, so with five people that's $1,000 each — great value for money, and ideal for a group of friends. Just plan your itinerary a little more carefully than we did, so you don't end up driving back and forth constantly and wearing yourselves out.
