title.$t: Kitakyushu Independent Travel | Shimonoseki City Sights | Getting from Mojiko to Shimonoseki | Karato Market | Japanese-Qing Peace Treaty Memorial Hall | Akama Shrine

content.$t:
Shimonoseki is a city in Yamaguchi Prefecture, Japan. Since ancient times it has flourished as "the gateway to Japan." It is the westernmost city on Honshu, and a place full of culture, history and natural beauty. Its most famous catches are pufferfish and monkfish — for both, Shimonoseki lands the largest hauls in all of Japan.

This is also the historic site where the Treaty of Shimonoseki was signed, so a trip to Mojiko is usually paired with Shimonoseki. After finishing our morning stroll around Mojiko and having lunch, we set off for a walk around Shimonoseki.

First, here's a map showing the relative locations:

Relative locations of Mojiko & Shimonoseki attractions
---

⛴ Getting from Mojiko to Shimonoseki

There are several ways to get from Mojiko to Shimonoseki:

  • Self-drive
  • Train (Sanyo Main Line)
  • Ferry (about 5 min)
  • Walking through the undersea tunnel (about 40 min)

Since the train doesn't drop you off conveniently near the attractions, and the entrance to the undersea tunnel isn't at Mojiko Station, we gave up on walking this time and took the ferry both ways.

Walk from Mojiko Station toward the waterfront and you'll immediately spot the boarding point for the boat to Shimonoseki.


A one-way adult ticket costs 400 yen



Note that boats to Ganryujima also depart from here, so don't buy the wrong ticket or board the wrong boat. Ganryujima is an uninhabited island in the Kanmon Strait

It's famous as the site of the duel between Miyamoto Musashi and Sasaki Kojiro. But from what others who have been there report, apart from a statue of the duel there's nothing much on the island… so we weren't interested enough to make the detour.

Pay attention to the direction of the boat when you board


This is the ferry that runs the connection


The ferry has both indoor and outdoor seating, but since the weather was pretty cold, the ride takes only five minutes, and there isn't much scenery to see anyway, you might as well just sit comfortably inside. Five minutes later, you're in Shimonoseki!

---

⚓ Kamon Wharf

  • Address: 〒750-0005 6-1 Karatocho, Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture
  • Opening hours: 09:00 ~ 22:00


Next to the wharf there's a small shopping complex, mostly restaurants.

---

🐟 Karato Market

  • Address: 〒750-0005 5-50 Karatocho, Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture
  • Opening hours:
    • 05:00 ~ 15:00 (Mon–Sat)
    • 08:00 ~ 15:00 (Sun)
  • Official website: http://www.karatoichiba.com/

Karato Market is a local wholesale market in the Karato district of Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture, and one of the city's best-known tourist attractions. In 1909 the government began permitting roadside vegetable vending here, and in 1933 it merged the vegetable market with the Karato fish market to form the "Shimonoseki Karato Fish and Vegetable Market," the forerunner of today's Karato Market.


Keep walking along the waterfront and you'll soon reach Karato Market. Packed with all kinds of fresh fish and seafood, it's nicknamed the "Kitchen of Kanmon" and "Pufferfish Paradise." You can buy plenty of fresh seafood here, with fishmongers selling their catch directly after unloading.

A huge pufferfish statue greets you at the entrance

Around the outside of the first floor are shops selling dried goods


The second floor has some very reasonably priced seafood restaurants, while the inside of the first floor is an ordinary fish market on weekdays. But the real highlight is the Friday-to-Sunday Ikiiki Bakanmachi food event — the so-called weekend sushi stalls, with many seafood snack booths selling all sorts of sushi and deep-fried seafood.


Sushi stalls



After buying food on the first floor, you can head up to the seating area on the second floor to eat. Since we'd already had lunch, we only bought some fried pufferfish & fried sea urchin to sample. As for which stall is the tastiest, we'll leave that for you to discover for yourselves!


Many people also take their food outside to the waterfront by Karato Market, enjoying their meal while taking in the beautiful views of the Kanmon Strait.


---

 Japanese-Qing Peace Treaty Memorial Hall

  • Address: 〒750-0003 4-3 Amidaijicho, Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture
  • Opening hours: 09:00 ~ 17:00
  • Admission: Free
  • Official website: http://www.shimohaku.jp/page0106.html


We all learned about it in history class as kids: the Qing Empire fought the First Sino-Japanese War against Japan, was defeated, and was forced to sue for peace, signing the Treaty of Shimonoseki, which ceded Taiwan and ended the war. The place where Qing envoy Li Hongzhang and Japanese representative Ito Hirobumi signed the treaty is right here — "Shunpanro."

The "Japanese-Qing Peace Treaty Memorial Hall" next door commemorates this piece of history. The treaty was originally signed on the second floor of Shunpanro, but after the building was rebuilt following an earthquake, all the artifacts were moved to the memorial hall beside it. Today the hall recreates the scene of the negotiations and displays the related documents used by both sides at the time.


This is the very seat Li Hongzhang sat in back then


---

 Akama Shrine

  • Address: 〒750-0003 4-1 Amidaijicho, Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture
  • Opening hours: Daily
  • Official website: http://www.tiki.ne.jp/~akama-jingu/



Akama Shrine, which looks like the mythical undersea Dragon Palace, is one of Shimonoseki's must-visit sights. It stands right next to the Japanese-Qing Peace Treaty Memorial Hall, just a 15-minute walk from the ferry terminal.

Suitenmon Gate


The most distinctive feature is Akama Shrine's Suitenmon Gate, which looks just like the Dragon Palace from Japanese folklore — and there's a historical story behind it.

Akama Shrine was built to enshrine the young Emperor Antoku. During the great civil war between the Taira and Minamoto clans, Emperor Antoku was carried into the sea by two nuns who drowned themselves with him. It is said that the Dragon Palace-like Suitenmon Gate exists because, before he entered the water, his grandmother told him that "there is a capital beneath the waves too." Another version says the two nuns chanted a poem meaning "there is a palace in the depths of the sea as well." Later generations therefore designed the shrine to resemble the Dragon Palace, symbolizing the divine spirit enshrined beneath the sea.

Beside the main hall there is also a stone monument enshrining the Yata no Kagami, one of the Three Sacred Treasures. Legend has it that Emperor Antoku took all three treasures with him into the sea; afterwards the Minamoto clan recovered only the Yasakani no Magatama and the Yata no Kagami, while the Kusanagi sword was never found — and the Yata no Kagami is said to be enshrined here.


As at any shrine, you can tie up unlucky fortune slips here


Take this little path and you'll reach the Hall of Hoichi the Earless and the Nanamoritsuka, which enshrines the Taira clan. If you're interested in the ghost story of Hoichi the Earless, you can read about it on Wikipedia: Further reading: The tale of Hoichi the Earless



---

After finishing at Akama Shrine, we strolled slowly back to the ferry terminal. Keep an eye out along the way — pufferfish motifs are everywhere! Back in Mojiko, we checked the JR timetable and headed off to our next destination: Fukuoka!

title.$t: 北九州自由行 | 門司港市區景點篇 | 小倉往門司港交通 | 門司港懷舊區 | 海峽廣場

content.$t:
門司區是個面向瀨戶內海的港口地區，門司港曾經是日本三大港之一，是相當重要的國際貿易據點。門司港的「聯絡船」更是連結九州與本州的重要交通，在當時聚集了眾多西洋商行、洋樓、銀行等等。這天我們的行程，計畫從小倉出發，要去司門港&下關走走，結束後晚上直接回到福岡的住宿地點。

 小倉到門司港交通

延伸閱讀：北九州自由行 | 小倉市區住宿篇 | ARK BLUE HOTEL 藍色方舟飯店 (已改名 ホテルリリーフ小倉ANNEX)

這天我們早上就從小倉旅館離開，拖著行李往門司港出發，預計在門司港玩完之後，直接就從門司港搭車回去福岡。交通上其實很容易，有點像我們在台灣搭乘區間車的感覺，這段鐵路是鹿兒島本線的最後一段，在 google map 上查好時間跟月台，使用 北九州 JRPass，直接到月台上車就好囉！

現在使用 google map 都可以很清楚的查到時刻與月台了



列車就像區間車一樣，也不用劃位，車上人也很少，到處都是空位。列車會沿著海岸一路往北走，中間經過三站，很快的15分鐘過後就會到門司港車站囉！


---

 門司港車站


1891年4月1日 九州鐵道的門司站啟用，這是門司港車站的前身，現在的這棟是於1914年由原來的門司站，向東邊200m移動，1942年才改名為門司港車站。車站的外觀、內裝都重現了大正時期的設計，為九州最古老的火車站，整個車站是木製的風格，很有懷舊的風味。



---

💼 門司港車站寄物處


如果和我們一樣拖著大行李箱的人，門司港車站也有寄物處可以使用，就在出剪票口的左手邊，沿著 google map 街景圖，走到後面就可以看到有小小一區的置物櫃。數量不多，但是寄物的人也不多。(我們抵達這天日週日上午)


公告上可以清楚看到價格，都是以一天來計算

  • 小型：¥ 400
  • 中型：¥ 600
  • 大型：¥ 700
  • 特大：¥ 900
實測大概 26~28 吋的行李箱，需要放入“大型”才裝得下

---

🏫  門司港懷舊區（門司港レトロエリア）

門司港以懷舊區聞名，這裡保留了許多明治、大正時期保留下來的建築物，並且以門司港車站附近地區。許多興建於20世紀初的西式建築為中心，此區域的旅館、商業設施亦隨之配合以該時期懷舊風格為主題，充滿大正浪漫的情懷，由門司港車站為出發點，一路往海峽廣場，可以看到許多大正時期保留下來的建築物。從車站一出來，就會看到許多人力車


⛴   藍翼門司吊橋（ブルーウィングもじ）

  • 地址：〒801-0852 福岡県北九州市門司区港町４−1

往海邊方向直直走，可以看到一座會打開的橋，在 10:00 ~ 16:00 整點期間，吊橋會打開讓船隻經過，20分鐘後才會再次恢復。不妨在這裡等待一陣子，坐在一旁等待吊橋升降，悠閒的體驗一下門司港的悠閒風情。


在過了吊橋到對面，還可以看到路邊有街頭藝人在說故事，蠻有意思的，但可惜都是講日文聽不懂。


---

🏦 北九州市舊門司稅關

  • 地址：〒801-0853 福岡県北九州市門司区東港町１−24
  • 開放時間：09:00 ~ 17:00
  • 門票：參觀免門票
  • 官方網站：http://www.mojiko.info/3kanko/spot_zeikan.html

當站在藍翼門司吊橋旁時，對面就可以看到北九州市舊門司稅關(下面那棟兩層樓的橘色建築)，建築原為門司稅關使用，此建築於1912年完工啟用，一直使用至1927年為止。


目前建築內一樓作為常設海關展覽空間和旅客休息空間，可以坐在沙發上看看一些紀錄影片，或是到二樓的展望台，看看門司港的海景。


---

📗 北九州市立國際友好圖書館


  • 地址：〒801-0853 福岡県北九州市門司区東港町１−12
  • 開放時間：09:00 ~ 17:00
  • 官方網站：https://www.gururich-kitaq.com/kanmon/en/detail/index.php?id=29&app=0

北九州市立國際友好圖書館建於1995年，為北九州市的友好都市大連市的歷史建築的仿建，後面那棟高聳的建築是門司港レトロハイマート，他是一棟住宅公寓，頂樓是展望台。


---

🌉  海峽廣場

  • 地址：〒801-0852 福岡県北九州市門司区港町５−1
  • 開放時間：10:00 ~ 20:00
  • 官方網站：http://www.kaikyo-plaza.com/

海峽廣場建於1999年，為針對觀光客所設計的複合商業設施，有很多小店還有一些餐廳，還有許多特色小店，可以來這裡走一走。

前面還有兩尊香蕉人的雕像，愛的正義使者與節電使者，據說原來在日治時期外銷至日本的台灣香蕉，是以門司港為集貨地，這也是大家來門司港必拍景點之一。


由於一路上一直看到這種冰淇淋，雖然價格不便宜，但還是買一隻來嚐嚐，類似白色戀人的餅乾搭配冰淇淋起來很好吃。

title.$t: Northern Kyushu Independent Travel | Mojiko City Attractions | Kokura to Mojiko Transport | Mojiko Retro District | Kaikyo Plaza

content.$t:
Moji Ward is a port district facing the Seto Inland Sea. Mojiko was once one of Japan's three great ports and an extremely important international trading hub. The Mojiko "ferry connection" was also a key link between Kyushu and Honshu, and back then the area was filled with Western trading houses, Western-style buildings, banks and more. On this day our plan was to set off from Kokura to explore Mojiko and Shimonoseki, and then head straight back to our accommodation in Fukuoka in the evening.

 Getting from Kokura to Mojiko

Further reading：Northern Kyushu Independent Travel | Kokura City Accommodation | ARK BLUE HOTEL (now renamed Hotel Relief Kokura ANNEX)

That morning we checked out of our Kokura hotel and headed for Mojiko with our luggage in tow, planning to travel straight back to Fukuoka from Mojiko after sightseeing. Getting there is actually very easy — it feels a bit like riding a local commuter train in Taiwan. This stretch of railway is the final section of the Kagoshima Main Line. Just check the times and platform on Google Maps, use your Northern Kyushu JR Pass, and go straight to the platform to board!

These days Google Maps clearly shows both the timetable and the platform



The train is just like a local commuter train — no seat reservations needed, and there were very few passengers, with empty seats everywhere. The train runs north along the coast, passing three stations along the way, and after just 15 minutes you arrive at Mojiko Station!


---

 Mojiko Station


On 1 April 1891, the Kyushu Railway's Moji Station opened — the predecessor of today's Mojiko Station. The current building was moved 200m east of the original Moji Station in 1914, and it was renamed Mojiko Station in 1942. Both the exterior and interior recreate the Taisho-era design, making it the oldest railway station in Kyushu. The whole station has a wooden style, full of nostalgic charm.



---

💼 Luggage Storage at Mojiko Station


If you're hauling a big suitcase like we were, Mojiko Station also has luggage storage available. It's on the left-hand side as you exit the ticket gates — follow along as on Google Maps Street View and walk to the back, where you'll find a small bank of lockers. There aren't many, but there aren't many people using them either. (We arrived on a Sunday morning.)


The notice clearly shows the prices, all calculated per day

  • Small: ¥ 400
  • Medium: ¥ 600
  • Large: ¥ 700
  • Extra large: ¥ 900
From experience, a 26–28 inch suitcase needs to go in a "Large" locker to fit

---

🏫  Mojiko Retro District (門司港レトロエリア)

Mojiko is famous for its retro district, which preserves many buildings from the Meiji and Taisho eras, concentrated around Mojiko Station. Centred on numerous Western-style buildings erected in the early 20th century, the hotels and commercial facilities in this area have followed suit with a nostalgic period theme, full of Taisho-romance atmosphere. Starting from Mojiko Station and walking all the way to Kaikyo Plaza, you'll see many buildings preserved from the Taisho era. As soon as you step out of the station, you'll see plenty of rickshaws.


⛴   Blue Wing Moji Bridge (ブルーウィングもじ)

  • Address: 〒801-0852 4-1 Minatomachi, Moji-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka

Walk straight toward the sea and you'll see a bridge that opens up. On the hour between 10:00 and 16:00, the bridge lifts to let boats pass, and only returns to normal 20 minutes later. It's worth waiting a while here — sit off to one side and watch the bridge rise and fall while soaking up Mojiko's laid-back atmosphere.


After crossing the bridge to the other side, you can also see street performers telling stories by the roadside — quite interesting, though sadly it was all in Japanese, which we couldn't understand.


---

🏦 Kitakyushu Former Moji Customs House

  • Address: 〒801-0853 1-24 Higashiminatomachi, Moji-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka
  • Opening hours: 09:00 ~ 17:00
  • Admission: free
  • Official website: http://www.mojiko.info/3kanko/spot_zeikan.html

Standing beside the Blue Wing Moji Bridge, you can see the Kitakyushu Former Moji Customs House across the water (the two-storey orange building below). The building originally served as the Moji Customs House; it was completed and opened in 1912 and remained in use until 1927.


Today the ground floor houses a permanent customs exhibition space and a rest area for visitors — you can sit on the sofas and watch documentary footage, or head up to the observation deck on the second floor for sea views over Mojiko.


---

📗 Kitakyushu Municipal International Friendship Library


  • Address: 〒801-0853 1-12 Higashiminatomachi, Moji-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka
  • Opening hours: 09:00 ~ 17:00
  • Official website: https://www.gururich-kitaq.com/kanmon/en/detail/index.php?id=29&app=0

The Kitakyushu Municipal International Friendship Library was built in 1995 as a replica of a historic building in Dalian, Kitakyushu's sister city. The tall building behind it is the Mojiko Retro Highmart, a residential apartment tower with an observation deck on the top floor.


---

🌉  Kaikyo Plaza

  • Address: 〒801-0852 5-1 Minatomachi, Moji-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka
  • Opening hours: 10:00 ~ 20:00
  • Official website: http://www.kaikyo-plaza.com/

Kaikyo Plaza was built in 1999 as a mixed-use commercial complex designed for tourists. There are lots of small shops, some restaurants and many quirky specialty stores — well worth a stroll.

Out front there are also two "banana man" statues, the Messenger of Love and Justice and the Power-Saving Messenger. Apparently Taiwanese bananas exported to Japan during the Japanese colonial period were collected at Mojiko, and these statues are one of Mojiko's must-photograph spots.


Since we kept seeing this kind of ice cream everywhere along the way, we bought one to try even though it wasn't cheap — the biscuit, similar to Shiroi Koibito, pairs deliciously with the ice cream.

content.$t:
小倉鉄なべ 総本店

  • 造訪日期：2019-12-07
  • 晚餐花費：¥ 2,312 (鐵鍋煎餃兩人份 + 兩杯酒)
  • 付款方式：可刷卡
  • 地址：〒802-0006 福岡県北九州市小倉北区魚町２丁目３−12
  • 營業時間: 每日 11:00–23:30
  • 官網：http://tetsunabe-g.com/shopinfomation/

 

🥟 鐵鍋餃子

「鐵鍋餃子」據說是發源於北九州，其名稱是「八幡鐵鍋餃子」，並且被稱為日本三大餃子之一，在祇園，中州川端，小倉都有各自有名的鐵鍋餃子專賣店 。其實去年在福岡祇園也有吃過鐵鍋餃子，印象中就是好吃但份量很少，在小倉想吃到最正宗道地的鐵鍋餃子的話 ，網路上大家都推目前在小倉市區的小倉鉄なべ 。

📍 地理位置

我們這次是去總本店，總本店在JR小倉站旁，走路大約6分鐘的地方。從 JR 小倉站的方向沿著魚町銀天街走，到這個轉角左轉，再一直直走就會看到囉！ 總本店位於前方的轉角


📜 菜單

在官網上有最新的英文菜單
  • http://tetsunabe-g.com/wp/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/english.pdf
如果連結失效 可以直接到官網看
  • http://tetsunabe-g.com/grandmenu/
必點的當然就是鐵鍋餃子 一人份是八顆 (¥528)
 

我們總共一人點一份煎餃&飲料 

兩人份鐵鍋煎餃 (¥1056)

梅酒蘇打 Plum Wine with Soda (¥500) 

           


                

 口感就和在去年在福岡祇園吃到的差不多 酥脆，內餡香甜，可惜是份量不多就是了

              

 生啤 Sapporo Draft Beer (¥528) 

   

當天我們大約六點左右抵達，還不用排隊，店內約坐了六分滿，所以也沒有等很久，餐蠻快就來了！
        

點完餐店員還會拿來很中國風(?)的盤子


桌上會有三罐調味料，依序是柚子胡椒，辣椒，醬油。網路上很推柚子胡椒，辣椒的話很辣但很香，要酌量使用。
             


煎的非常酥脆的鐵鍋煎餃！

總結一下，想體驗道地的鐵鍋煎餃，不妨來試試看這間小倉鉄なべ 。但是因為份量不是很多，可以考慮點多人份一點，或是再去吃別的。

店內環就蠻寬敞的，但由於日本人習慣在室內抽煙，我們就遇到隔壁桌就在邊吃邊抽煙，實在不是很舒服，如果不喜歡煙味的要斟酌一下。

title.$t: Northern Kyushu Trip | Kokura City Food | Kokura Tetsunabe – Iron Pot Gyoza

content.$t:
Kokura Tetsunabe (小倉鉄なべ) Main Store

  • Date visited: 2019-12-07
  • Dinner cost: ¥ 2,312 (iron pot gyoza for two + two drinks)
  • Payment: credit cards accepted
  • Address: 〒802-0006 2-3-12 Uomachi, Kokurakita-ku, Kitakyushu City, Fukuoka Prefecture
  • Opening hours: daily 11:00–23:30
  • Official site：http://tetsunabe-g.com/shopinfomation/

 

🥟 Iron Pot Gyoza

"Iron pot gyoza" is said to have originated in Kitakyushu, where it is known as "Yahata iron pot gyoza," and it is counted as one of Japan's three great gyoza. Gion, Nakasu-Kawabata and Kokura each have their own famous iron pot gyoza specialty shops. I actually tried iron pot gyoza in Fukuoka's Gion last year — my impression was that it was delicious but the portion was small. If you want the most authentic iron pot gyoza in Kokura, everyone online recommends Kokura Tetsunabe in the Kokura city center.

📍 Location

This time we went to the main store, which is next to JR Kokura Station, about a 6-minute walk away. From the direction of JR Kokura Station, walk along Uomachi Ginten-gai shopping street, turn left at this corner, and keep going straight and you'll see it! The main store is on the corner up ahead.


📜 Menu

The latest English menu is available on the official website
  • http://tetsunabe-g.com/wp/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/english.pdf
If the link is dead, you can check the official site directly
  • http://tetsunabe-g.com/grandmenu/
The must-order is of course the iron pot gyoza One serving is eight pieces (¥528)
 

We each ordered one serving of gyoza and a drink 

Iron pot gyoza for two (¥1056)

Plum Wine with Soda (¥500) 

           


                

 The taste was much like what we had in Fukuoka's Gion last year — crispy, with a sweet, savory filling. The only pity is that the portion isn't very big.

              

 Sapporo Draft Beer (¥528) 

   

We arrived around six that evening and didn't have to queue. The restaurant was about 60% full, so we didn't wait long and the food came pretty quickly!
        

After ordering, the staff brought over some very Chinese-style (?) plates


There are three condiment jars on the table: yuzu pepper (yuzu kosho), chili, and soy sauce. The yuzu kosho is highly recommended online; the chili is very spicy but very fragrant, so use it sparingly.
             


Super crispy pan-fried iron pot gyoza!

To sum up: if you want to experience authentic iron pot gyoza, Kokura Tetsunabe is worth a try. But since the portions aren't large, consider ordering servings for more people, or plan to eat somewhere else afterwards.

The restaurant is fairly spacious, but since smoking indoors is common in Japan, the table next to us was smoking while eating, which wasn't very pleasant. If you dislike cigarette smoke, keep that in mind.

content.$t:
這篇主要是記錄一下當初購買 JRPass，以及由布院之森買票&劃位的過程

主要分三個主題來介紹：

  • 該買哪種 JRPass
  • 由布院之森怎麼訂票
  • 福岡博多車站領票地點

🚉  JRPass (鐵路周遊卷)

通常到日本來玩，如果會跑好幾個點，都會建議要買張 JR Pass 不僅方便又省錢。這次行程除了福岡之外，還會去由布院，小倉，門司港，這時候就需要來買張 JR Pass 了！

種類

北九州的JR pass (鐵路周遊卷) 分為三種：全區，北九州，南九州

九州鐵路官網介紹：https://www.jrkyushu.co.jp/chinese/railpass/railpass.html

九州鐵路官網裡面寫的其實非常清楚，幾乎想要知道的訊息都有了，在購票的時候根據自己要去的點，來選擇票種與決定區域跟天數。

票種 範圍 特急列車可劃位車種
全區域 下關在內九州區域的普通列車/特快列車 由布院之森、由布、音速、海鷗、綠、豪斯登堡、坐Ａ列車去吧、阿蘇男孩!、SL人吉、翡翠 山翡翠、隼人之風、指宿之玉手箱、海幸山幸、九州新幹線(博多～鹿兒島中央)
北九州 熊本・三角及大分以北的普通列車/特快列車 由布院之森、由布、音速、海鷗、綠、豪斯登堡、坐Ａ列車去吧、阿蘇男孩!、九州新幹線(博多～熊本)
南九州 熊本及大分以南的普通列車/特快列車 坐Ａ列車去吧、阿蘇男孩!、SL人吉、翡翠 山翡翠、隼人之風、指宿之玉手箱、海幸山幸、九州新幹線(熊本～鹿兒島中央)

❗ 注意事項

  • 購買條件 (必須兩點都符合)
    • 持有日本國以外的國家政府所發行的護照
    • 不在日本居住，以「短期逗留」的在留資格從外國入境的旅客
  • 新幹線只可搭乘往博多以南
  • 3日，5日連續日期不能中斷
  • 可使用有效區域內特快列車的指定席、自由席
  • 使用周遊券時請務必攜帶護照

購買方式

可以選擇在台灣跟旅行社買，或是到了日本再買都可以，但通常先在台灣買好的價格會比較優惠，幾乎各大旅行社或是 kkdays, klook 都有販售。因為是購買後直接拿到電子交換憑證 eMCO，所以如果沒有特別偏好哪一間，只要找價格最低的其實就可以了

P.S. 價格會隨著日幣而浮動，可以觀察一下再買

提供幾個連結給大家參考：(若商品下架連結會失效)
  • https://www.kkday.com/zh-tw/product/3494
  • https://www.klook.com/zh-TW/activity/2371-jr-kyushu-jr-pass/ 
  • https://activity.liontravel.com/detail?productCode=157001&Foreign=1
  • https://www.colatour.com.tw/C10T_Ticket/C10T02_Feature.aspx?ItemNo=733
買完之後會領到電子交換票卷，到時候要這張到臨櫃去領票 (建議印出來)


另外，領到這張後，也才能預定其他的特急列車

預定特急列車

  • 可以事先在 JR Kyushu Rail Pass Online Booking 預訂特急列車
  • 網路上事先預約每張票需要 1000 日圓
  • 到日本當地劃位特急列車座位不需收費
  • 劃位次數
    • 3日券10次
    • 5日券16次

🚞  由布院之森訂票

在訂任何的特急列車票之前，一定要購買 JR Pass，並且取得序號，才能夠在網路上購買。由於由布院之森列車是全車指定席，也就是說沒有指定劃位根本上不了車 😅

由布院之森官方介紹：https://www.jrkyushu.co.jp/chinese/train/yufuin_no_mori.html

時刻表

這是官方時刻表的內容 (2019.3.16～2020.2.29) 

https://www.jrkyushu.co.jp/chinese/booking/pdf/01Yufuinnomori_190301.pdf


P.S. 檔案若失效，請到官網看最新的時刻表：官方網站

從博多前往由布院，一天有三班指定席的 由布院之森，也有可以搭乘自由座的特快列車 由布


線上訂票步驟

1) 申請九州鐵路的帳號


進入 JR Kyushu Rail Pass Online Booking 申請帳號

進入指定席預約 (非預約受理時間可以先進去申請帳號)


註冊一個新的帳號



這裡有特別提醒要用當初買 JR Pass 一樣的電子郵件，當然如果是在台灣跟旅行社買的，那這個就只要填一個可以收到 email 的就可以囉。

P.S. 我自己購買的狀況就是這樣



之後等待一下，就可以收到一封確認信




然後再進去填一些資料就可以完成註冊囉！

2) 預定特急列車車票


注意，預定一定要在受理時間才能訂票

受理時間：
  • 日本時間：05:30~23:00
  • 台灣時間：04:30~22:00

再用你申請好的帳號去做登入


雖然我是不知道為何一定要在受理時間才可以預定

不是系統自動做嗎....？？？？？


3) 選座位

最熱門搶手的，一定是第一節車廂最前面的景觀位置，如果沒搶到，也可以跟我們一樣搶最後一節車廂的最後一排，一樣會有景觀喔！(雖然是在背後反過來的)

第四節車廂是木質風也會比較美喔，詳細列車介紹，請參考另一篇

https://travel-sean.blogspot.com/2019/12/yufuin-no-mori.html

4) 完成預定

完成後就會收到確認信件，注意操作完會跳出明細，這時候記得另存成PDF下來，之後印出來帶去日本，因為後來我就找不到任何可以找到訂票明細的地方了...


📄  福岡博多車站領票地點

當一切都買好票定好票之後，抵達福岡後，可以到任一 JR 車站去領票，以最方便的博多站為例，要到 JR九州 みどりの窓口 去領票


基本上很好找，只要在博多車站一樓大廳很容易就可以找到



這個綠色的 JR 服務處就是了

左邊有一個專門為 JR Pass 開的櫃檯


只要將事先印出來的電子領票卷還有護照，給櫃檯人員就可以囉！

如果有在網路上預訂特急列車，也是一起給他就好了，櫃檯服務人員會問你要開始使用的時間，之後就可以拿到 JR Pass 了！

記得簽名 ＆ 搭車隨身攜帶，另外，如果想直接預定特急列車，也可以直接跟他說，在日本當地臨櫃透過 JR Pass 預定特急是免費的喔 (在數量限制內劃位次數：3日券10次，5日券16次)

title.$t: Northern Kyushu Independent Travel | JR Pass Buying & Seat Reservation Guide | How to Book the Yufuin no Mori | Where to Pick Up Tickets at Hakata Station

content.$t:
This post is mainly a record of how I bought the JR Pass, plus the process of buying tickets and reserving seats for the Yufuin no Mori.

It's divided into three main topics:

  • Which JR Pass should you buy
  • How to book the Yufuin no Mori
  • Where to pick up tickets at Hakata Station in Fukuoka

🚉  JR Pass (Rail Pass)

Generally when traveling in Japan, if you plan to visit several places, it's recommended to buy a JR Pass — it's both convenient and money-saving. On this trip, besides Fukuoka, we also went to Yufuin, Kokura and Mojiko, so a JR Pass was exactly what we needed!

Types

The Northern Kyushu JR Pass (rail pass) comes in three types: All Kyushu, Northern Kyushu, and Southern Kyushu

Official JR Kyushu site:https://www.jrkyushu.co.jp/chinese/railpass/railpass.html

The official JR Kyushu website explains everything very clearly — pretty much all the information you'd want is there. When buying, just pick the pass type, area and number of days based on where you plan to go.

Pass type Coverage Limited express trains available for seat reservation
All Kyushu Local/limited express trains in the Kyushu area including Shimonoseki Yufuin no Mori, Yufu, Sonic, Kamome, Midori, Huis Ten Bosch, A-Train, Aso Boy!, SL Hitoyoshi, Kawasemi Yamasemi, Hayato no Kaze, Ibusuki no Tamatebako, Umisachi Yamasachi, Kyushu Shinkansen (Hakata–Kagoshima-Chuo)
Northern Kyushu Local/limited express trains north of Kumamoto・Misumi and Oita Yufuin no Mori, Yufu, Sonic, Kamome, Midori, Huis Ten Bosch, A-Train, Aso Boy!, Kyushu Shinkansen (Hakata–Kumamoto)
Southern Kyushu Local/limited express trains south of Kumamoto and Oita A-Train, Aso Boy!, SL Hitoyoshi, Kawasemi Yamasemi, Hayato no Kaze, Ibusuki no Tamatebako, Umisachi Yamasachi, Kyushu Shinkansen (Kumamoto–Kagoshima-Chuo)

❗ Things to note

  • Eligibility (both conditions must be met)
    • Hold a passport issued by a government other than Japan
    • Not residing in Japan, and entering from abroad with "Temporary Visitor" status
  • The Shinkansen can only be taken south of Hakata
  • The 3-day and 5-day passes must be used on consecutive days
  • Both reserved and non-reserved seats on limited express trains within the valid area can be used
  • Always carry your passport when using the pass

How to buy

You can buy it from a travel agency in Taiwan, or after arriving in Japan, but buying in Taiwan in advance is usually cheaper. Almost all major travel agencies, as well as KKday and Klook, sell it. Since what you get right after purchase is an electronic exchange voucher (eMCO), if you have no particular preference, just go with whoever has the lowest price.

P.S. Prices fluctuate with the yen, so watch the rate before buying

Here are a few links for reference: (links will break if the product is delisted)
  • https://www.kkday.com/zh-tw/product/3494
  • https://www.klook.com/zh-TW/activity/2371-jr-kyushu-jr-pass/ 
  • https://activity.liontravel.com/detail?productCode=157001&Foreign=1
  • https://www.colatour.com.tw/C10T_Ticket/C10T02_Feature.aspx?ItemNo=733
After purchasing you'll receive an electronic exchange voucher, which you take to the counter later to collect your pass (I recommend printing it out)


Also, only after receiving this can you book other limited express trains

Booking limited express trains

  • You can book limited express trains in advance at JR Kyushu Rail Pass Online Booking
  • Booking online in advance costs 1,000 yen per ticket
  • Reserving limited express seats in person in Japan is free
  • Number of seat reservations
    • 3-day pass: 10 times
    • 5-day pass: 16 times

🚞  Booking the Yufuin no Mori

Before booking any limited express tickets, you must buy a JR Pass and get the serial number in order to buy online. Since the Yufuin no Mori is entirely reserved seating, without a seat reservation you simply can't board 😅

Official Yufuin no Mori page:https://www.jrkyushu.co.jp/chinese/train/yufuin_no_mori.html

Timetable

This is the official timetable (2019.3.16–2020.2.29) 

https://www.jrkyushu.co.jp/chinese/booking/pdf/01Yufuinnomori_190301.pdf


P.S. If the file is no longer available, check the latest timetable on the official site:Official website

From Hakata to Yufuin there are three reserved-seat Yufuin no Mori services a day, and there's also the limited express Yufu, which has non-reserved seats


Online booking steps

1) Register a JR Kyushu account


Go to JR Kyushu Rail Pass Online Booking to register an account

Enter Reserved Seat Booking (you can go in and register an account outside of booking hours)


Register a new account



There's a special reminder to use the same email address you used when buying the JR Pass. Of course, if you bought it from a travel agency in Taiwan, you just need to enter any email address you can receive mail at.

P.S. That was my own situation



After a short wait, you'll receive a confirmation email




Then go back in, fill in some details, and registration is complete!

2) Book limited express tickets


Note: you can only book during the accepted booking hours

Booking hours:
  • Japan time: 05:30–23:00
  • Taiwan time: 04:30–22:00

Then log in with the account you registered


Though I have no idea why bookings can only be made during those hours

Isn't it all done automatically by the system....????


3) Choose your seat

The most popular seats are definitely the panoramic ones at the very front of car 1. If you can't grab those, you can do what we did and grab the last row of the last car — you still get the view! (though it's facing backwards)

Car 4 has a wooden decor and is prettier too. For a detailed look at the train, see my other post

https://travel-sean.blogspot.com/2019/12/yufuin-no-mori.html

4) Complete the booking

Once done you'll receive a confirmation email. Note that a booking summary pops up after you finish — remember to save it as a PDF, then print it out and bring it to Japan, because afterwards I couldn't find anywhere to look up the booking details...


📄  Where to pick up tickets at Hakata Station, Fukuoka

Once everything is bought and booked, after arriving in Fukuoka you can pick up your tickets at any JR station. Taking the most convenient one, Hakata Station, as an example, head to the JR Kyushu Midori no Madoguchi (green ticket window) to collect your tickets


It's basically easy to find — just look around the first-floor concourse of Hakata Station



This green JR service center is the place

On the left there's a counter dedicated to the JR Pass


Just hand the printed electronic exchange voucher and your passport to the staff at the counter!

If you booked limited express trains online, hand those over at the same time. The staff will ask you what date you want to start using the pass, and then you'll get your JR Pass!

Remember to sign it and carry it with you when riding. Also, if you want to reserve limited express seats right there, just tell them — reserving limited express seats with the JR Pass at a counter in Japan is free (within the limit: 10 reservations for the 3-day pass, 16 for the 5-day pass)

We booked our return Yufuin no Mori right there on the spot

title.$t: 北九州自由行 | 小倉市區景點篇 | 小倉區一日遊 | 旦過市場 | 常盤橋 | 小倉城

content.$t:
小倉市，位於福岡縣東北部，正確來說現在已經沒有小倉市這個地區，1963年的時候門司市、小倉市、戶畑市、八幡市、若松市，五個市合併成為現在的北九州市，而小倉市就變成現在的「小倉區」，1974年的時候小倉區再分為小倉北區跟小倉南區，一直沿用至今。

小倉站位於小倉北區，而靠近小倉站附近的景點並不是太多，這裡比像是個悠哉的二線城市，如果要跟九州其他熱門景點比起來比較冷門一點。

主要可以去看看的點有這幾個

  • 旦過市場
  • 北九州河畔步行街
  • 小倉城
  • 魚町銀天街

小倉站

我們抵達的時候的這天是 2019-12-07，這時候不是旅遊旺季，是個楓葉快掉光，櫻花還沒出來的尷尬季節，不過好在路上還是有幾顆完整的銀杏樹，才可以在巷子的小公園發現難得的美景


🥦 旦過市場

  • 地址：〒802-0006 福岡県北九州市小倉北区魚町４丁目２−18
  • 營業時間：10:00 ~ 18:00 (週日休息)

從JR小倉站步行約十分鐘即可到達旦過市場，剛好我們住的旅館 - ARK BLUE HOTEL 藍色方舟飯店 (已改名 ホテルリリーフ小倉ANNEX) 也離這裡不遠，從旅館走過來也是差不多十分鐘步行距離。

從旅館過來會剛好從旦過市場中間的進去

旦過市場是位於日本福岡縣北九州市小倉北區魚町的一座市場，有「北九州的廚房」之稱，市場內有多達200家以上的店鋪，和福岡市的柳橋聯合市場並列為福岡縣內的兩大市場。

這個市場很有日本的傳統市場的氛圍，有著各種生鮮，肉類，炸物，青菜等等，充滿非常多在地人在這裡採買。


旦過市場，最開始是大正時代的漁業起貨場，慢慢隨著蔬菜攤商從外地集中，逐漸發展成爲現在的樣貌，這裡除了北九州的廚房之稱之外，也被稱為小倉人的廚房，可以找到許多平價美食，也可以體驗當地人的生活。

我們抵達的時間是中午過一點點，本來的目標也是在這裡吃午餐，不過市場內熟食比想像中的少，大部分還是生鮮居多。

大學堂

網路上最有名的大學堂，只買白飯跟咖啡，你可以到市場去買各種的配菜來這裡買一碗白飯吃，是個非常特別的文化，但如果沒有一定要吃碗白飯，就不一定要選擇這裡囉。


旦過市場最尾端的一間炸物店


經過的時候發現很多在地人在購買，店內販售各種烤串與炸物，有炸可樂餅、炸魚等等。我們買了幾串烤肉串還有可樂餅來試試看味道。


味道不差，但是不是現做所以涼掉，有點可惜

中間賣餃子的店

在這個小攤位買了蒸包子，這是使用鹿兒島的黑豬肉內餡配上洋蔥，吃起來味道清爽不錯，口感的話很像小籠包。


接著往另一頭走，又發現一家很多人在買的店，看起來比較像是賣各種魚板魚漿料理


買了一個號稱旦過市場名物，是個裡面是魚漿、外面去炸的食物，一顆份量很大，很扎實。外面炸的那層皮很薄很脆，口感很不錯，不過裡面的魚漿不會特別驚豔但也不難吃。


很在地的市場，沒有什麼觀光氣息

👜 魚町銀天街

  • 地址：〒802-0006 福岡県北九州市小倉北区魚町１丁目４−6
  • 營業時間：10:00 ~ 18:00

這裡跟中央商店街整條算是接在一起的，所以可以從小倉站一路逛過這裡，然後再一路走到旦過市場。中間橫向的也有很多商店，餐廳，是一個尋找晚餐地點的好地方。

不過跟其他城市的這種傳統商店街比較起來，小倉的商店街相較起來好像比較不好逛，但餐廳倒是不少，在這裡吃了不錯吃的鐵鍋餃子：

北九州自由行 | 小倉市區美食篇 | 小倉鉄なべ 鐵鍋煎餃

📍 常盤橋


  • 地址：〒802-0006 福岡県北九州市小倉北区魚町４丁目２−18

從魚町銀天街旁出來，意外發現有一座橫跨紫川的木造橋「常盤橋」，查了一下才知道他是日本百大名橋之一，往小倉城的路上有路過可以順道看看這座木橋，晚上經過應該會別有一番風味。


🏯  小倉城

  • 地址：〒803-0813 福岡県北九州市小倉北区城内２−1
  • 營業時間：09:00–17:00 (戶外地區無限制)

從北九州河畔步行街，可以接到小倉城的北面入口，這裡有一條路可以直接通過小倉城的護城河，直接進到小倉城的區域內。


小倉城的區域內有小倉城庭園

旁邊的鳥居，是八坂神社的一個入口，八坂神社又稱為祇園社，據說是戀愛祈願的聖地。


到了小倉城發現部份楓葉與銀杏還留著，搭配小倉城可以拍出蠻美的景色。


再往小倉城裡面走一點，就會到進入小倉城的入口，可以從高處望下整個庭園。

小倉市區其實真的不算是觀光熱區的城市，如果只在小倉市區短暫停留的話，大概半天可以走完所有景點，不過如果是自駕，那可以到小倉外圍一點，還有蠻多郊區的景點可以去走走。

title.$t: Kitakyushu Independent Travel | Kokura City Attractions | One-Day Kokura Ward Itinerary | Tanga Market | Tokiwabashi Bridge | Kokura Castle

content.$t:
Kokura City is located in the northeastern part of Fukuoka Prefecture. To be precise, the city of Kokura no longer exists today: in 1963, five cities — Moji, Kokura, Tobata, Yahata and Wakamatsu — merged to form present-day Kitakyushu City, and Kokura City became "Kokura Ward." In 1974, Kokura Ward was further divided into Kokurakita Ward and Kokuraminami Ward, which remains the case today.

Kokura Station is in Kokurakita Ward, and there aren't many attractions right around the station. The area feels more like a laid-back second-tier city, and compared with Kyushu's other popular spots it's relatively off the beaten path.

The main places worth visiting are these:

  • Tanga Market
  • Kitakyushu Riverwalk
  • Kokura Castle
  • Uomachi Gintengai Shopping Street

Kokura Station

The day we arrived was 2019-12-07, outside of peak travel season — that awkward time when the autumn leaves have almost all fallen and the cherry blossoms haven't come out yet. Luckily there were still a few intact ginkgo trees along the streets, so we were able to find some rare beautiful scenery in a small park down an alley.


🥦 Tanga Market

  • Address: 4-2-18 Uomachi, Kokurakita Ward, Kitakyushu City, Fukuoka Prefecture 802-0006
  • Opening hours: 10:00 – 18:00 (closed Sundays)

Tanga Market is about a ten-minute walk from JR Kokura Station. As it happens, the hotel we stayed at — ARK BLUE HOTEL (now renamed Hotel Relief Kokura ANNEX) — isn't far either; it's also roughly a ten-minute walk from there.

Coming from the hotel, you enter right in the middle of Tanga Market

Tanga Market is a market in Uomachi, Kokurakita Ward, Kitakyushu City, Fukuoka Prefecture, known as "the kitchen of Kitakyushu." It has more than 200 shops, and together with Fukuoka City's Yanagibashi Rengo Market it is one of the two largest markets in Fukuoka Prefecture.

The market has a wonderfully traditional Japanese atmosphere, with all kinds of fresh seafood, meat, fried foods, vegetables and more, and plenty of locals doing their shopping here.


Tanga Market began in the Taisho era as a fish unloading area, and gradually developed into its present form as vegetable vendors from outside the area gathered here. Besides being called the kitchen of Kitakyushu, it's also known as the kitchen of Kokura's residents — a place to find plenty of affordable food and experience local life.

We arrived a little after noon, intending to have lunch here, but there were fewer cooked-food stalls than expected; most vendors sell fresh produce and seafood.

Daigakudo

Daigakudo, the most famous spot online, sells only white rice and coffee. You buy various side dishes around the market and then come here for a bowl of rice — a very unique bit of local culture. But if you're not set on having a bowl of rice, you don't necessarily need to come here.


A fried-food shop at the far end of Tanga Market


As we passed by we noticed a lot of locals buying here. The shop sells all sorts of grilled skewers and fried items, including croquettes and fried fish. We bought a few meat skewers and a croquette to try.


Tasted decent, but it wasn't made fresh so it had gone cold — a bit of a shame

The dumpling shop in the middle of the market

We bought steamed buns from this little stall. They're filled with Kagoshima black pork and onion — light and tasty, with a texture much like xiaolongbao.


Walking on to the other end, we found another shop with lots of customers — it seemed to specialize in fish cake and surimi dishes.


We bought something billed as a Tanga Market specialty: surimi on the inside, deep-fried on the outside. Each piece is large and very filling. The fried outer layer is thin and crisp with a great texture; the surimi inside isn't especially amazing, but it's not bad either.


A very local market, with hardly any touristy feel

👜 Uomachi Gintengai Shopping Street

  • Address: 1-4-6 Uomachi, Kokurakita Ward, Kitakyushu City, Fukuoka Prefecture 802-0006
  • Opening hours: 10:00 – 18:00

This street is essentially connected to the Chuo Shopping Arcade, so you can stroll all the way here from Kokura Station and then continue on to Tanga Market. The cross streets in between are also full of shops and restaurants — a great place to look for somewhere to have dinner.

That said, compared with similar traditional shopping arcades in other cities, Kokura's arcade seems a bit less fun to browse — though there are plenty of restaurants. We had some really good iron-pan gyoza here:

Kitakyushu Independent Travel | Kokura Food | Kokura Tetsunabe Iron-Pan Gyoza

📍 Tokiwabashi Bridge


  • Address: 4-2-18 Uomachi, Kokurakita Ward, Kitakyushu City, Fukuoka Prefecture 802-0006

Coming out beside Uomachi Gintengai, we unexpectedly came across a wooden bridge spanning the Murasaki River — Tokiwabashi. A quick search revealed it's one of Japan's 100 famous bridges. It's on the way to Kokura Castle, so you can stop by for a look; passing by at night must have a charm all its own.


🏯  Kokura Castle

  • Address: 2-1 Jonai, Kokurakita Ward, Kitakyushu City, Fukuoka Prefecture 803-0813
  • Opening hours: 09:00–17:00 (no restrictions for the outdoor areas)

From the Kitakyushu Riverwalk you can reach the north entrance of Kokura Castle, where a path leads straight across the castle moat and directly into the castle grounds.


The castle grounds include the Kokura Castle Japanese Garden

The torii gate beside it is one of the entrances to Yasaka Shrine, also known as Gion Shrine, said to be a sacred spot for praying for love.


At Kokura Castle we found some maple and ginkgo leaves still hanging on, which made for some quite beautiful photos with the castle.


Walk a bit further into the castle grounds and you'll reach the entrance to the castle keep, from where you can look down over the whole garden.

Downtown Kokura really isn't a major tourist hotspot. If you're only making a short stop in the city center, half a day is about enough to see all the sights. But if you're driving, head a little outside Kokura — there are quite a few suburban attractions worth exploring.

title.$t: 北九州自由行 | 小倉市區住宿篇 | ARK BLUE HOTEL 藍色方舟飯店 (已改名 ホテルリリーフ小倉ANNEX)

content.$t:
• 入住日期：2019-12-07 (雙床房週六一晚)
  • 價格：¥ 8,866
  • 付款方式：可刷卡
  • 地址：〒 802-0081 福岡県北九州市小倉北区紺屋町 12-16
  • 其他備註：已改名 ホテルリリーフ小倉ANNEX

這間旅館是我們這次北九州旅遊的第一間住宿，會選擇第一天下飛機就直奔小倉來玩，也是因為週六福岡的住宿爆炸貴，同樣住宿週六竟然直接貴了快八倍...

P.S. 後來猜測可能是因為這周假日剛好有 Arashi 5x20 活動，福岡幾乎人手一個紀念袋

在訂房網站上找了一輪，靠近小倉站的不是沒房間，就是有一點太貴了。後來找到了這間 ARK BLUE HOTEL，價格便宜，感覺房間又很大，最後就選擇這間了！

📍地點位置


這間旅館位於小倉站東南方，走路大約 15 分鐘的位置，由於小倉的街道大致上都方方正正的，所以只要往那個方向走並不難找，如果走中間那區會經過小倉的風化區，夜晚的話也可以選擇走外面的大路。

路口有一家全家便利商店，看到之後轉進來就會到旅館了！旅館正前方也有一個蠻大的平面停車場，如果是開車前來停車應該也還算方便。

🏢 旅館環境

這間旅館是一間有獨立套房與 Hotstal 共用房型的旅館，一樓的空間很寬敞，目前是一間咖啡廳，如果有早餐的話會在這裡用餐。

早餐供應時段是 6:30 ~ 9:30

入口處咖啡廳的櫃檯

如果要住宿的旅客，一進門要通過這個入口處咖啡廳的櫃檯，要往左走到地下室轉搭電梯，或是往右到一樓上面的電梯入口，然後搭電梯到二樓，才可以到旅館的櫃檯喔！

一樓與地下一樓是 Hostal 的部分，包含可以泡澡的大浴池也在這裡，女生的浴池當你入住後會給你開門的密碼，男生大浴池就沒有上鎖的門。


搭乘電梯一到二樓之後

除了櫃檯還可以看到一個很舒服的公共空間提供入住旅客在這裡休息。

另外，如果要寄放行李的話，櫃檯會請你自己去拿上面照片左邊藍色的鎖，然後你就自己找地方鎖你的行李就可以了，非常自助式且隨性 😂

🛏 房間環境



這次入住的是雙人雙床間，位於旅館的三樓，打開發現空間比想像中的大很多很多，跟以往日本旅館都小小的印象完全不一樣！

床鋪軟硬適中，大小也不小

還有一個蠻大的長桌可以使用

從另一個角度可以看到，床跟長桌中間還有一段蠻大的空間


吹風機提供的是基本的摺疊吹風機，掛在電視旁的袋子裡面

也有提供基本的浴袍跟拖鞋

底下也有保險箱


熱水壺跟杯子都可以在長桌上找到，晚上想要吃泡麵也蠻方便的。由於日本的水是可以直接飲用的，所以房間並沒有提供水，如果需要的話旅館外面就是全家，或是過馬路也有 7-11 很方便買水。

另外房間內還有空氣清淨加濕器，對於乾燥的日本，加濕器真的很重要。


床頭的部分有提供兩個 USB 插座，還有一個簡易的小時鐘


🛁 浴室

房間的浴室就如同一般日本的旅館一樣很小，就是簡簡單單的配上一個小浴缸。


浴缸上有著 Shower break 的沐浴乳，洗髮精和身體乳液

盥洗用品也是最簡單旅遊用的

✔ 優缺點


優點

  • 房內空間非常大
  • 假日價格便宜
  • 離旦過市場很近，走路約5~10分鐘
  • 附近有全家跟7-11，很方便

缺點

  • 距離小倉站蠻遠，要走15分鐘左右
  • 房間內沒有對外窗，必須一直使用空調

如果假日在小倉想找便宜舒適的住宿，不介意稍微走遠一點，那這間 ARK Blue Hotel，自己住過覺得算是 CP 值不錯又舒適的旅館。

title.$t: Kitakyushu Independent Travel | Kokura City Center Accommodation | ARK BLUE HOTEL (now renamed Hotel Relief Kokura ANNEX)

content.$t:
• Stay date: 2019-12-07 (twin room, one Saturday night)
  • Price: ¥ 8,866
  • Payment: credit cards accepted
  • Address: 〒 802-0081 12-16 Konyamachi, Kokurakita-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka
  • Other notes: now renamed Hotel Relief Kokura ANNEX

This hotel was the first place we stayed on this Kitakyushu trip. We chose to head straight to Kokura right after landing on day one because accommodation in Fukuoka was insanely expensive on Saturday — the same room was nearly eight times more expensive on a Saturday...

P.S. We later guessed it was because the Arashi 5x20 event happened to be on that weekend — almost everyone in Fukuoka was carrying a commemorative bag.

After browsing the booking sites for a while, places near Kokura Station were either fully booked or a bit too pricey. Then we found ARK BLUE HOTEL — cheap, and the rooms looked really big, so we went with this one!

📍 Location


The hotel is southeast of Kokura Station, about a 15-minute walk away. Since Kokura's streets are laid out in a fairly neat grid, it isn't hard to find as long as you head in the right direction. If you cut through the middle you'll pass Kokura's red-light district, so at night you may prefer to take the main road around it.

There's a FamilyMart at the intersection — turn in after you see it and you'll reach the hotel! There's also a fairly large surface parking lot right in front, so driving here should be reasonably convenient.

🏢 Hotel Environment

This property offers both private en-suite rooms and shared hostel-style rooms. The ground floor is very spacious and currently houses a café, which is where breakfast is served if you book it.

Breakfast is served from 6:30 to 9:30

The café counter at the entrance

Hotel guests need to pass this café counter at the entrance when they walk in, then either go left down to the basement to catch the elevator, or right to the elevator entrance on the ground floor, and take it up to the second floor to reach the hotel reception!

The ground floor and basement level are the hostel section, including the large baths where you can soak. For the women's bath you'll be given a door code when you check in; the men's bath has no locked door.


Once the elevator reaches the second floor,

besides the reception you'll also find a very comfortable common area where guests can relax.

Also, if you want to store luggage, the front desk will ask you to grab one of the blue locks on the left in the photo above, then find a spot and lock up your own bags — very self-service and laid-back 😂

🛏 The Room



We stayed in a twin room on the third floor. When we opened the door we found it was far, far bigger than expected — completely different from the impression of tiny Japanese hotel rooms!

The beds are just the right firmness, and a decent size too

There's also a fairly large long desk to use

From another angle you can see there's still a good amount of space between the beds and the desk


The hair dryer is a basic folding one, kept in the bag hanging next to the TV

Basic robes and slippers are provided as well

There's a safe underneath as well


The kettle and cups are on the long desk, which is handy if you want instant noodles at night. Since tap water in Japan is drinkable, no bottled water is provided in the room; if you need some, there's a FamilyMart right outside the hotel, or a 7-Eleven just across the street.

The room also has an air purifier/humidifier — in dry Japan, a humidifier really matters.


At the bedside there are two USB sockets and a simple little clock


🛁 Bathroom

The bathroom is small, just like in most Japanese hotels — simple, with a small bathtub.


On the tub there's Shower Break body wash, shampoo and body lotion

The toiletries are the simplest travel-sized kind

✔ Pros and Cons


Pros

  • Very spacious rooms
  • Cheap weekend rates
  • Very close to Tanga Market, about a 5–10 minute walk
  • A FamilyMart and a 7-Eleven nearby — very convenient

Cons

  • Fairly far from Kokura Station — about a 15-minute walk
  • No exterior window in the room, so the air conditioning has to run constantly

If you're looking for cheap, comfortable weekend accommodation in Kokura and don't mind walking a bit further, then ARK Blue Hotel — from my own stay — is a comfortable place with good value for money.

title.$t: 北九州自由行 | 福岡往小倉交通篇 | 福岡機場接駁巴士 | JR 特急ソニック (音速號)

content.$t:
這次的北九州行，我們下飛機的第一站就是要直接去小倉，原因其實是因為假日福岡的住宿實在太貴，一個晚上都是台幣八千起跳的價格，而小倉的住宿費用相對於親民很多，所以才決定第一天一下飛機就直奔小倉。

✈  福岡機場到市區

從福岡機場進入福岡市區，大概是我去過城市中數一數二方便又快速的了，只要搭乘機場線地鐵就可以了。

但是由於國際線出境之後，不會直接到機場線地鐵站，機場線地鐵站是位在國內線的航廈那一端，所以必須要先搭乘接駁巴士到國內線航廈，才可以轉搭機場線的地鐵。不過這也不是太困難，因為一出來出境大廳馬上就可以看到很清楚的標示。


接駁巴士位於四號門外，可以很明顯看到巴士

接駁巴士是免費的，只要排隊上車就可以了

巴士抵達後，直接站牌前方就是地鐵入口了，且福岡空港站是地鐵的起站，任何車都可以搭，所以也不用去思考怕會搭錯方向。


🚄 福岡到小倉

從福岡要前往小倉站，最容易也比較快的方式就是透過鐵路：

山陽新幹線

  • 交通時間：15分鐘
  • 票價：將近四千日幣
  • 備註：不可使用JR九州的PASS，可以使用西日本的 JR Pass

JR特急

  • 交通時間：49分鐘
  • 票價：約一千八日圓
  • 備註：可以使用九州的 JR Pass

這樣大概看一下，如果你的行程會在九州附近走走而且會買九州JR Pass的話，那就直接搭乘JR特急比較省錢方便，但如果是要往廣島方向一路玩過去的話，可以考慮購買山口地區鐵路周遊卷來搭乘新幹線。

如何搭車

我們這次有購買北九州JR Pass，所以選擇透過 JR特急前往小倉，要搭車首先要到博多車站。

往小倉的這段JR的路線是 博多 – 別府 – 大分，車種是 JR 特急ソニック (音速號)


如果更詳細關於音速號的內容可以到官網查看：

音速號詳細介紹

我們下飛機抵達博多車站領完 JR Pass 之後，看一下時刻表，離我們時間最近的就是 特急ソニック21號 11:57分的車。

P.S. 由於使用 北九州 JRPass 所以特急都可以畫指定席的座位喔！

詳細介紹可以見另一篇：

北九州自由行 | JRPass 買票訂位篇 | 由布院之森訂票攻略 | 博多車站領票地點



如果沒有劃位，記得要找自由座的車廂入口排隊上車

車內環境還蠻寬敞的

莫約50分鐘的車程，就可以抵達小倉車站了喔！


回程

回程的話其實是一模一樣的，可以先去小倉車站的JR服務處免費劃位 (不劃位搭自由座也可以)，他就會多給你這張有位置的票卷，到時候車上驗票要和北九州 JR Pass 一起出示才可以。





基本上交通算是蠻簡單的，一點都不複雜，而且 JR 服務處針對外國人買的 JR Pass 都有專設櫃檯，英文溝通都沒有問題。

抵達小倉後，這次的行程就算正式開始了！

title.$t: Northern Kyushu Independent Travel | Getting from Fukuoka to Kokura | Fukuoka Airport Shuttle Bus | JR Limited Express Sonic

content.$t:
For this Northern Kyushu trip, our very first stop after getting off the plane was to head straight to Kokura. The reason was simply that accommodation in Fukuoka on weekends is far too expensive — starting at around NT$8,000 a night — while lodging in Kokura is much more affordable. So we decided to go directly to Kokura the moment we landed on day one.

✈  From Fukuoka Airport to the City

Getting from Fukuoka Airport into central Fukuoka is probably one of the most convenient and fastest airport transfers among all the cities I've visited — you just take the airport subway line.

However, after clearing international arrivals, you won't arrive directly at the airport subway station; the subway station is located over at the domestic terminal. So you first need to take a shuttle bus to the domestic terminal before transferring to the airport subway line. That said, it's not difficult at all, because clear signage is visible as soon as you step out into the arrivals hall.


The shuttle bus stop is just outside Gate 4 — the buses are easy to spot

The shuttle bus is free — just queue up and board

Once the bus arrives, the subway entrance is right in front of the bus stop. And since Fukuoka Airport Station is the line's terminus, any train works, so there's no need to worry about boarding in the wrong direction.


🚄 From Fukuoka to Kokura

The easiest and fastest way to get from Fukuoka to Kokura Station is by rail:

Sanyo Shinkansen

  • Travel time: 15 minutes
  • Fare: nearly 4,000 yen
  • Note: Not valid with the JR Kyushu Pass; the JR West Pass can be used

JR Limited Express

  • Travel time: 49 minutes
  • Fare: about 1,800 yen
  • Note: The JR Kyushu Pass can be used

Looking at this overall: if your itinerary stays around Kyushu and you're buying the JR Kyushu Pass, then taking the JR limited express is cheaper and more convenient. But if you're travelling onward toward Hiroshima, you might consider buying the Yamaguchi-area rail pass and taking the Shinkansen.

How to Board

We bought the Northern Kyushu JR Pass this time, so we chose the JR limited express to Kokura. To catch it, you first head to Hakata Station.

The JR route to Kokura runs Hakata – Beppu – Oita, and the train type is the JR Limited Express Sonic (ソニック).


For more details about the Sonic, check the official website:

Sonic detailed introduction

After landing and picking up our JR Pass at Hakata Station, we checked the timetable — the closest departure was the Limited Express Sonic No. 21 at 11:57.

P.S. With the Northern Kyushu JR Pass, you can reserve seats on all limited express trains!

For full details, see this other post:

Northern Kyushu Independent Travel | JR Pass Buying & Reservations | Yufuin no Mori Booking Guide | Where to Collect Tickets at Hakata Station



If you haven't reserved a seat, remember to queue at the entrance for the non-reserved cars

The interior is quite spacious

After roughly a 50-minute ride, you arrive at Kokura Station!


The Return Trip

The return journey is exactly the same. You can go to the JR service counter at Kokura Station to reserve a seat for free (or just ride in a non-reserved car). They'll give you an extra ticket showing your seat, and when the conductor checks tickets on board you must show it together with the Northern Kyushu JR Pass.





Overall the journey is quite simple and not complicated at all, and the JR service counters have dedicated windows for foreigners with JR Passes, so communicating in English is no problem.

Once we arrived in Kokura, the trip officially began!

2019 北九州自由行

九州是日本西南部的一個島，為日本本土四大島之一，也是距離台灣最近的日本地區，台灣現在也有不少航班可以直飛九州的各大城市。然而這次的目標是想要去九州北部，俗稱北九州。而說到北九州，廣義來說是福岡、佐賀、大分等九州北部的三個縣市。這趟旅程以福岡為中繼點，分別到北九州市與由布院旅行，到由布院泡溫泉與體驗慢活生活，到北九州看看不一樣的日本大正時代風情。

行程

旅遊時間：2019-12-07 ~ 2019-12-12

行程簡述

Day 1 小倉半日遊 


今日行程：

抵達福岡後，直接前往小倉半日遊，夜晚入住小倉


小倉區是一個位於九州北部的區，比較像是個悠哉的二線城市，跟九州其他熱門景點比起來比較冷門一點，適合放個半天在這裡漫步。著名的景點有旦過市場與小倉城。小倉部分住宿比其他城市要來得便宜一些，如果要去北九州市遊玩，可以考慮把小倉當作一個住宿點喔！


Day 2 門司港與下關一日遊



 今日行程：一早從小倉出發前往門司港與下關一日，晚間回到福岡住宿

門司區是個面向瀨戶內海的港口地區，門司港曾經是日本三大港之一，是相當重要的國際貿易據點。而面對門司港的下關，是位於日本山口縣的城市，自古以來一直作為“日本的門戶”而繁榮發展，是本州最西端的都市，也是一座充滿文化、歷史和大自然美景的城市。



下關除了有著新鮮魚貨的唐戶市場，外型像龍宮城的赤間神宮，是下關必去的景點之一。最特別的是赤間神宮的水天門，外型就像日本童話中的龍宮城，其實背後是有歷史故事的。


Day 3 由布院


今日行程：出發由布院，進行由布院深度之旅，夜宿由布院溫泉旅館

說到九州的溫泉勝地，除了別府，熊本之外，由布院(湯布院)絕對榜上有名，甚至可能還是第一個想到的溫泉度假勝地，也是遊客來九州自由行最喜歡的景點之一。由布院有著許多特色的小店，白天的時候是個觀光勝地，充滿了各地的遊客。一到晚上遊客走了之後，由布院就會寧靜下來，可以在這裡體會寧靜溫泉鄉的慢活步調。

晚上我們住了一間有著貓咪的溫泉旅館，除了體驗著名的由布院溫泉之外，更可以跟親人的貓咪玩，除此之外，員工與房間舒適度也很優秀，是一間個人覺得蠻值得的一間住宿。


Day 4 福岡市區巡禮


今日行程：下午左右回到福岡市區，進行短暫的福岡市區巡禮，夜宿福岡

今天回到福岡的時間已經下午快傍晚了，所以只簡單去幾個點，吃個飯就結束今天的行程。位於川端通商店街尾端的櫛田神社歷史十分悠久，自古就作為博多的氏神和總鎮守而聚集當地人的信仰，來到福岡市區必定要去參拜一下櫛田神社。


櫛田神社旁邊是大型購物城 - 博多運河城，這是在福岡市中心的購物和娛樂中心，也是每個人來到福岡市區必逛的大型商場。商場中間有一條運河，也是運河城的名稱由來。去完櫛田神社可以來這裡 shopping 或是吃美食喔！


Day 5 福岡一日遊


今日行程：完整的福岡一日遊，夜宿福岡

今天終於有完整的一天，可以好好逛逛福岡市區。福岡是九州最大都市與政治、經濟、交通中心，由於離台灣非常近，也成為台灣人旅遊常常來的地點之一。
如果要看歷史景點，可以到大濠公園那一區去看看福岡城遺址 。如果想體驗福岡的購物，那天神地下街就是絕對不能錯過的地點了！

Day 6 離開福岡，回程

2019 Northern Kyushu Independent Travel

Kyushu is an island in southwestern Japan and one of Japan's four main islands. It is also the part of Japan closest to Taiwan, and there are now plenty of flights from Taiwan directly to Kyushu's major cities. This time, however, our goal was northern Kyushu, commonly known as Kitakyushu. Broadly speaking, northern Kyushu refers to the three prefectures of Fukuoka, Saga and Oita. On this trip we used Fukuoka as our base, travelling out to Kitakyushu City and Yufuin — soaking in hot springs and enjoying the slow pace of life in Yufuin, and seeing a different, Taisho-era side of Japan in Kitakyushu.

Itinerary

Travel dates: 2019-12-07 ~ 2019-12-12

Itinerary at a Glance

Day 1 Half-day in Kokura 


Today's plan:

After arriving in Fukuoka, head straight to Kokura for a half-day visit; overnight in Kokura


Kokura is a ward in northern Kyushu that feels like a laid-back second-tier city. Compared with Kyushu's other popular destinations it sees fewer tourists, making it perfect for a leisurely half-day stroll. Its best-known sights are Tanga Market and Kokura Castle. Accommodation in Kokura tends to be cheaper than in other cities, so if you're travelling around Kitakyushu City, consider making Kokura your base!


Day 2 Day trip to Mojiko and Shimonoseki



 Today's plan: Set out early from Kokura for a full day in Mojiko and Shimonoseki, then return to Fukuoka for the night

Moji Ward is a port area facing the Seto Inland Sea. Mojiko was once one of Japan's three great ports and an important hub for international trade. Facing Mojiko across the strait is Shimonoseki, a city in Yamaguchi Prefecture that has prospered since ancient times as the "gateway to Japan." It is the westernmost city on Honshu and a place rich in culture, history and natural beauty.



Besides Karato Market with its fresh seafood, Shimonoseki is home to Akama Shrine, which looks like the mythical Dragon Palace and is one of the city's must-see sights. Most striking of all is Akama Shrine's Suitenmon gate, shaped just like the Dragon Palace of Japanese folklore — and there's a real historical story behind it.


Day 3 Yufuin


Today's plan: Head to Yufuin for an in-depth exploration; overnight at a Yufuin hot spring inn

When it comes to Kyushu's hot spring destinations, alongside Beppu and Kumamoto, Yufuin definitely makes the list — it may even be the first hot spring resort that comes to mind, and it's one of the favourite stops for independent travellers in Kyushu. Yufuin is full of charming little shops, and by day it's a bustling tourist town packed with visitors from everywhere. Once evening falls and the day-trippers leave, Yufuin grows quiet, and you can savour the slow rhythm of a peaceful hot spring village.

That night we stayed at a hot spring inn with resident cats. Besides enjoying the famous Yufuin hot springs, you can also play with the friendly cats. On top of that, the staff and the comfort of the rooms were excellent — personally I found it a really worthwhile place to stay.


Day 4 Exploring downtown Fukuoka


Today's plan: Return to downtown Fukuoka around the afternoon for a short city tour; overnight in Fukuoka

By the time we got back to Fukuoka it was already late afternoon, so we simply visited a few spots, had a meal and called it a day. Kushida Shrine, at the end of the Kawabata Shopping Arcade, has a very long history; since ancient times it has served as Hakata's guardian deity and the focus of local faith. A visit to Kushida Shrine is a must when you're in central Fukuoka.


Right next to Kushida Shrine is the huge shopping complex Canal City Hakata, a shopping and entertainment hub in the heart of Fukuoka and a mall everyone visiting the city should check out. A canal runs through the middle of the complex, which is where its name comes from. After Kushida Shrine, come here to shop or grab something delicious!


Day 5 A full day in Fukuoka


Today's plan: A full day exploring Fukuoka; overnight in Fukuoka

Today we finally had a whole day to properly explore downtown Fukuoka. Fukuoka is Kyushu's largest city and its political, economic and transport centre, and because it's so close to Taiwan it has become one of Taiwanese travellers' most frequent destinations.
If you're after historic sights, head to the Ohori Park area to see the ruins of Fukuoka Castle. And if you want to experience Fukuoka shopping, the Tenjin Underground Mall is absolutely not to be missed!

Day 6 Leaving Fukuoka, heading home
